text:
The circularity of the AI capex problem

If you are worried about supply of fresh equity, why are those companies who benefit from the spend of this new capital being sold?

Why is everyone worried about dilution? Don't these projects have good margins with utility like demand than meta's business as a whole? There is a gap of a few years but tech investors have rarely been worried about things like that before.

The only proper sense bearish take to explain a day like today is that there will be insufficient demand for compute in the future and that all this spending is on a white elephant. I haven't really heard many make this case.

But I think it's the only thing that underlies these sort of moves. People doubt AI fundamentally and when they get asked to make a sacrifice for it (handing out capital), they flinch. It's not going to work, there's not enough demand. This makes selling across the AI supply chain rational.

Companies like coreweave are the ultimate expression of this. Individually unimportant in the whole scheme of things being opportunistic extremely highly leveraged (not just financially either, but to input pricing and execution risk) players that will just have their supply absorbed by someone else if they fail. There pricing offers a barometer in the belief in this future demand.

So, it's all just sentiment. And this makes sense. It's an enormous bet on something that is doubted by and is frightening to many and is many years into the future. Much harder than selling ads now.

AI has to generate enough economic productivity to pay for itself and the margins that justify these capital raises in the first place. I think it will. I don't think most agree and they are just getting pulled along as beta.

Even if it is successful in generating enough productivity to pay for itself (plus some juicy inference margin) you have many that are frightened of it in addition to doubting it. The corporate factory line worker is at risk just like they were to machines in the industrial revolution. This will prompt a response from government. How do you price that? By discounting the ROI on these investments?

This would get you to the point of being worried about dilution. The trade is just too uncertain and needs so much capital that the only realistic way it fails in the medium term is that we become forever compute constrained and AI has a small percentage of the effect it could've had, taking down the labs with it.

When you carry wounds, you carry blind spots.

Inverted, malignant, extractive people show up.

They offer what you think is the shiny - the overcompensation for the wound that you carefully elaborated.

You tell them what that is. And they listen. But they also poke, like a doctor, for your pain point. And you volunteer that, too, thinking this is about healing.

Then they hit on that pain, blind spot, where you can't see clearly, while they promise the shiny. Hey, you can't have the shiny yet don't you see, you have this blind here, see that pain? it's ugly, yeah keep it blind, I don't want you to see me manoeuvering around it, clawing my fangs, it's all your fault, I don't wanna be, seen.

So. that connection is real. Yet, wrong. So you task yourself to correct the wrongness. Yeah ffs let's fix this relationship how hard can it be?

A weakened body trying to make a fair relationship with its parasite. Hey parasite, everything you say is mostly true, you do have a point, bit can you at least be, fair? I have needs, too!

Eventually the parasite has nowhere to hide and leaves, finds a new body.

You remain analizing the situation, trying to find the wisdom - how can a connection be right, yet wrong. How can it be that everything you thought you wanted, was self destruction. Why does that feel true as well. Because you did not want this - but did you.

Blind - spot.

As usual. The way out is obvious and invisible.

The parasite loved the mask of you that you built to compensate for the wound. The mask.

You can do that yourself.

Give yourself permission. Love that bullshit completely. Not because it's the truth nor the final state, but because it's the best you can do for now.

The sole point is to feel the love flowing through you.

Now let go of that mask. It was not needed. Love deeper. Truer.

Let the shape be the true one. The uncorrupted one. Feel how that shape is incompatible with the parasite fangs, still in your body. Let the contrast expell them.

Your actual shape was never broken.

You moved away from it. Because you have that, freedom.

Be free to return.

The parasite attack had to be confusing and had to be painful and had to hit deep. Had to bring you closer to death.

So you can wake up.

Not because it was good.

But because it was ugly.

You needed - the contrast.

To finally see.

text:
The New Humanity

A Dialogue from the Global Council

ELITIST: You still believe we want people to love one another?

CITIZEN: Isn’t that what you tell us? Unity. Diversity. A world without borders.

ELITIST: Unity is a useful slogan. What we actually want is uniformity. People who eat the same food, watch the same programs, speak the same approved language, and have forgotten why their grandparents ever fought to preserve anything.

CITIZEN: You want us to abandon our cultures?

ELITIST: Abandon? No. We want you to turn them into merchandise. Sell the costumes. Celebrate the festivals. Put the old traditions on television between advertisements. Keep the decorations; discard the convictions.

CITIZEN: And mixing every culture together will somehow make us easier to govern?

ELITIST: A population without a common memory is a population without a common purpose. Give people a thousand identities, a million distractions, and a thousand reasons to distrust their neighbors. Then offer them one authority capable of managing the chaos.

CITIZEN: So you manufacture the problem and sell yourselves as the solution.

ELITIST: Now you’re learning.

CITIZEN: And what happens to the people who refuse?

ELITIST: They become inconvenient. We call them backward, intolerant, or dangerous. We don’t need to silence every dissenter. We merely need to make dissent socially expensive.

CITIZEN: And the ruling class? Will your children live under the same system?

ELITIST: Of course not. Our children will attend the finest schools, live behind secure gates, and inherit the institutions that manage everyone else’s lives.

CITIZEN: Then this isn’t equality. It’s an aristocracy wearing the mask of progress.

ELITIST: Every age has its aristocracy. The clever ones simply learn to call theirs something more appealing.

CITIZEN: And what do you call yours?

ELITIST: Global governance. Sustainable development. Human cooperation. Choose whichever phrase makes you sleep best.

CITIZEN: One world, ruled by a few.

ELITIST: Precisely. And the beautiful part is that the public will argue endlessly about the slogans while we consolidate the power.

CITIZEN: You think people are too stupid to see what you’re doing.

ELITIST: No. I think people are too busy, too divided, and too exhausted to do anything about it.

CITIZEN: And if they finally wake up?

ELITIST: Then we will tell them that the world is too complicated to run without us.

The Citizen looks through the glass wall at the city below: a thousand flags in the museums, a thousand languages fading from the streets, and one enormous emblem glowing above the government tower.

CITIZEN: You haven’t united humanity.

ELITIST: What have we done, then?

CITIZEN: You’ve made the whole world a kingdom—and convinced the people they elected the king.

For the first time, the Elitist says nothing.

text:
It is metaphorical: WHAT IT MEANS TO BE A LEADER IS not a literal claim about divine selection that can be verified. The intent is to give meaning and purpose to experiences of difference or isolation. It means your heightened awareness is being framed as a purposeful role, not a problem. Breaking it down line by line: “You were chosen to see what others sleep through.”
You notice, understand, or perceive things that most people remain unaware of (the “sleep”). The word “chosen” casts this as intentional rather than random—implying a special capacity for insight.
“That is not loneliness. That is assignment.”
The resulting feeling of being different, set apart, or isolated is not meant to be experienced as mere loneliness or rejection. Instead, it is presented as a mission or task you have been given.
“Stay awake. Stay clear.”
Do not lose or dull the awareness you have. Remain conscious and mentally/spiritually unclouded so you can fulfill the role.
“The ones still dreaming will need your light when they open their eyes.”
People who are currently unaware (“dreaming”) will eventually gain awareness (“open their eyes”). At that point, they will need guidance, clarity, or direction from those who were already awake. Your “light” is the insight or perspective you can offer them.
Overall meaning: The message is a motivational reframe common in spiritual, Christian “chosen one,” and personal-growth content. It tells the reader that feeling like an outsider because of greater perception is not a flaw or punishment—it is preparation for a guiding role. It encourages maintaining that clarity so it can later serve others who wake up to the same realities.

Kent, the bible doesn't say that Cain "brought the fruit of the ground" .  The KJV says "brought of the fruit of the ground". Cain’s Offering: Fruit on the Ground

Genesis 4:3 describes Cain’s offering with an unusual phrase: **מִפְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה** (*mipperî hāʾădāmāh*)—“from the fruit of the ground.” My argument is that this wording may describe fruit associated with the ground itself—fruit already lying on Cain’s ground. Cain's ground fits the Hebrew well.
1. The wording is distinctive
The Bible refers to fruit many times. Before that verse, depending on the translation Fruit is mentioned up to 9 time but Genesis 4:3 uses a notably different construction: “fruit of the ground.” That difference deserves interpretive weight. If the author meant ordinary cultivated produce, why describe Cain’s gift this way rather than with the more familiar language used everywhere for fruit in the bible and elsewhere?
The Hebrew phrase unusual wording, used no where else, invites us to ask, is that the reason Cain's offering had no respect?

2. The earlier uses of “fruit” provide a frame of reference
The earlier biblical references to fruit establish a pattern for what “fruit” means and how it is described. Genesis 4:3 should be read in light of that foundation, not as though *perî* automatically means any agricultural produce. The contrast between those earlier descriptions and Cain’s wording may signal that something about his offering was unusual.

3. The offerings are contrasted, and Cain’s is rejected
Abel brings the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. Cain’s gift is described differently, and the Lord has no respect for it. The passage does not explicitly explain the reason for the rejection, but the contrast makes the nature and quality of Cain’s offering relevant. If his gift consisted of fruit already "sacrificed to" the ground.

4. Fallen fruit is sacrificed by the tree.
If the fruit had fallen from the tree, it could be understood as something the tree had already given up. Cain would then be presenting something already sacrifice by its source, rather than offering a fresh gift of his own. On this reading, it would not function as a genuine sacrifice: something already given up cannot be sacrificed a second time would have no respect from the Lord.

5. The Lord came down and warned Cain. 
The Lord didn't even mention the fruit. The Lord's only concern was how angry Cain was at Abel, that tells us he murdered his brother for an underlying reason, not the Lord's lack of respect.

6. Nowhere in the Bible does fruit come from anywhere except a tree, a womb, a vine, a limb, or a market. 

Conclusion   
Taken together—the one and only use of that Hebrew wording, the earlier biblical pattern for “fruit,” the contrast between Cain’s and Abel’s offerings, Hermeneutics, and Cain’s rejection—these details support that Cain brought fruit already lying on his ground, rather than a fresh, deliberately offered harvest aka a sacrifice. 
This is the only coherent explanation for why Cain’s offering was described differently and was not accepted and the Lord did not mention the fruit to Cain.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Gold Movie

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. The film is loosely based on the true story of the 1997 Bre-X mining scandal, when a massive gold deposit was supposedly discovered in the jungles of Indonesia; however, for legal reasons and to enhance the appeal of the film, character names and story details were changed.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Gold Movie

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. The film is loosely based on the true story of the 1997 Bre-X mining scandal, when a massive gold deposit was supposedly discovered in the jungles of Indonesia; however, for legal reasons and to enhance the appeal of the film, character names and story details were changed.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

SANITY is on the ballot, and we’re absolutely LOVING how this looks.

Jon Ossoff is Jewish. James Talarico is a Christian who's studied to become a minister. Abdul El-Sayed is Muslim. 

They practice three different faiths and share one belief: the Constitution still means something, and the government should work for regular people instead of billionaires and Donald Trump's ego.

That's the whole pitch: sanity. Republicans haven't offered any in years.

Ossoff is defending his seat in Georgia. In Texas, Talarico is running against Ken Paxton, and the latest polling has Talarico slightly ahead. In TEXAS. 
A few years ago, anyone predicting a Democrat would lead a Senate race there would have been laughed out of the room. 
In Michigan, El-Sayed holds a narrow lead over Mike Rogers.

So yes, things are looking better. But don't let that turn into comfort. Polls don't win elections. Votes do. 

A "slight edge" or a "narrow lead" can disappear inside the margin of error, and Republicans know exactly how to get their people to the polls.

Taking back the Senate ends the rubber stamp. It brings back real oversight and real hearings, and it puts a check on a president who treats the law like a suggestion.

Check your registration. Make a plan. Bring a friend. Then let's make the image in this post come true.
~Notice News

text:
Five seconds. That is how long Abdul El-Sayed lasted in the final debate before introducing himself as a doctor. He holds no medical license. He cannot treat a single patient, write a prescription, or legally give medical advice, yet the claim leads his pitch to Michigan voters, delivered with total confidence on the biggest stage of the race.
The distinction matters, and he knows it, which is why he never makes it. A degree earned years ago is not a license, and a man who ran a city health department from an office is not the practicing physician voters picture when they hear the title. Letting voters picture someone else is not a rounding error. It is the campaign.
Mike Rogers offers Michigan a record voters can check. El-Sayed offers a biography that dissolves the moment anyone checks it, and a debate performance that started with the claim his own licensing record refutes. If a candidate will stretch the truth about himself in the first five seconds, voters should ask what he will stretch in the United States Senate.

text:
THURSDAY EVENING DISPATCH ROUNDUP

October 22, 2026 | Colorado Front Range

Emergency crews, law enforcement officers, animal control personnel and transportation officials responded to numerous incidents across the Colorado Front Range Thursday afternoon and evening. Reports included a two vehicle rollover with injuries, a three vehicle crash with heavy damage, a felony traffic stop, medical emergencies, a reported overdose, weapons complaints, vehicle fires, dangerous driving and multiple roadway hazards.

The following incidents were reported through preliminary emergency dispatch communications. Times are Mountain Daylight Time.

LAKEWOOD, JEFFERSON COUNTY AND SURROUNDING AREAS

5:33 PM | Unconscious Person Reported

Emergency medical crews were dispatched for a reportedly unconscious person near South High Street. The precise jurisdiction and location remain unclear from the available dispatch summary.

5:29 PM | Disabled Vehicle on I-25

Roadside assistance personnel responded to northbound Interstate 25 near Alameda Avenue, where a woman was experiencing vehicle trouble. A unit reportedly performed a fluid transfer and remained with the driver while arrangements were made for her to continue safely.

5:27 PM | Medical Emergency at Colorado Mills

Emergency crews were dispatched to Colorado Mills Cinema, 14500 West Colfax Avenue in Lakewood, for a person reportedly experiencing a medical emergency. Medic 5 was assigned.

5:24 PM | Two Vehicle Rollover With Injuries

Emergency responders were dispatched to a reported two vehicle rollover near West Belleview Avenue and Long Street, east of the Walden area. One vehicle reportedly overturned, all occupants were outside the vehicles, and injuries were reported. Medical command was established.

5:19 PM | Reckless Driver on Highway 285

A white Chevrolet pickup was reported driving erratically near Highway 285 and Conifer Road, including passing into oncoming traffic and traveling at inconsistent speeds. The reporting party indicated the vehicle entered a nearby tavern parking area before being lost from sight.

5:15 PM | Children’s Playhouse Blocking Kipling Street

A children’s playhouse was reported partially obstructing the right southbound lane of Kipling Street near West 39th Avenue in Wheat Ridge.

4:50 PM | Possible Unconscious Person

Engine 1 and Medic 11 were dispatched to West 17th Avenue in Lakewood for a person reportedly unconscious or close to fainting.

4:47 PM | Possible Overdose in Lakewood

Engine 2 and Medic 17 were dispatched for a reported overdose or poisoning near West 20th Avenue and Lewis Street. The person’s condition was not available.

4:32 PM | Elderly Woman Trapped Beside Bed

Fire and medical crews responded to an apartment near Kipling Street in Arvada after an 82 year old woman reportedly became trapped with her arms between a bed and a wall. She was conscious and breathing when emergency assistance was requested.

4:29 PM | Traffic Lane Blocked Near Wadsworth

Transportation officials reported a right lane obstruction in the West 6th Avenue and Wadsworth Boulevard area. One automated dispatch summary also referenced West 10th Avenue, so the precise location requires confirmation.

4:28 PM | Vehicle Fire in Lakewood

Fire crews were dispatched to a reported vehicle fire near South Union Boulevard and West Alameda Parkway.

4:25 PM | Disabled Vehicle on Interstate 25

A possible disabled vehicle was reported on the left shoulder of northbound I-25 near the 58 marker. Responding units reportedly checked the area without locating the vehicle.

4:16 PM | Threat Complaint Near Mississippi and Garrison

A caller reported that an operator allegedly threatened to strike him if he did not provide identification. The complaint was associated with South Garrison Street and West Mississippi Avenue in Lakewood. The allegation has not been independently verified.

4:16 PM | Suspicious Activity at Red Rocks

Venue personnel reported a minivan carrying several people leaving a backstage parking area after occupants allegedly expressed a desire to bless the stage without authorization. Staff requested a camera review and documented the vehicle’s temporary registration.

4:13 PM | Crash Blocking Westbound Sixth Avenue

A reported collision blocked the right lane of westbound Sixth Avenue just east of Wadsworth Boulevard. Jeffcom requested traffic control assistance.

4:07 PM | Vehicle Stop Near Golden Office

Officers reported a vehicle registration inquiry involving a red Ford Explorer near a Golden office location. The exact location and circumstances were not independently confirmed.

3:59 PM | Transit Passenger Needs Assistance

A bus operator was asked to check on a passenger near West Colfax Avenue and Quail Street in Lakewood after reports that previous buses had passed the waiting customer.

3:39 PM | Crash at Peyton Parkway and Dartmouth

Emergency crews responded to a reported motor vehicle collision near South Peyton Parkway and West Dartmouth Avenue in Lakewood.

3:37 PM | Three Vehicle Crash on Interstate 25

Dispatch traffic described a three vehicle collision on northbound I-25 near the Aurora exit, with fire personnel responding. The extent of injuries was not established.

3:33 PM | Pickup Blocking Interstate 70 Ramp

A pickup truck reportedly obstructed part of the eastbound I-70 entrance ramp from Colfax Avenue in Wheat Ridge. The vehicle was subsequently moved to the shoulder, allowing traffic to resume.

3:20 PM | Disabled Vehicle on Interstate 70

A vehicle stopped on the right shoulder of eastbound I-70 near Garrison Street in Wheat Ridge. The driver reportedly completed a tire change and returned to traffic.

3:18 PM | Outdoor Fire in Lakewood

Fire crews were dispatched for a reported small outdoor fire near West 13th Avenue and Chase Street.

3:00 PM | Two Vehicle Crash Near Kipling and I-70

A reported side impact collision occurred near Kipling Street and Interstate 70 in Wheat Ridge. Dispatch communications indicated minor vehicle damage and deployed airbags. Responding units investigated the scene.

2:54 PM | Elevator or Escalator Rescue

Fire personnel were dispatched to a possible elevator or escalator rescue near Pierce Street in Lakewood.

2:50 PM | Loose Dogs in Traffic

Animal control received reports of two dogs loose near West Belleview Avenue and South Alkire Street in the Dakota Ridge area. The animals were described as a black brindle mastiff and a brown boxer or pit bull mix. Personnel attempted to contact the owner.

2:42 PM | Animal Complaint on Raleigh Street

An officer was assigned to investigate a possible loose rooster complaint near South Raleigh Street in Denver.

RED ROCKS PARK AND MORRISON

5:33 PM | Camera Crew Reported at Red Rocks Box Office

Rangers were asked to investigate a reported camera crew operating near the Red Rocks box office without apparent authorization. The crew’s identity and whether permission was required or obtained remain unconfirmed.

4:40 PM | Wrong Way Driver Reported

A caller reported a possible black vehicle traveling on the wrong side of a roadway inside Red Rocks Park. Venue personnel were asked to locate and contact the driver.

DENVER

5:57 PM | Unattended Bags at Downtown Bus Stop

Officers were directed to investigate a reported unattended Walmart bag and suitcase at a bus stop near 16th Street and Lawrence Street. No information was available indicating whether the items were hazardous.

5:31 PM | Knife Threat Reported

A caller reported that someone displayed or pulled a knife during a party near West Second Avenue. Officers received the complaint as a possible weapons incident.

4:55 PM | Fire Alarm at Grocery Store

Fire crews were dispatched for a reported water flow alarm at a King Soopers location on South Wadsworth Boulevard in the Littleton area.

4:41 PM | Medical Response at Grocery Store

Emergency personnel responded to a King Soopers on South Sheridan Boulevard after a 34 year old man was reportedly experiencing hallucinations. No weapon was reported.

4:35 PM | Disturbance at Transit Platform

Transit personnel reported a passenger playing loud music, smoking and refusing to leave a platform near Chestnut Place.

4:30 PM | RTD Bus Collision at 27th and California

An RTD bus reportedly struck or clipped a parked white Kia Soul near 27th Street and California Street. A crash unit was dispatched, and the incident was referred for follow up. Earlier dispatch communications indicated both parties remained at the scene.

4:12 PM | Rail Crossing Safety Incident

A train operator reported a person walking in front of a train and throwing a crossing gate arm near Lamar Street. The operator reportedly sounded the train horn because of the hazard.

4:04 PM | Traffic Cones Blocking Downtown Street

A caller reported traffic cones obstructing part of 15th Street between Glenarm Place and California Street. A unit was assigned to investigate.

4:02 PM | Crash Near Sixth Avenue and Broadway

Emergency crews were dispatched to a reported collision near West Sixth Avenue and Broadway, including the westbound ramp area.

3:43 PM | Ambulance Blocking Belleview Ramp

Dispatch traffic indicated an ambulance was obstructing a lane on the Belleview Avenue exit ramp from Interstate 25.

3:37 PM | Disturbance Near Park Volleyball Court

An officer reported a man yelling near a parked police vehicle in a park in the West 16th Avenue area. Another unit was requested to assist in monitoring the situation.

3:30 PM | Felony Traffic Stop at 17th and Pennsylvania

Officers conducted a felony traffic stop near East 17th Avenue and Pennsylvania Street. Traffic was temporarily blocked while officers secured the scene. Dispatch communications indicated involved parties were taken into custody.

3:13 PM | Reported Drug and Alcohol Activity

A caller reported approximately 15 people allegedly using narcotics and consuming alcohol near Colorado Boulevard and Bruce Randolph Avenue. The allegations were not independently verified.

3:06 PM | Possible Vehicle and Train Collision

A public works employee relayed a report of a possible collision between a vehicle and train near a dump area. The precise location and whether a collision occurred were not confirmed.

3:00 PM | Animal Control Reports

Animal control communications referenced a possible cat bite reported in Arvada, with the cat reportedly quarantined at a Denver location. A separate loose dog complaint was reported near West Mexico Avenue and South Bryant Street.

2:49 PM | Traffic Collision on Fourth Avenue

Officers responded to a reported minor collision near East Fourth Avenue. A responding unit indicated photographs would be taken before the scene was cleared.

2:20 PM | Three People Detained at Union Station

Officers responded to a reported confrontation involving a Taser at Union Station. Dispatch communications indicated one person was initially held at Taser point, and three people were subsequently detained. The scene was later reported secure.

2:15 PM | Crash Near 38th and Blake

A possible traffic collision was reported near 38th Street and Blake Street, with dispatchers discussing traffic impacts and turning restrictions.

AURORA

5:53 PM | Three Vehicle Injury Crash at Quincy and Chambers

Aurora fire crews responded to a reported three vehicle collision near East Quincy Avenue and South Chambers Road. Heavy vehicle damage was reported, and one occupant may have remained inside a vehicle. Fire command was established.

5:47 PM | Juvenile Injured in Crash

Emergency personnel responded to a possible vehicle collision east of Chambers Road involving a juvenile male. The child was reportedly conscious and breathing. The precise location was not provided.

5:45 PM | Additional Crash Response at Quincy and Chambers

Police and fire units responded to the reported injury collision near East Quincy Avenue and South Chambers Road. Additional fire resources were requested. Dispatch traffic also referenced a possible separate single vehicle collision near East Terminal Circle.

5:35 PM | Tow Truck Working Along Interstate 225

Officers provided traffic protection for a private tow truck assisting a disabled vehicle on the right shoulder of southbound I-225 near Mississippi Avenue.

4:57 PM | Vehicle Blocking Intersection

A vehicle was reported obstructing traffic near East 13th Avenue and Boston Street. Crash response personnel were reportedly operating in the area.

4:54 PM | Bus Breakdown and Crash Report

Transit communications referenced a bus breakdown and a reported serious collision on Parker Road. The relationship between the two incidents was unclear.

4:34 PM | Possible Choking Emergency

Emergency crews responded near East Mississippi Avenue and South Chambers Road for a conscious, breathing man experiencing a possible choking emergency.

THORNTON, COMMERCE CITY AND ADAMS COUNTY

5:41 PM | Two Vehicle Crash on Interstate 25

A two vehicle collision was reported on northbound I-25 near Thornton Parkway. Both vehicles were reportedly on the right shoulder, with one disabled. Police and fire personnel were on scene, and no injuries were reported in the dispatch summary.

5:30 PM | Injury Crash on Interstate 25

Engine 14 was dispatched to a reported injury collision on northbound Interstate 25. The exact mile marker was unclear in the automated transcription.

5:29 PM | Traffic Stop at Washington and 71st

Officers reported a traffic stop involving a white Toyota Corolla near Washington Street and East 71st Avenue in the Commerce City area.

5:24 PM | Hit and Run on Interstate 76

A possible hit and run was reported on eastbound I-76 near Washington Street involving a dark gray Acura and white Ford Fusion. The reporting party reportedly photographed one vehicle before losing sight of it. Officers were assigned to follow up.

5:23 PM | Pothole Hazard on Interstate 25

Dispatchers discussed a possible large pothole or roadway defect in a southbound I-25 travel lane south of the 218 area. Vehicles and pedestrians were reportedly moving near the hazard.

4:59 PM | Reckless Work Truck Reported

A caller reported a white work truck driving aggressively and swerving near Grant Street and East 104th Avenue in Thornton. The vehicle allegedly nearly struck a pedestrian before leaving the area. Its reported travel direction and final location were not confirmed.

4:24 PM | Unregistered SUV Stopped on Interstate 25

Officers conducted a traffic stop involving a black Chevrolet Tahoe with no visible license plate and dark tinted windows near southbound I-25 and 84th Avenue. A summons was reportedly issued for an unsafe or defective vehicle, and towing assistance was requested.

2:04 PM | Patient Evaluated After Crash

Emergency crews evaluated a patient following a reported crash near East 104th Avenue and Marion Street in Thornton. Dispatch communications indicated one injured person was being assessed.

FEDERAL HEIGHTS AND WESTMINSTER

5:17 PM | Parking Violation Complaint

Officers received a complaint involving a Toyota Tacoma and Chevrolet van reportedly parked for several weeks near West 92nd Avenue and Elm Court in Federal Heights.

4:54 PM | Verbal Disturbance at Apartment Complex

Police responded to a reported dispute between a man and woman near West 103rd Avenue in Federal Heights. The parties were reportedly arguing over property, with an unconfirmed allegation that rocks had been thrown at a door.

4:22 PM | Minibike Rider Circling Police

Officers reported a minibike repeatedly circling near West 84th Avenue in Federal Heights. An additional patrol unit was requested.

3:31 PM | Bus Stop Sign Knocked Down

A caller reported a bus stop sign lying on the ground near West 120th Avenue and Zuni Street in Westminster. The sign may have been struck by a vehicle.

BOULDER COUNTY

5:19 PM | Injured Coyote in Superior

Dispatch received a report of a possible injured coyote near Alpha Court in Superior. A unit offered to check on the animal.

ADDITIONAL TRAFFIC AND TRANSIT REPORTS

5:49 PM | Highway 6 Lane Blockage

A lane was reported blocked on the westbound U.S. Highway 6 off ramp to Federal Boulevard. The duration of the obstruction was not established.

5:26 PM | Accident and Tow Coordination

Transportation personnel coordinated a tow following a reported collision near DTC Boulevard in Greenwood Village.

4:52 PM | Possibly Abandoned Dog in Road Median

A caller reported an older black Labrador possibly abandoned and tied in the median near Green Valley Ranch Boulevard and North Tower Road. The dog’s condition and whether animal control recovered it were not established.

4:40 PM | Interstate 25 Lane Obstruction

A disabled vehicle was reported blocking two northbound lanes of I-25 near the Belleview exit. An officer was requested to assist.

2:18 PM | Abandoned Chevrolet on Interstate 25

Transportation personnel investigated a possible abandoned Chevrolet on the right shoulder of southbound I-25 near Colorado Boulevard. Another vehicle initially reported at the location had departed.

2:06 PM | Road Rage Complaint in Littleton Area

A caller reported a blue Volvo speeding and swerving near South Riverside Parkway and East Powers Avenue. The driver allegedly threw a cigarette toward another vehicle before leaving the reporting party’s view.

TRANSIT DISTURBANCE

5:48 PM | Smoking Passenger on Train

Transit personnel reported a passenger smoking aboard a train near Aberdeen Station in Aurora despite announcements to stop. The train was directed to stop near Second and Abilene, according to the dispatch summary, and security assistance was discussed.

PUBLIC SAFETY REMINDER

Drivers should use caution around emergency scenes, disabled vehicles, debris and temporary lane restrictions. Motorists should move over when safely possible and follow instructions from responding personnel.

Anyone witnessing an active emergency should contact 911 rather than relying on preliminary dispatch updates.

Times Mountain Daylight Time. Information comes from preliminary dispatch audio and AI-generated summaries, not independently verified official incident reports. Details may change.

text:
The same day Michael Rosenblum disappeared, police found the car he was driving and towed it to their lot.

His family didn't find out for three months.

It was Valentine's Day 1980, near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Michael was 25 and fighting an addiction to prescription painkillers. The night before, a month after rehab, his mother found pills in his room and told him to leave until he was clean. She later said she would blame herself until the day she died.

The next morning, he dropped his girlfriend off at a gas station and drove off in her car. He said he would meet her at his parents' house in two hours. He never arrived. His money stayed in the bank and his clothes stayed in his closet.

Pittsburgh police searched for the car for two weeks. His father, Maurice, put up flyers, offered a reward and traveled as far as California. Over the years he spent nearly a quarter of a million dollars looking for his son.

That May, police in the suburb of Baldwin Borough told the girlfriend they had her car. An officer had found it on River Road two hours after Michael left her, with two flat tires, no keys and a cold engine. Police said they had mailed her a letter the next day. She said it never came.

Then it got stranger. An anonymous caller told Maurice his son had been arrested by Baldwin police. That July, Baldwin police issued a warrant for Michael over a burglary committed two months after he vanished. The victims had described a man in mirrored sunglasses, but the sketch showed his whole face. The warrant was dropped a week later.

Years later, the police chief's secretary said that months after the tow, the chief had him write a letter to the car's owner dated the day after the car was found. He said he filed it and never mailed it. In 1987 the borough council fired the chief for interfering with the investigation. A civil service commission reinstated him, finding no misconduct, and a state investigation had found no evidence of wrongdoing.

In 1992, a hiker found part of a human skull in the woods near River Road. Tests confirmed it was Michael's. After 12 years, his parents could finally bury their son. How and why he died has never been determined, and no one has ever been charged.

His parents got their son back, but never the answer they spent 12 years looking for.

What do you think happened to Michael that day?

📂 Case file: The Disappearance of Michael Rosenblum (Pennsylvania, 1980)

text:
The Collectivist Delusion: Why Aristotle and Marx Fail the Test of Biblical Truth

In the theater of political philosophy, modern leftists often attempt to cloak their radical economic engineering in the respectable robes of antiquity. They point to Karl Marx’s deep admiration for Aristotle—specifically the ancient Greek assertion that man is merely a politikon zoon, a "political animal"—as proof that human beings are meant to be subjugated to a collective whole.
But this intellectual lineage reveals a deeper, more troubling truth: both Aristotelian paganism and Marxist socialism share a fundamental flaw. They subordinate the sacred, God-given sovereignty of the individual to the tyranny of the collective, whether that collective is called the polis or the proletariat. This pagan-materialist synthesis stands in direct opposition to the true, foundational principles of Western civilization rooted in the Holy Scriptures.

The Pagan State as an Idol

When Aristotle claimed in his Politics that the state is logically "prior to the individual" and that those living outside it are "either beasts or gods," he laid the groundwork for state worship. In the pagan worldview, a man’s worth was derived entirely from his utility to the city-state.
Marxism merely modernized this pagan idolatry. By replacing the Greek polis with the socialist collective and redefining man as a "species-being" (Gattungswesen), Marx stripped humanity of individual soul and free will. In both systems, the individual is reduced to an interchangeable cog in a grand political machine. Whether forced to serve an ancient aristocratic elite or a modern bureaucratic dictatorship of the proletariat, the results are identical: the erasure of personal autonomy and the destruction of true freedom.

The Biblical Contrast: Sovereign Individuals under God

The Holy Scriptures offer a radically different, far more elevated understanding of the human condition—one that completely rejects the collectivism of both the Greek marketplace and the Marxist manifesto.
Created in the Image of God (Imago Dei): Genesis 1:27 establishes that God created man in His own image—as individuals, not as a faceless collective. Human dignity does not depend on a relationship to a state (polis) or an economic class, but on a direct, personal relationship with the Creator.
Individual Free Will and Moral Responsibility: The Bible places the burden of moral choice squarely on the individual. In Ezekiel 18:20, Scripture declares that "the soul who sins is the one who will die" and that a son will not bear the iniquity of the father. Salvation and damnation are individual matters, completely incompatible with Marxist notions of collective class guilt or Aristotle's civic determinism.
The Sanctity of Private Property and Family: While Marx demanded the total abolition of private property and the traditional family, and Aristotle sought state regulation of the household, the Bible firmly protects both. The Commandments "Thou shalt not steal" and "Thou shalt not covet" inherently legitimize private ownership. Property and inheritance are viewed as fruits of honest labor and blessings from God to be managed by families, not tools of production to be seized and redistributed by a predatory state.

True Charity vs. Compulsory Solidarity

Apologists for socialism often try to conflate the early Christian voluntary sharing of goods (as seen in the Book of Acts) with Marxist state coercion. This is a profound misreading of Scripture. Biblical charity is rooted in voluntary, individual giving born of a transformed heart (2 Corinthians 9:7: "Each man should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion").
In contrast, Marxist socialism relies on the raw power of the state to confiscate property, stoke class envy, and enforce a gray, uniform equality. Where the Bible preaches love, personal responsibility, and spiritual redemption, Marxism and pagan collectivism offer only materialist envy, state worship, and the crushing of the individual spirit.

Reclaiming the Foundation

The historical link between Aristotle's politikon zoon and Marxist socialism serves as a stark warning. When a society divorces itself from the transcendent truths of the Bible, it invariably slides back into pagan collectivism, elevating the government or the collective into the position of God.
True freedom, economic prosperity, and moral order cannot be found by looking to the pagan city-states of the past or the failed socialist experiments of the modern era. They are preserved only when we recognize that man is not a political animal bound to the state, but a sovereign creation accountable to God alone.

text:
I'd like to share a little about what I've been working on at my new company @ultrametricai with my cofounder @tylerlastovich. We have been exploring how we could automate the startup itself, leaving founders with more time to focus on their exact mission.

Enter our first release of the Open Startup Repo: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

A common foundation for transparent automation of the startup. 

After close to 20 years in silicon valley, backing hundreds of amazing founders & startups, being in the trenches of founding Heyzap (YC08), then solo founding @golden, going through 2 acquisitions and working behind the scenes with some of the iconic companies today, I'm witnessing the largest change to how we work I could have imagined - a truly monumental era of creative abundance. 

I believe the next generation of companies will largely run themselves: from operations, code, product upgrades, growth, vendor control & selection, process execution, special situations, strategy etc etc. That leaves founder time for 'the art' at the very niche core: the (currently) unautomatable, the special leaps humans tend to make, and north star setting.

We want founders to go super deep into the main problem they are trying to solve and not get held up doing anything else, from searching for domain availability with trademark checks to setting their company up, to running their processes on autopilot. 

So to help that broad foundational layer for starting and running a company, we have spent around a year exploring how to help founders focus on their mission across different verticals, geos, stages and initial starting conditions.

Our first few attempts at making something useful actually failed as the market and AI was moving so fast; it just got absorbed into the models or other product releases. We saw polsia happen, openclaw, then grokbot, muse, dots, etc era as the astras, fables, opuses, kimis and jevs rolled out. What seemed to have been missing along the way was a common repo to identify, unify, open and normalize all the lego bricks that startups have to interact with (vendors, processes, business logic, law, best practices, surface areas, art of the possible). 

As the number of software vendors blew up, the interfaces to drive them multiplied, the international startup founder blew up as silicon valley moved from a specific location to a state of mind and global movement. Unlimited pre seed funding in unlimited vertical sub markets and permutations has brought us to the age of infinity but we have yet to achieve being able to type into an agent a very simple sentence with very complex implications 'just setup my company and make $1m/m'. We have ended up with a hybrid mismash of computer use, API calls, plugins, shifting surface areas (API/MCP/CLI/plugins/chats/musish futures), and changing model absorption to vendor balance making it an exciting and unstable time. 

As our first step we started to rank all the vendors that startups interface to when going about their journey in terms of how agentically controllable they are via their APIs, MCPs, CLIs etc and computer use compatibility as we are largely switching from a UI driven world to the agentic control surfaces and onto full automation. We have 100 ranking areas you can check out with an overall open ranking here: https://t.co/V6XRMME0Ib

Then we looked at the processes that startups do and how the vendors rank for the sub steps or process as a whole and how this changes across geos. Open processes: https://t.co/iSQ90poYxq

Then we started to hack on an open repo for startups that would contain all the components we are going to need for a common foundation for founders across the globe even if our gov processes vary so much from Bengaluru to SF or Lisbon to Shenzhen.  The founder spirit is geo-invariant. 

We have looked at special founder/startup situations, the business logic that will make open modules for the startup that we can hack on together, ranked law firms, government services and interfaces, stacks that go well together. We have mapped the law and lore that maps to startups and the schemas that make up the data objects and documents. But also the open documents and the missing gaps. MUCH TO DO.

All the BS processes and fluff work that founders waste their time on needs to goto zero. I want to see more supersonic planes, cancer drugs, seemingly impossible missions done and increase the bang for buck founders have with their funding. 

This is a work in progress and we are keen for the community to come hack on the repo with us here: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

Lets get into the structure of the general repo and the visualizations we made on https://t.co/XEYK9ipnfI site with example links: 

- Open rankings: https://t.co/V6XRMME0Ib

- Open rankings example (online payments): https://t.co/1kXHZCVfIi

- Open ranking example 2 (cap table): https://t.co/oqBjatGkfW 

- Open processes: https://t.co/iSQ90poYxq

- Open process example (Incorporate C-Corp) https://t.co/pxKUXpW03D

- Open situations that founders face: https://t.co/AFzAp5FRPk

- Open startup simulator (you can test our different initial starting conditions): https://t.co/QqPek01J7K 

- Open modules (e.g. cap table, payroll logic etc - we'd love help improving these) https://t.co/sfzIhgAJYS

- Open law (we are interested in how law changes the processes, situations and normalizing this over time) https://t.co/5yJnYbC0bk

- Open lore (we are interested in the historical lore of startups, the rules of thumb and heuristics that might guide your agent): https://t.co/gjliXoQwe1

- Open fields (we are interested in how the schema for the data connects to the open modules, business logic, open documents and artifacts of each process eg how is a EIN defined?) https://t.co/59rcEXhnCx

- Open documentation (eg SAFE notes and missing! docs) https://t.co/BbvBow2Olt

We have looked at YC companies as well in terms of which ones do well agentically: https://t.co/snnJ83r9ly

We are interested in stacks and how people are changing their work: https://t.co/wFHoew5V9I

We are interested in what is automatable and where the agentic ceiling is currently and how to push that up in all areas: https://t.co/WmTDjmNyV4

There is more for you to explore and a lot more coming in terms of how you will be able to navigate business in an optimal way in your chosen surface area; whether you are hanging in grokbot, dots, muse, claude, terminal, chat, or whatever is coming up in this exciting time. 

We have a lot of data to collect, clean up and help agents navigate the vast landscape emerging functionality the entire startup ecosystem has to offer. 

Come join us getting your vendor in, ranked or that access pattern you have wanted or getting the data more accurate in terms of which vendor is best for a process or steps. Or open a module of something that currently cost money that could be free. 

Also come play in our discord for founders and join the chaos (we can solve each others issues including fund raising tips from me personally): https://t.co/AmBtzFy0Bz 

It's time to lift all the boats in the harbor and I'm extremely excited as to what the community of hackers and painters will hack into the repo, what asks they will have and whether we can shift normalization of processes globally, gov agentic interfaces and have common repo for founders that grows over time. I expect a lot of experimentation along the way, bugs and upside...

I appreciate our backers having faith in us as well from @ycombinator with @garrytan to @immad doing a sizable check (congrats on $1bn rev homie) to @darbyw (congrats on Stripe buying @clerkyinc), @drewhouston form @Dropbox and also @pioneer_fund @tomerlondon cto @GustoHQ and hopefully this is 'boring' and complex enough for Charlie Songhurst :> @delingpole @Liquid2V @ivolo from @segment @ryanpowe @sonicaghi of @kong @DellyTamer+ other supporters (@michaelwfrank, Fundamental ventures and if I missed you sorry moving fast!). 

[And don't worry, all vendor rankings are open scoring methods so no favors are being done if someone backed us and is a vendor they have to compete with how agentic and automatable they are just like anyone else.]

PS: we have bugs and many quality upgrades to make but thought better to go out early and fix as a community. 

PPS: we have other stuff to launch we just thought this was a great place to start and have 200 PRs coming out pretty soon but I still want to know what is broken or doesnt make sense or inaccurate. 

Special thanks to current and past team members for getting us here and all the experiments we did you know who you are.

AI Overview
Ricci Road in Dayton, Nevada, is named after the historic Ricci family and the Ricci Ranch, a prominent Italian-American family that pioneered local agriculture and ranching along the Carson River. 

Key Details
Family Roots: Bernardo Ricci moved to Dayton from Lucca, Italy, around 1900, and built the family ranch house on the property in 1912.
Agricultural History: The Ricci family—along with other Italian immigrant families—helped make the Dayton Valley the "breadbasket of the Comstock," supplying fresh produce, turkeys, and farm goods to Virginia City, Carson City, and regional mining towns. 
Location & Infrastructure: Ricci Road marks the eastern terminus of Nevada State Route 822 (which starts at US Route 50 and crosses the Carson River over the historic 1956 bridge).

Christina Ricci (born 12 February 1980) is an American actress and producer. She portrays Wednesday Addams in the 1991 film The Addams Family. She reprised her role as Wednesday Addams for the 1993 sequel Addams Family Values. She portrays Marilyn Thornhill in seasons one and two of the 2022 Netflix TV series Wednesday.
