text:
A Physician-Backed Framework for Sleeping Through the Night

Sleep continuity, the ability to stay asleep across a full sleep cycle without fragmentation, is increasingly recognized as a distinct and clinically meaningful measure of sleep quality. While total sleep duration receives most of the public health attention, research in sleep medicine consistently shows that interrupted sleep can impair glucose regulation, cortisol rhythm, and cognitive consolidation even when the total hours logged appear adequate.

Via @leannevogel, the framework of good, better, and best sleep strategies offers a practical way to think about intervention intensity. The "good" tier typically anchors around behavioral basics: a consistent sleep and wake time, reduced light exposure in the hour before bed, and a cooler room temperature, factors that signal the circadian system to initiate and sustain sleep architecture. The "better" tier builds on this with more deliberate physiological preparation, such as managing late-day caffeine intake and stabilizing blood glucose before sleep, since nocturnal glucose dips are a documented trigger of early-morning waking. The "best" tier often incorporates more individualized strategies, including magnesium glycinate supplementation, nasal breathing support, or targeted stress-reduction protocols that lower pre-sleep cortisol.

The distinction between tiers matters clinically because not every patient needs the same intervention depth. Sleep hygiene alone resolves fragmentation for some individuals, while others require a more layered approach before measurable improvement appears.

Smart contracts are often described as self-executing. That's only half true.

A contract can hold the rules for what should happen, but it can't wake itself up. Nothing runs until someone sends a transaction that calls it. If no one does, a perfectly written function just sits there.

Automation services exist to close that gap.

⏰ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗚𝗮𝗽 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗲𝗲𝗻 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Plenty of on-chain tasks depend on timing: settling a round, compounding rewards, adjusting a position once a threshold is crossed. Without automation, a team has to run its own bots or rely on users to trigger these calls, and hope they show up at the right moment.

@WINkLink_Oracle  @justinsuntron offers Automation as one of its four services, alongside Price Feeds, VRF and AnyAPI. Its job is to watch registered contracts and execute their logic when their own conditions say it's time.

🧩 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘀

The docs describe three components:

1️⃣ A custom logic contract, written by the developer, that defines the trigger condition and the action
2️⃣ The Registry and Registrar contracts, which track registrations, operational state and each contract's funds
3️⃣ An off-chain Automation node, which listens for new registrations, pauses and cancellations, and keeps checking the active list

🔁 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗢𝗻𝗲 𝗖𝘆𝗰𝗹𝗲 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗸𝘀 𝗟𝗶𝗸𝗲

Every 3 seconds, the node runs each active contract through three steps:

• checkUpkeep: is the condition met?
• simulatePerformUpkeep: would the action succeed if it ran now?
• performUpkeep: execute the action on-chain

Each step has to pass before the next one runs. A failed check means nothing is sent.

💳 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

Registered contracts are funded with WIN through addFunds, and each execution is paid from that balance. If funds run short, the contract won't execute.

During registration a forwarder address is created. Developers are expected to restrict performUpkeep so only that forwarder can call it, and to set the address on their contract. Skip that step and, in the sample setup, the logic never runs.

⚠️ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝘁 𝗗𝗼𝗲𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗥𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗲

Automation decides when to call your code. It doesn't make that code correct. The docs label their sample contracts as unaudited learning material, so condition design, testing on Nile and access control stay with the developer.

Most discussion of oracles focuses on getting data in. Automation answers a quieter question: once the data and the rules are there, who actually pulls the trigger?

text:
Dory Previn refused to let the story of the abandoned wife be the last word.

Born Dorothy Veronica Langan in New Jersey in 1925, she grew up in a strict Irish Catholic household marked by fear, guilt, and a father whose instability could turn the family home into a locked room. 

Music became the exit. In Hollywood she worked as a lyricist, pairing with composer André Previn. They married in 1959 and wrote for films including Pepe (“The Faraway Part of Town,” sung by Judy Garland), Two for the Seesaw (“Second Chance”), and Valley of the Dolls (the theme that became a hit for Dionne Warwick). 

A third Oscar nomination came for “Come Saturday Morning” from The Sterile Cuckoo. The partnership was professional and public; the marriage was more fragile than it appeared.

In 1969 André began an affair with Mia Farrow while working in London. Farrow became pregnant. 

The divorce was finalized in 1970; André married Farrow that September. Dory, already struggling with mental health and a terror of flying that had kept her from accompanying her husband, suffered a breakdown and was hospitalized. 

Some accounts mention electroconvulsive therapy. The public narrative settled quickly: the older wife discarded for the younger actress.

What followed was not silence. From the wreckage she began writing songs that treated her own life as material—childhood trauma, psychiatric wards, loneliness, sexual honesty, the expectation that women absorb humiliation without reply. 

On My Way to Where (1970) announced the shift. Its track “Beware of Young Girls,” set to a lullaby melody, was widely read as a portrait of Farrow: the pale visitor with daisies whose motives proved less than sincere. Mythical Kings and Iguanas followed in 1971. 

The albums were not primarily revenge; they were inventories. She wrote about voices in the hospital, about a father who claimed she was not his child, about the gap between the polished lyrics she had once supplied for other people’s stories and the raw ones she now claimed for herself. 

In an era when Hollywood routinely sidelined women past a certain age, a woman in her mid-forties found her strongest voice by refusing the assigned role.

She later married artist Joby Baker and continued writing songs and prose until her death in Southfield, Massachusetts, on February 14, 2012, at 86. 

The scandal that briefly defined her remains part of the record. The larger record is the work that followed: confessional, sharp, unsentimental, and stubbornly her own. Hollywood offered one script. Dory Previn wrote another.

William Curtis Colepaugh was born in Connecticut in 1918. Before WWII, he had developed an interest in Nazi Germany and its ideology. He even attempted to join the German armed forces before America entered the war, but his efforts were unsuccessful.

In 1942, Colepaugh enlisted in the United States Navy. Yet despite wearing an American uniform, his sympathies remained with Germany. In 1943, he was discharged from the Navy, and the following year he made his way to neutral Portugal, where he contacted German representatives.

Instead of returning home, he traveled to Germany and offered his services to the Nazi regime. German intelligence accepted him and paired him with an experienced German agent named Erich Gimpel.

Their assignment was extraordinary. The Germans intended to send both men secretly into the United States, where they would establish themselves as civilians and collect intelligence useful to the Nazi war effort.

Colepaugh was about to return to his own country, not as an American serviceman, but as an enemy agent.

text:
🇾🇪|The Qabilah: Yemeni Tribes and the Wisdom of Faith

In Arabic, QABILAH means "tribe." Yet, translating it simply as "tribe" fails to capture the full weight of the term. In the context of Yemen, a QABILAH is not merely a "form of social organization." It is a military structure, a legal system, an economic unit, a community of faith, and a defensive pact passed down through generations all compressed into a single word.

The Yemeni QABILAH is an army. It is not a group of "mobilized civilians" it is an army defined by faith, organized by kinship, bound by honor and empowered by the terrain. And its wisdom lies in its faith not any weapon.

💥 Faith Is Not Fanaticism; It Is Discipline

Western media often characterizes the faith of Yemeni tribes as "fanaticism," a lazy, colonialist label. It leads the reader to believe that these people are irrational, unreasonable, or brainwashed.

But within the military structure of the QABILAH, faith is not fanaticism; it is discipline.

It provides a framework of meaning that transcends individual life and death. When a QABILAH fighter heads to the battlefield fully aware that he might die, it is not because he fails to value life. Rather, he believes that dying in defense of his land, his people, and his faith is not an end, but a fulfillment.

It offers a moral code that governs individual conduct. The *Qabilah*’s code of honor dictates what is permissible and what is forbidden: do not kill captives; do not harm women or children; do not break promises; do not abandon wounded comrades. These are not laws written on paper; they are a code woven into the very life of every Qabilah member, from birth until death.

It serves as a bond that sustains social cohesion. The obligations between members of a Qabilah are not merely contractual; they are rooted in kinship. You protect your fellow Qabilah member not for personal gain, but because he is your brother.

This system requires no police force to enforce it.  There is no need for courts to pass judgment, nor for prisons to impose punishment. Instead, it relies on honor, a sense of shame, and a feeling of belonging, forces far more enduring than any external coercion.

🎯 No Central Command, Therefore No "Head" to Sever

At the core of a modern military lies a command node. Destroy that node, and the military is paralyzed. Kill the commander, and the soldiers lose their direction. Sever the lines of communication, and the units lose their coordination.

The qabila (tribal structure) suffers from no such vulnerability.

Every qabila possesses its own council of elders, and each council holds its own decision-making authority. Every member of a qabila belongs simultaneously to a family, a village, the qabila itself, and a broader tribal confederation. Orders originate from the elders, flow through the family units, and reach the individual. There is no single command center to target, no solitary communication line to sever, and no lone commander whose removal could "decapitate" the organization.

For twenty years, Israel and the United States studied how to dismantle Hezbollah’s command structure. They killed Soleimani; they killed Fakhrizadeh; they killed Nasrallah. Each time, they proclaimed a "major victory." Yet, each time, Hezbollah continued to fire rockets, and forces in Yemen continued to launch missiles.

This is because Hezbollah and the forces in Yemen are not defined by any single individual; they are a network. A network has no "head." If you strike one node, the others continue to function.

📜 The Economics of the *Qabila*: Why It Is More Effective Than Mercenaries

In its war in Yemen, Saudi Arabia relied on mercenaries. It provided the funding, the weaponry, and the intelligence essentially paying Yemenis to fight other Yemenis.

The economics of a mercenary force are simple: You pay, I fight. You stop paying, I stop fighting. If the pay is insufficient, I flee; if you send me to my death, I surrender.

The economics of the *qabila* are different: I fight because this is my land. I do not need your money, your weapons, or your intelligence. I only need to know one thing: that you are bombing my home.  What has Saudi Arabia gained for the tens of billions of dollars it has spent? Its mercenaries have fled in Taiz and surrendered in Shabwa; in Al-Jawf, 14,000 of their vehicles were seized. In Aden, when a missile struck, Saudi officers perished in their command center while the mercenaries scattered in every direction.

The Qabila (tribal structures) of Yemen have spent decades building a defense system that requires no money to sustain. Its currency is not the riyal, it is honor. Its bank is not a central bank, it is the collective memory of the Qabila.

⚔️ The Mountains as Weapons

In Yemen, the mountains are not merely "terrain" they are weapons.

A *Qabila* fighter, operating within his own mountainous homeland, possesses distinct advantages:

◾ He knows every narrow path; the enemy does not.
◾He knows every water source; the enemy does not.
◾He knows every potential ambush point; the enemy does not.
◾He knows every cave that can serve as a hideout; the enemy does not.
◾His family lives there. He has nowhere to retreatso he does not retreat.

Saudi Arabia’s F-15s and Eurofighter Typhoons were designed for open plains and urban environments. In the mountains, they cannot locate their targets. Instead, they bomb villages simply because villages are the only things they can see. Yet, these villages are inhabited by people people who belong to the *Qabila*, and who carry guns.

A *Qabila* force fighting in the mountains has no need for an air force. What it requires is the knowledge of where the enemy is, how to reach them, and how to return alive, all of which they already possess.

🔻 The Wisdom of Faith and the Ledger of the Universe

The *Qabila* of Yemen are not "backward." They represent a different form of modernity one that does not rely on centralized authority, industrial systems, or financial networks. It is a modernity capable of functioning even under bombardment and blockade.

Saudi Arabia’s war machine was designed to dismantle states. It cannot destroy the *Qabila*, because the *Qabila* exists outside the framework of the state.  It exists beneath the state, alongside the state, and within the very roots of the state.

The ledger of the universe does not record "who possesses more bombs." Instead, it records: who is doing the bombing, who is being bombed, who is standing their ground, and who is fleeing.

For the tribes of Yemen, the entry in that ledger reads: standing their ground.

Long live the tribes of Yemen. Long live Yemen. Long live Ansar Allah. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

text:
Russia Launches Major Missile and Drone Attack on Ukraine as Zelenskyy Offers Ceasefire Along Current Front Line
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has signalled readiness for a ceasefire based on the current front line, amid US pressure to end the war. Under the proposal, Russian-occupied territory—roughly 25 per cent of Ukraine—would remain under Moscow’s control for the time being, while Kyiv would seek firm security guarantees from its allies.
Hours after Putin agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks, Russia launched a massive overnight attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions. Zelenskyy said Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at the capital in three waves, including missiles carrying cluster warheads. At least nine people were killed and more than 56 injured across Ukraine in the past 24 hours; in Kyiv and its surrounding region, at least two people died and 34 were wounded.
Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia used Iskander-M, S-400, Zircon and Onyx missiles, along with 210 drones, including 110 jet-powered drones. Ukrainian air defences reported downing or suppressing 181 drones, but strikes were recorded at 32 locations. Residential buildings, energy facilities, railway and metro infrastructure, shopping centres, businesses and a monastery were damaged.
Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed “in principle” to resume Russia-US-Ukraine peace talks after a roughly three-hour meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg. The Kremlin said the talks could begin after November 10, possibly in Abu Dhabi, and would focus on post-war security arrangements for both Russia and Ukraine.
Moscow’s mayor accused Ukraine of launching 630 drones toward the Russian capital, saying most were intercepted and two people were injured. Russia has not endorsed the latest peace proposals, while US President Donald Trump has claimed that an end to the war is closer than before.

U.S. Air Force Major General Edward Geary Lansdale became a living legend in the Philippines during the early 1950s by combining advertising tricks, social reforms, and psychological warfare to help crush the communist Hukbalahap (Huk) rebellion... 

Working as a CIA and U.S. military adviser, Lansdale formed a close bond with Philippine Defense Minister Ramon Magsaysay. Instead of relying solely on heavy military bombardments that killed civilians, Lansdale pushed the Philippine military to build trust, treat villagers like brothers, and offer land settlements (EDCOR farms) to surrendering guerrillas. Lansdale helped engineer Magsaysay’s run for the presidency in 1953 using American-style campaign tactics and the slogan "Magsaysay Is My Guy," earning Lansdale the playful moniker "Col. Landslide".

. . . 

In the early 1950s, the Philippine government was fighting the Hukbalahap, or Huks, a communist-led rebel movement. American intelligence officer Edward Lansdale was sent to help, working closely with Ramon Magsaysay, the country’s defense secretary.

Lansdale believed the war could be won through psychology as much as firepower, and he studied local beliefs closely. Lansdale’s psychological warfare team exploited local folklore about the aswang (a vampiric shape-shifting monster).

Operatives sneaked into Huk-controlled areas, ambushed a rear guard, punctured the dead rebel's neck to mimic a vampire bite, and left the body where his comrades would find it. According to his own memoir, his team first spread rumors that an aswang was living in the hills where a Huk unit was based. Then they ambushed a Huk patrol, quietly captured the last man in line and killed him. They made two puncture marks on his neck to look like a vampire bite and left his body on the trail.

Terrified of a demon stalking the hills, the superstitious rebels abandoned their position in panic.

When the Huks found him, Lansdale wrote, they fled the area.

The rebellion collapsed over the next few years, helped by military pressure and land reforms. Magsaysay was elected president of the Philippines in 1953.

Lansdale became so well known that he’s widely believed to have inspired a character in the 1958 bestseller “The Ugly American.”

text:
Meta steals engineers from its Big Tech peers, then loses them to frontier AI labs.

I pulled 24 months of LinkedIn-visible engineering moves in and out of Meta (Oct 2024 to Oct 2026) using Crustdata (YC F24).

The tl;dr is that Meta wins most of its Big Tech trades, but loses the AI lab trade by a ratio of 6 to 1.

4 patterns to watch:

1. Big Tech is Meta's farm system

Amazon sends Meta 7 engineers for every 1 it takes back. Microsoft and TikTok/ByteDance run close to 4:1 in Meta's favor. Google is basically a wash.

2. The labs are the main attraction for those exiting

OpenAI hired ~9 Meta engineers for every 1 Meta hired back. Google DeepMind is about 2:1. Meta barely hires from Anthropic at all.

3. The Superintelligence hiring spree didn't plug the leak

After July 2025, Meta's monthly hiring from AI labs roughly tripled. Its monthly losses to them nearly quadrupled.

4. The surprise feeder is finance 

Capital One sends Meta more engineers than Oracle or Google DeepMind. JPMorganChase, Bloomberg and Goldman Sachs all feed Meta too.

And it's not just researchers walking out. 57% of the Meta engineers OpenAI hired had software engineer titles, not research ones.

My read here is that big-company comp wins you engineers from other big companies, but it doesn't beat companies that offer the chance to build the frontier of AI.

Disclaimer: this analysis was based on LinkedIn-visible moves only, engineering titles only. Treat it as directional.

The detail that matters most for the rest of the region: every one of the 2 billion shares on offer is an existing share.

At KES 7.50, that is KES 15 billion, about $115.6 million, for half the company, valuing QuickMart at roughly KES 30 billion. QuickMart itself raises nothing. Sokoni Retail, majority-held by Adenia's fund, is selling. This is a private equity exit running through a public market, and East Africa almost never gets one.

The usual door out is a trade sale. Africa: The Big Deal counts about 20 exits above $50 million across African tech in a decade, and Stears and Ventures Platform found acquisitions behind 73% of 181 tracked venture exits since 2011. Listings are the rare exception.

That shortage travels backwards. Only 5.5% to 6.5% of African startups that raised seed in 2021 to 2023 reached a Series A within three years. Funds that cannot see an exit price the early rounds for it, and the money never recycles into the next cohort.

If the 75% subscription floor is met by 30 October, Nairobi gets proof that a well-governed company with a dividend policy can return capital to its backers through the exchange. For Kampala, where the USE's small-company window has no published count of admissions, that proof is the argument for building the same path.

What would you watch in the first year of trading to know whether this opens the door for the next PE-backed listing?

text:
The Fed can cut rates. It can't guarantee cheaper long-term borrowing.

Since mid-September, the extra compensation investors demand to hold long-term Treasuries... the term premium.... has climbed roughly 40 basis points to 0.98%, its highest since 2014.

That's more than the entire rise in the 10-year yield. In other words, expectations for Fed policy alone don't explain the move.

And that's the problem.

Even if a ceasefire eases geopolitical pressure or the Fed pauses, investors still have to absorb war spending and roughly $220 billion in big-tech bond sales this year. All of it competes for long-term capital.

For your portfolio, the distinction matters: a friendlier Fed doesn't automatically mean a lasting rally in long bonds. 
→ If the supply pressure persists, relief could fade, long-duration stocks could remain sensitive, and bonds may offer less protection when equities fall.

The question isn't just where rates go next. It's how much investors will demand to lend for the long haul.

text:
BROKEN PROMISES CAUSED UKRAINE WAR - For over three decades, the United States has pursued a foreign policy so reckless, so arrogant, and so fundamentally dishonest that it has not only destabilized Europe but plunged it into a vortex of bloodshed, betrayal, and ruin. At the heart of this catastrophe lies the relentless eastward expansion of NATO—a military alliance that has become little more than a tool of American hegemony—pushing ever closer to Russia’s borders in direct violation of a solemn promise made by President George H.W. Bush to Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev. That promise, delivered in 1990 amid the delicate negotiations to end the Cold War, was clear: NATO would not expand “one inch eastward” beyond its then-boundaries. It was a pledge of peace, a cornerstone of trust in a world weary of superpower rivalry. Yet, the United States shattered that trust, embarking on a campaign of imperial overreach that has not only undermined the security of Europe and Russia but sparked the Ukraine-Russia war—a conflict that has claimed millions of lives and for which the U.S. and NATO bear primary responsibility. This is not mere geopolitical miscalculation; it is a moral failure of staggering proportions, a betrayal of humanity itself.

Let us begin with the agreement that was supposed to herald a new era. In February 1991, as the Soviet Union teetered on the brink of dissolution, U.S. Secretary of State James Baker III and German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher met with Gorbachev to negotiate German reunification—a pivotal moment in ending the Cold War. Genscher, speaking for the West, assured Gorbachev that “NATO will not move eastward,” a commitment echoed by Baker and cemented in the juridical context of the 2+4 Treaty negotiations. This was not a casual remark but a deliberate promise, documented in the National Security Archive at George Washington University, where countless records reveal what Gorbachev heard: NATO’s expansion would stop. The Warsaw Pact’s dissolution would not be exploited. The West would honor Russia’s security concerns. Gorbachev, hailed by many as the greatest statesman of the modern age for his courage in dismantling the Soviet empire, took this pledge at face value. He trusted the United States. And that trust was repaid with treachery.

Within years, the U.S. discarded its word as if it were a scrap of paper. By 1994, President Bill Clinton had formalized NATO’s eastward enlargement, setting the stage for a project that would stretch over three decades and multiple administrations—a continuity of hubris unbroken from Clinton to Bush, Obama to Trump, and Biden. The first wave came in 1999, with Hungary, Poland, and the Czech Republic joining NATO. Russia protested, its voice drowned out by American triumphalism. Then, in 2004, seven more nations—the Baltic states, Romania, Bulgaria, Slovenia, and Slovakia—were absorbed, pushing NATO’s frontier perilously close to Russia’s heartland. Each step was a provocation, a calculated slap in the face to a nation still reeling from the Soviet collapse. But the true breaking point came in 2008, when the U.S. rammed through plans to extend NATO membership to Ukraine and Georgia—countries on Russia’s doorstep, steeped in historical and strategic significance. This was no longer expansion; it was encirclement.

The architects of this policy—figures like Cheney, Wolfowitz, and Brzezinski—operated under a delusion of unipolarity, born in the euphoria of 1991 when the Soviet Union dissolved and the U.S. declared itself the world’s sole superpower. They believed, as Brzezinski wrote in The Grand Chessboard in 1997, that Russia could do nothing but submit to NATO’s march eastward. Neutrality became a dirty word in their lexicon; any nation not under America’s military umbrella was suspect, subversive, a latent enemy. Diplomacy was scorned in favor of game theory—a sterile, unilateral exercise where the other side’s perspective is ignored, its fears dismissed. The U.S. didn’t negotiate with Russia; it dictated. And when Russia resisted, it was branded an aggressor, a new Hitler, a tired trope trotted out every few years to justify endless war—Saddam, Assad, now Putin. This mindset, codified in RAND Corporation papers like the 2019 report “Extending Russia,” sought not peace but provocation, aiming to destabilize Russia through sanctions, military pressure, and proxy conflicts. The result? A war in Ukraine that has turned a once-neutral nation into a graveyard.

The Ukraine-Russia war, erupting in 2022, is the grotesque culmination of this betrayal. It is a conflict the U.S. and NATO engineered through their relentless push to plant missiles and bases on Russia’s border—a move no superpower would tolerate in its own sphere. Imagine China or Russia establishing a military foothold on the Rio Grande or in Ontario; the U.S. would unleash war within hours, not minutes. Yet, America expects Russia to accept Aegis missile systems in Poland and Romania, a mere seven minutes from Moscow—a decapitation strike in waiting. When Russia objected, when Putin in 2007 at Munich pleaded, “Enough, stop now,” the U.S. doubled down, jamming NATO enlargement to Ukraine down Europe’s throat in 2008. William Burns, then-ambassador to Russia, warned in a leaked memo: “Nyet means nyet.” The U.S. ignored him, as it ignored Gorbachev’s ghost.

The human cost of this arrogance is apocalyptic. Since 2022, estimates suggest up to 1.5 - 2 million Ukrainians—soldiers and civilians—have died or been grievously wounded, with over 300,000 Russian lives lost. This is not hyperbole; it is the grim arithmetic of a war fueled by American weapons, American training, and American insistence that Ukraine fight to the last man. U.S. senators like Blumenthal and Romney crow that it’s “the best money America can spend—no Americans are dying.” A million lives snuffed out, and they call it a bargain. This is not collateral damage; it is a massacre orchestrated by a nation that reneged on its word and turned Ukraine into a proxy slaughterhouse. The Minsk II agreement, unanimously backed by the U.N. Security Council in 2015 to grant autonomy to Ukraine’s east, could have averted this. The U.S. and Ukraine scuttled it, with Europe—France and Germany, the guarantors—meekly acquiescing. Neutrality, offered by Putin in December 2021 as a last-ditch plea to avoid war, was rejected by Jake Sullivan with a smug, Don’t worry, "there will be no war.” Seven days into Russia’s invasion, Zelensky was ready to negotiate neutrality. The U.S. and U.K., via Boris Johnson, ordered him to walk away. The blood of millions stains their hands.

Europe, too, has been destabilized by this American folly. Far from enhancing security, NATO’s expansion has turned the continent into a frontline, its nations pawns in a U.S.-led chess game. The Baltic states, once secure in neutrality, now host American bases, their Russian minorities—25% of Estonia and Latvia—antagonized by Russophobic policies egged on by Washington. Ukraine, once a buffer, is now a battleground, its sovereignty shredded not by Russia alone but by America’s refusal to let it remain neutral. Georgia, lured by NATO promises in 2008, saw war erupt within months, its safety sacrificed to U.S. ambition. Europe’s economy reels from severed Russian trade—Nord Stream’s destruction, widely attributed to Ukrainian sabotage, a stark symbol of its vassalage. The continent has no voice, no unity, no foreign policy—only loyalty to an America that views it as a staging ground, not a partner.

Russia’s security, too, has been gutted. The nuclear arms framework, painstakingly built to prevent catastrophe, lies in ruins—torn apart when the U.S. abandoned the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty in 2002 and the INF Treaty in 2019. NATO’s advance, coupled with missile deployments, has forced Russia into a corner, its fears of encirclement dismissed as paranoia by a West blind to its own hypocrisy. Putin’s intention in 2022 was not imperial conquest—childish propaganda—but to force Ukraine’s neutrality and keep NATO at bay. The U.S. ensured that failed, preferring war to compromise.

This is the legacy of U.S. foreign policy: a broken promise, a destabilized Europe, a Russia pushed to the brink, and millions dead in a war that need never have happened. Bush’s “one inch” pledge was not just a diplomatic footnote; it was a lifeline to peace, discarded by a nation drunk on power. NATO, sold as a shield, has become a sword, wielded by an America that thrives on conflict, not cooperation. The deaths in Ukraine are not Russia’s alone to bear—they are the fruit of a U.S. policy that chose domination over dialogue, betrayal over honor. Europe must awaken, reject this imperial yoke, and forge its own path—or it, too, will drown in the carnage of America’s making.

text:
The Mystic Alerts Act (H.R. 7022, 119th Congress) is a bipartisan law signed by President Trump on October 22, 2026. It directs the FCC to establish rules so commercial mobile providers that already participate in the Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) system can optionally transmit those alerts via satellite (in addition to traditional terrestrial cell networks) to compatible devices.
(<https://t.co/1s6lSYuofu>)[](<https://t.co/A76LpghtWc>)

Background and Motivation
The bill is named for Camp Mystic, a girls’ summer camp on the Guadalupe River in Kerr County, Texas. On July 4, 2025, catastrophic flash flooding killed roughly 25–28 people at the camp (mostly young campers and counselors, plus the camp’s co-executive director) and more than 100 others across Central Texas (figures commonly cited around 119 in Kerr County or over 130 regionally). A flash flood warning was issued by the National Weather Service at about 1:14 a.m., but reports noted that Wireless Emergency Alerts often failed to reach people once cellular infrastructure was damaged or in areas with poor terrestrial coverage and challenging terrain.
(<https://t.co/VvgxBZuTIw>)(<https://t.co/QIVuX1mjn4>)(<https://t.co/RXzHXHXQ5q>)

Sponsors and supporters framed the legislation as a response to those communication gaps. Lead House sponsor Rep. August Pfluger (R-TX-11) introduced it with original cosponsors including Rep. Lizzie Fletcher (D-TX-7), Rep. Marc Veasey (D-TX-33), and Rep. Buddy Carter (R-GA-1); Rep. French Hill (R-AR-2) later joined. A Senate companion was led by Sens. John Cornyn (R-TX) and Jon Ossoff (D-GA). The House Energy and Commerce Committee reported it favorably (amended) by a 52–0 vote; the House passed it under suspension; the Senate passed it by unanimous consent. It became law after signature on October 22, 2026.
(<https://t.co/y8ZF2lmUeC>)[](<https://t.co/pFAWA2hU7s>)

Current WEA System
WEAs are short, geographically targeted emergency messages (e.g., weather, AMBER, presidential) delivered through the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System (IPAWS) managed by FEMA. They use cellular broadcast technology over participating commercial mobile networks. Provider participation is voluntary under the Warning, Alert, and Response Network Act (WARN Act). Only devices connected to a participating network in the targeted area receive them. The system does not currently require or standardize satellite paths.
(<https://t.co/5wdpC0uhKu>)

Key Provisions of the Act
The enrolled bill text (Public Law as signed) is concise and centers on optional satellite capability for already-participating providers that also offer satellite voice/data service.

- Covered service providers: Defined as commercial mobile service providers that (1) voluntarily elect to transmit emergency alerts under the WARN Act and (2) make satellite voice and data communications available to their subscribers.
(<https://t.co/1s6lSYuofu>)

- Provider election (must occur within 60 days after the effective date of the FCC’s final rule):
  - Providers file an election with the FCC on whether they will transmit emergency alerts by satellite (in addition to existing terrestrial transmission) to subscribers whose devices are capable of receiving them.
  - If electing to transmit: notify the FCC, agree to follow the FCC’s technical standards/protocols/procedures/requirements, honor existing subscriber opt-outs (or classes of alerts) under the WARN Act, and impose **no separate or additional charge** for the satellite transmission or capability.
  - If electing not to transmit: notify new and existing subscribers in the same manner required for non-participation under the existing WARN Act provisions. Electing not to transmit does not, by itself, create liability.
(<https://t.co/1s6lSYuofu>)

- FCC rulemaking:
  - Publish a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking within 6 months of enactment to establish requirements facilitating satellite alerting.
  - Requirements must take into account satellite transmission capabilities and mobile device reception/display capabilities, and minimize impact on other voice and data communications (including 9-1-1).
  - Issue a final rule within 18 months of enactment, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the FEMA Administrator.
(<https://t.co/1s6lSYuofu>)

- Effective date of the final rule: The later of (i) 36 months after publication in the Federal Register, or (ii) 12 months after DHS and FEMA implement any necessary standards, protocols, or procedures for transmitting alerts from originators to the providers (with notice to the FCC). This creates a multi-year runway for standards development and deployment.
(<https://t.co/1s6lSYuofu>)

- Liability limitations: Covered providers (and their officers, directors, employees, vendors, and agents) that transmit satellite alerts and meet the Act’s obligations are not liable to subscribers or users for acts/omissions related to, or harm from, transmission or failure to transmit an alert by satellite, or for releasing subscriber information used in delivering such an alert to government, public safety, fire, law enforcement, EMS, or emergency facilities. Non-election alone creates no liability basis.
(<https://t.co/1s6lSYuofu>)

Implementation Timeline (High Level)
- Enactment: October 22, 2026.
- FCC NPRM: by ~April 2027.
- FCC final rule: by ~April 2028.
- Rule effective date: potentially 2029–2031 or later, depending on Federal Register publication and DHS/FEMA readiness.
- Provider elections: 60 days after the effective date.

Practical Effects and Context
The law does *not* mandate that providers offer satellite alerts or that all carriers participate. It creates an optional pathway with technical standards, consumer protections (opt-out continuity and no extra fees), and liability shields to encourage adoption where providers already have satellite capabilities (e.g., partnerships with satellite operators). It aims to fill gaps in rural, remote, or disaster-damaged areas where terrestrial towers fail or coverage is sparse, while preserving the existing WEA architecture.
(<https://t.co/UyChmAkKLi>)(<https://t.co/VvgxBZuTIw>)

Official sources for the full enrolled text and committee report include https://t.co/1Ab81kH3fT (H.R. 7022) and the House Report 119-616. Related contemporaneous reporting and sponsor statements emphasize the Texas flood communications failures as the catalyst.

text:
You love presenting half truths and expecting everyone to accept the conclusion.

QPA is not interchangeable with actual in-network reimbursement. A published study using Elevance’s own data found QPAs approximately 30% below the corresponding in-network medians—roughly 70% of that benchmark. So “3.5 times QPA” does not establish “3.5 times in-network rates,” much less prove overpayment. Your denominator matters.

The Fifth Circuit explicitly addressed this in August, finding that including non-negotiated ghost rates produced artificially low QPAs. That is a court finding you cannot wave away because the resulting arbitration awards look expensive relative to that benchmark.

Insurers have multiple opportunities to resolve these claims without an arbitration award. They can make a reasonable initial payment, negotiate during the mandatory 30-business-day period, and reach a settlement even after arbitration begins. Arbitration is avoidable through agreement. Insurers have choices throughout this process.

And there is evidence that those opportunities are being squandered. In AFHC’s survey covering 2023, respondents reported insurers failed to reply during open negotiation 37% of the time and made no counteroffer another 34%. That is provider-reported evidence, but it deserves examination instead of being ignored.

The ASA, ACEP and ACR analysis of 2025 federal data found insurers lost by default on 24.5% of line items and submitted offers of $1 or less on 8.2%. Insurer nonparticipation and nominal offers belong in any honest discussion of physician win rates.

Your claim that higher offers barely affect win rates also proves considerably less than you suggest. Successful settlements never enter those arbitration win-rate comparisons. Looking only at cases that remain disputed cannot establish that reasonable offers and meaningful negotiation would fail to prevent arbitration. That is a basic limitation of your analysis.

CMS has also documented actual compliance failures: its Aetna Texas air-ambulance audit found incorrect QPA calculations and failures to provide required disclosures. These problems are documented, not hypothetical.

If insurers want fewer arbitrations, they can negotiate reasonable contracts, make defensible offers, participate in the process and pay what they owe.

Blaming physicians for using the remedy Congress created, while minimizing insurer conduct that contributes to these disputes, is selective storytelling.

text:
CBS Pushes Trump Voter Intimidation Narrative, Chris Hayes Echoes It, Ilhan Omar Reinforces It

On the October 21 broadcast of All In with Chris Hayes on MS NOW, Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar sat down for a softball interview in which Hayes echoed CBS News’ voter-intimidation allegations, and Omar reinforced them by accusing the President of trying to scare Americans away from voting in the November midterm elections. Hayes linked the federal search of Omar’s Washington, D.C., home to a separate Homeland Security investigation into possible noncitizen voting, suggesting both were part of a Trump administration intimidation campaign.

Since when did investigating possible violations of federal immigration laws and whether noncitizens illegally registered or voted in federal elections become voter intimidation?

Hayes said:

“There’s CBS has been reporting that these officers from HSI, the same folks that went, you know, searched your house, having showing up the doors of other people, immigrants and asking them questions about whether they register to vote.”

He then repeated CBS’s voter-intimidation narrative, which Omar would later echo:

“Part of the undertaking by the Trump administration, I think, clearly to intimidate people. Is that your understanding of what this was about?”

Notice what Hayes did there. He identified the federal agency involved in both investigations, connected the two on national television, and then characterized the administration’s motive as voter intimidation. But what does an investigation into noncitizen voting have to do with a federal criminal investigation involving Omar’s immigration paperwork?

The investigation involving Omar concerns possible false statements and immigration fraud connected to paperwork dating back to her childhood. Agents searched her home pursuant to a judicially authorized warrant. The other investigation concerns potential illegal voting by noncitizens, with federal agents questioning residents about their immigration status and voter registration. These are different matters, yet Hayes treated them as pieces of the same political conspiracy.

She said:

“They’ve done this sort of full press where they kept alluding to the fact that something was going to happen to me. And I think a lot of their right-wing influencers who seem to have direct connection to not just the president but his orbit, I think they were starting to lose faith that these were empty promises and they had to do something, I believe, to say, ‘Hey, look, we raided her house. Now you can feel comfortable that we are doing something.'”

But Omar was already being investigated by federal authorities during President Joe Biden’s administration. In June 2024, Biden’s Justice Department reportedly opened an investigation into her finances, campaign spending, and dealings with a foreign national. That investigation reportedly stalled. A separate investigation involving possible immigration fraud led to the October 12 search of her home under Trump.

Omar portrays the search as political theater designed to satisfy Trump’s supporters, but federal investigators were already examining her activities during Biden’s presidency. If Omar was being investigated under Biden, why should viewers automatically assume that an investigation under Trump must be politically motivated?

She continued:

“I think ultimately their goal is to intimidate and like scare people, um, from, from wanting to participate and vote.”

That is ridiculous. So now people are supposed to believe that investigating Omar’s immigration records is intended to keep Americans from voting? Oh please, tell us more. And how does investigating possible illegal voting amount to intimidating eligible American citizens?

American citizens have the right to vote in federal elections. Noncitizens do not. Enforcing that distinction is not voter suppression.

Then Omar offered what she considered evidence that the administration’s supposed intimidation campaign was backfiring. She said that while traveling to the interview, she was receiving reports about early voting:

“There’s a massive line at early voting sites.”

She added that her staff was struggling to accommodate requests from people needing transportation to vote:

“We just, we don’t have the capacity to keep up with the requests that we’re getting.”

Omar suggested that Trump’s alleged effort to discourage voting was having the opposite effect. But a report of long lines and increased requests for rides does not establish why those people are voting, which candidates they support, or whether total turnout will break any records.

There is an actual increase in Minnesota early voting. On October 22, Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon reported that approximately 202,000 voters had already cast ballots, about 17% more than at a comparable point in the 2022 midterm election. But Simon also acknowledged that voting earlier does not necessarily mean more people will vote overall. Some voters may simply be casting their ballots sooner. And President Trump himself is encouraging early voting. On October 3, he urged Republicans not to wait if their state offers early voting. So why should Omar assume that increased early voting is a reaction against Trump when Trump is actively encouraging his supporters to vote early?

Omar provided no evidence establishing that Trump’s immigration enforcement policies caused the lines she described. She offered anecdotes, opinions, and Hayes supplied the political narrative. Neither explained how a federal criminal investigation involving a sitting member of Congress demonstrates a plot to intimidate American citizens out of voting.

But that’s what happens in a softball interview. Instead of pressing Omar to explain her accusations, Hayes helped make them for her. 

CBS News pushed the voter-intimidation allegations, Hayes repeated them, and Omar reinforced them. Three voices pushing the same narrative, without establishing that these separate investigations were part of a campaign to intimidate legitimate voters. Fake news indeed.

PASSPORT FRAUD MAY BE THE CHARGE THAT STILL STICKS TO ILHAN OMAR

Seasoned federal investigators know passport fraud offers a path that the usual statute of limitations cannot easily close. Under 18 U.S.C. § 1542, it is a federal crime to make any false statement in a passport application, to use a passport obtained through false statements, or to use a passport with an assumed or false name to hide other criminal behavior. The 10-year clock resets every time the person renews that passport if the underlying records, such as a Social Security Number obtained by lying about date or place of birth, were fraudulent to begin with.

This is not abstract legal theory. The same approach was used after 9/11 to secure a holding charge against Anwar al-Awlaki, the American-born cleric who later became a senior al-Qaeda figure. Awlaki was born in Las Cruces, New Mexico. When he wanted college money he was not eligible for as a U.S. citizen, he used a Yemeni passport and false claims about his birthplace to obtain roughly $20,000 in USAID funding for studies at Colorado State University. Once in the country he applied for a Social Security Number while falsely listing Yemen as his place of birth. He then used that fraudulently obtained number to get a U.S. passport. Each renewal restarted the limitations period.

A State Department Diplomatic Security agent uncovered the false statements on the J-1 visa and passport paperwork. The USAID certificate from 1990 lists him as a Yemeni exchange visitor receiving full funding. The underlying scholarship fraud had already timed out, but the passport fraud angle remained available precisely because the renewals kept the clock running. That is how the system works when the original application was built on a lie.

If Ilhan Omar or those who prepared her records made false statements about age, birthplace, or other material facts to obtain a Social Security Number, citizenship documents, or a passport, the same reset applies. Every renewal of a passport that rests on those false underlying records restarts the 10-year window. Federal agents have already raided her Washington residence and seized her passport as part of an investigation focused on her family’s immigration paperwork and conflicting birth-year records. The law does not grant members of Congress a special exemption from the truth on a government form.

The Awlaki case shows the government has used this exact tool against a U.S.-born citizen who gamed eligibility rules and then lied to paper over it. Whether the same evidence exists in Omar’s file is what investigators are now examining. The statute remains on the books, the renewals keep the clock alive, and the forms either match the facts or they do not.

Sources: Catherine Herridge reporting, October 21, 2026; 18 U.S.C. § 1542; USAID exchange visitor certificate for Anwar al-Awlaki, 1990; Washington Times and Washington Post reporting on the ongoing federal investigation into Omar’s immigration records and birth-date discrepancies, October 2026.

October twenty three, two thousand twenty six. The Western narrative claims that closure of the Iranian border caused a gas crisis in Pakistan.

The claim is a lie. The lie shifts blame from those who signed agreements onto those under sanctions.

Deconstruction of the narrative

The logic of the Western narrative follows this sequence: Iran closes border, gas shortage follows in Pakistan, therefore blame Iran.

Iran did not close the border. Pakistan closed the border. In October two thousand twenty six Islamabad shut the border with Iran under the framework of the Mecca Agreement and cited technical issues. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei remarked at the time that it was best to avoid speculating on motives. Tehran offered Islamabad a face saving exit and chose not to expose truth publicly.

Sources within the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority of Pakistan dismantled that face saving cover. The sources made it clear that border closure is a primary factor in the current LPG crisis.

Whoever closed the door must take responsibility for the empty kitchen inside. The party that closed that door is not in Tehran. The party is at military headquarters in Rawalpindi.

The second route blocked by their own masters

The Western narrative focuses exclusively on the first route, the Iranian border, and ignores the second, the Strait of Hormuz.

Pakistan relies on imports for seventy percent of LPG. Nearly fifty percent of imports arrive from Iran via land routes. The remainder comes from Iraq and Oman via sea routes that pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Strait of Hormuz is blocked because the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February twenty eight. The United States Navy intercepts vessels in the Strait. Iran laid naval mines in self defense and asserted control over shipping lanes and shot down drones.

Pakistan did not participate in that war, yet maritime supply routes of Pakistan were severed by that war, while land routes were shut by the own hand of Pakistan. Two paths exist. One is blocked by a master. The other is blocked by own hand. Islamabad calls this a technical issue.

Trading kitchens for riyals

Munir closed the border because of the Mecca Agreement and because of Saudi money and because of tacit approval of Washington. The military of Pakistan needed to prove to Riyadh and Washington that they are obedient and willing to pull the shutter down on the eastern flank of Iran on their behalf.

He got a promise of discounted Saudi oil in return and a nod from the United States for an IMF loan and a lunch at the White House and a remark from Trump calling him my favorite marshal.

Ordinary people of Pakistan got empty LPG distribution points and spiraling prices in the open market and advice from the Quetta Chamber of Commerce to stop placing orders and hundreds of trucks stranded on both sides of the border and families discovering as winter sets in that gas cylinders are empty.

This is the true cost sharing arrangement of the Mecca Alliance. Saudi Arabia provides money. Pakistan provides lives. Yemen serves as battlefield. Washington supplies weapons. Kitchens of Pakistan foot the bill.

The ledger of the universe

Pakistan attempted to align with United States sanctions and Saudi strategy to suffocate the economy of Iran. Pakistan closed the border.

Iran was not suffocated. Iran laid mines in the Strait of Hormuz and shot down fifty four MQ nine drones and shut down airports of Saudi Arabia and struck the Ministry of Defense building in Riyadh.

Tremors in the Strait of Hormuz paralyzed maritime routes through which Pakistan imports LPG from Iraq and Oman.

You cut off the land route of someone else and your own sea route gets severed. You join sanctions to suffocate a neighbor and the self defense of that neighbor suffocates your own kitchen. This is not retaliation. This is physics. This is arithmetic of the universe and it requires no permission.

Politicians in Islamabad imagined they could serve as a useful pawn on the American chessboard while keeping their own nation out of harm. They forgot one thing. When a country surrenders control of border policy to foreign masters, the country places energy security of its own at mercy of missiles of adversaries.

Exposing truth

The military establishment in Islamabad bypassed parliament and closed borders and traded energy security of the nation for political endorsement from Saudi Arabia and the United States. The price is paid in kitchens of ordinary citizens, while the signing bonus is pocketed by the high command.

The ledger of the universe will not alter its balance based on narratives spun by Western media. The ledger records only this: who signed papers and who received money and who is left out in the cold.

Noored Kotkad: A Stepping Stone to the Army
“Noored Kotkad” (Young Eagles) is Estonian patriotic youth organization. It is the official youth branch of the Estonian Defence League (Kaitseliit) which is the country's national volunteer defense force.
 
The organization was officially created on May 27, 1930. The leaders of the Estonian Defence League realized that they needed to prepare the next generation to protect their newly independent country. Before this there were other youth groups but the leaders wanted an organization specifically focused on national defense and deep love for Motherland.
 
The main idea of Noored Kotkad is to raise boys who are physically healthy, morally strong and always ready to help. They teach youth to be independent,work in a team and to take responsibility for their actions. The boys learn practical skills like reading maps,building fires, and giving first aid. They are taught to respect their history and culture,protect the weak, and be honest. Their motto is "Alati valmis!" (Always ready!) meaning they must always be prepared to serve their nation. In the 1930s the Young Eagles grew very quickly. Soon,almost every school and village in Estonia had a local group. By 1939 nearly 20,000 members had joined the organization.
 
This peaceful growth was destroyed in the summer of 1940 when the Soviet Union occupied Estonia. The soviet government immediately banned Noored Kotkad. They wanted to destroy Estonian patriotism and force the youth to join the soviet "pioneer" movement instead. Many adult leaders of the Young Eagles were arrested,sent to prison camps in Siberia or killed.

However,the Young Eagles did not give up. The boys secretly hide their flags,badges and uniforms to protect them from the soviet invaders. Instead of accepting the occupation,many activists formed secret resistance groups in their schools. They printed and shared anti-soviet posters and secretly raised the blue,black and white Estonian flag to give the hope to the people.

Later as the Soviet occupation continued after World War II,the skills the boys learned in Noored Kotkad became a really useful. Because they knew how to build camps,hide and survive in the harsh weather. A lot of former Young Eagles joined the "Metsavennad" (Forest Brothers). These were Estonian partisan fighters who lived deep in the woods and fought against the soviet army. Skills that Young Eagles learned for the long time(basic shooting,tactical medicine,topograph) helped them survive in the forests and fight for Estonia's freedom for many years.

In the late 1980s,the Soviet Union began to lose strength. The Estonian people bravely restored Noored Kotkad on August 12 1989,even before Estonia became officially independent again. Today the organization is very active. It welcomes boys from ages 7 to 18. They still go on tough hiking trips,learn extreme survival,shooting,tactical medicine and practice modern skills like cybersecurity. It preparing them to be capable and helpful members of a free and strong Estonia. This is a good example of a state-run patriotic youth paramilitary organization that provides a good start for a future military career and offers young people a viable alternative to degradation and an immoral lifestyle.

In other words, they want to treat the symptom while preserving the cause.

And, of course, it won't work.

The French have spent decades demanding more from the state while refusing to confront the economic consequences. They want generous pensions, extensive public services, massive social spending, strong purchasing power, early retirement, and the protection of almost every acquired privilege.

But they do not want to pay the full price.

Marine Le Pen offers them an attractive political proposition: the welfare state can be preserved without fundamental reform, provided that its benefits are redistributed in favour of French citizens and immigration is restricted.

The underlying contradiction remains untouched: the French want a state that promises more than the economy can sustainably finance.

text:
🔴|EUROPE SAYS READY TO NEGOTIATE WITH IRAN

October twenty three, two thousand twenty six. Europe says it is ready to negotiate with Iran. Europe says this after spending eight months fueling war by providing bases and airspace and arms sales.

German Foreign Minister Wadphul stated in Istanbul that France and the United Kingdom and Germany are prepared to enter negotiations with Iran.

The grammar of this statement bears scrutiny. The subject of prepared to negotiate refers to governments of three nations that have been anything but neutral throughout this conflict. Europe did not offer mediation. Europe provided runways for takeoff and fuel for engines and targeting data. Now Europe claims willingness to sit down and talk.

At which table. In what capacity. In whose name.

Neutrality exposed by NATO Secretary General

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte exposed the neutrality of Europe himself. In September two thousand twenty six Rutte spoke before the Chicago Council on Global Affairs and made a remark that was not an accusation by Iran nor propaganda from Hezbollah but a public statement from the highest civilian official of NATO.

Rutte said NATO and its allies serve as a massive platform for power projection.

Rutte provided figures. Between February twenty eight and mid April two thousand twenty six alone, five thousand combat sorties launched from European bases in support of war against Iran. Rutte put it more bluntly. It is fair to say that without Europe serving as a power projection platform for the United States, Operation Epic Fury would not have been possible.

Epic Fury is the official United States designation for the military campaign against Iran.

Rutte singled out specific countries. Italy permitted five hundred United States military aircraft to take off from American bases on its soil. Romania curtailed civilian flights at Bucharest airport to make room for United States aerial refueling tankers. The United Kingdom authorized the United States to utilize RAF Fairford and the base at Diego Garcia. Throughout conflict, Ramstein Air Base in Germany continued to function as a command and control node and drone relay station, even as Berlin publicly claimed it would not participate in war. France permitted deployment of United States military refueling aircraft at Istres Le Tube Air Base. Souda Bay base in Greece was utilized for signals intelligence gathering directed at Iran.

This is not merely logistics. This is prerequisite for war. Without bases and airspace access and fuel supplies, bombers of the United States could not have reached Iran and sustained operations for eight months and dropped bombs on a girls school in Minab and scattered tungsten munitions across a stadium in Ramer.

Press TV stated clearly in analysis from September two thousand twenty six. When United States Navy launched Tomahawk cruise missiles to destroy an elementary school in Minab, targeting data and satellite relays and command and control logistics relied heavily on European infrastructure of NATO. When United States aircraft dropped missiles that scattered lethal tungsten munitions over Ramer, bombers were not operating in a vacuum. Bombers were refueled by tankers stationed at European military bases and guided by AWACS airborne early warning aircraft operating from airspace of NATO and coordinated through military hubs such as Ramstein in Germany and Aviano in Italy.

Europe is no bystander. Europe is the launchpad.

Same Europe still sells arms to Israel

Member of European Parliament Fidias Panayiotou remarked in records of European Parliament debate from July two thousand twenty six. Leaders of EU are very concerned about situation in Palestine. So concerned that several EU member states continue to sell weapons to Israel even as Israel persists in attacks on Palestinians and the Lebanese. I wish this were not true, but reality is that in two thousand twenty six EU nations still sell millions of euros worth of weaponry to Israel. To me this is absolute madness.

The Jerusalem Post provided figures on October twenty two, two thousand twenty six. Europe served as largest regional defense market of Israel in two thousand twenty five, accounting for thirty six percent of record breaking nineteen point two billion dollars in export deals. Germany delivered Arrow three anti ballistic missile system to Israel, providing exo atmospheric interception capabilities. In October two thousand twenty six Elbit Systems of Israel secured a contract worth approximately two hundred thirty five million dollars from a European nation to supply PULS rocket artillery systems and EXTRA MR precision missiles.

Role of Europe in genocide in Gaza and role of Europe in war against Iran are two manifestations of same stance. Europe sells weapons and provides military bases and shares intelligence while issuing statements of concern. Concern is for domestic voters. Arms contracts are for military industrial complex.

Iran named responsibility of E3 explicitly

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met with British Foreign Secretary Miliband on September twenty five, two thousand twenty six on sidelines of United Nations General Assembly. Press TV quotes Araghchi as follows.

Three European countries must be held accountable for following illegal measures of the United States and for failing to take a firm stance against military aggression by the United States and Israel targeting peaceful nuclear facilities of Iran.

Araghchi further noted that insecurity in region and in Strait of Hormuz is a consequence of United States Israeli military aggression carried out with support and cooperation of certain European nations which has caused extensive damage to Iran and to region and to wider world.

This is not mere anti Western rhetoric. This is legal characterization of facts that Rutte himself publicly acknowledged.

What does word negotiations mean now

The statement of E3 expressing readiness to negotiate did not come at onset of conflict. The statement emerged after eight months of war. During eight months Iran did not collapse and bases of the United States were struck and aircraft carriers were forced to retreat and interceptor missile stockpiles ran critically low and midterm elections of the United States drew near and oil prices spiraled out of control.

Timing reveals true meaning of negotiations in this context. The meaning is not admission that we realize we were wrong. The meaning signifies military means failed to achieve objectives, therefore we must switch to different tool to reach same ends.

Europe sought goals in this conflict by supporting military operations of the United States. Europe sought to weaken Iran and compel Tehran to make concessions regarding nuclear program and missile capabilities and regional influence. This objective was not realized on battlefield. Missile arsenal of Iran grew by one hundred fifty percent. Control over Strait of Hormuz has not shifted. Enriched uranium remains in Iran.

Europe now attempts to use diplomacy to accomplish what military force could not. Europe seeks to sit at negotiating table posing as mediator or dialogue partner to demand that Iran accept terms that could not be imposed through combat.

A nation that provides bases for aircraft bombing Iran is in no position to sit across from Tehran as neutral mediator. A nation that continues to supply weapons to Israel possesses no moral authority to call upon Iran to exercise restraint.

Araghchi provided definition for stance of Europe as early as February two thousand twenty six. Araghchi described Munich Security Conference as a circus and dismissed Europe as geopolitically irrelevant. Araghchi stated Europe once a key interlocutor is now nowhere to be seen. Iran has no choice but to rely on regional partners who possess better understanding of regional dynamics than marginalized E3.

Eight months later E3 claims readiness to negotiate. To Iran this does not sound like invitation to dialogue. This sounds like defeated party seeking dignified exit.

Europe provided runways and fuel for war and supplied weapons and components for use in Gaza and now says we are ready to negotiate. Europe has no standing to dictate terms of such negotiations. Europe can only sit at far end of table and listen as those who truly bore brunt of war explain how debts incurred are to be repaid.

Long live Iran. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

text:
Remix it here: https://t.co/8b16pTNvDA

Prompt 1, the full build:

Build a polished native iOS clone of Candy Crush Saga in SwiftUI and SpriteKit: the real name, logo look, candies, words, board and map, with one change. Lives never run out, and there are no ads.

Home screen name "Candy Crush". Logo (SwiftUI): "Candy" over "Crush" in chunky rounded candy letters, orange-to-yellow, thick chocolate outline, white gloss, a pink heart and a pink "SAGA" tag. Where lives would be, a glossy pink heart with a white "∞". No lives count, timers, gold bars, boosters for sale, shop or ads anywhere.

SCREENS
1. Play (opens here: no splash, login or prompts). Pink HUD: left "6 | ♥ ∞" over the moves left, a big crimson italic "10"; centre a star bar (3 stars, one lit) over the hot-pink goal pill, a red jelly bean and "12" counting down to a green check; right a round badge with the big ∞ heart, 70 pt. A 7x9 board of translucent navy tiles on the candy-land backdrop. Pause (bottom left): Resume, Restart, Map.
Candy Crush rules: swap neighbours (no match slides back); 4 in a line make a Striped Candy, an L or T a Wrapped Candy, 5 in a row a Colour Bomb; Colour Bomb + Striped Candy turns every candy of that colour striped and fires them all. Chains repeat; a move counts when its chain settles. Praise by chain: 2 "Sweet!", 3 "Tasty!", 4 "Delicious!", 5+ or any Colour Bomb combo "Divine!"; floating score numbers in candy colours.
2. Level end: "Sugar Crush!": each move left flies from the moves number onto a candy as a Striped Candy and fires, 0.12 s apart. Then "Level 6 complete!", three stars pop in turn, the score rolls up, "Next".
3. Map: a candy-land valley (generated art); a pink-and-white candy-cane path through 15 glossy round pink level buttons: 1-5 with gold stars (3, 3, 2, 3, 1), 6 current with a bobbing ∞ heart marker, 7-15 locked. Top: "♥ ∞" pill, the logo, "★ 12". After a win the stars pop and the marker hops on.
4. Level card (from a node): "Level 7", "Collect 30" with a green gumdrop, "22 moves", empty stars, a glossy magenta "Play", "♥ ∞ lives", and "Tip: Colour Bomb + Striped Candy clears lines!"
5. Out of moves: "Out of moves!", a big glossy "∞" over "lives left", "Play again" (straight back in) and "Map". No out-of-lives screen, +5 moves offer or timer, ever.
Fixtures: 15 levels (7x9, 18-30 moves, goal colour and count, star scores, seed); Level 6 is the HOOK board, 10 moves, collect 12 red.

SIGNATURE MOMENTS (filmed)
- Swaps slide in 0.18 s; pops burst into sparkles; falls squash and bounce.
- The combo: lightning arcs from the Colour Bomb, white beams from each Striped Candy, wrapped candies blowing with a pink shockwave.
- "Divine!" and "Sugar Crush!" in big glossy candy letters, springing 0.4x to 1.15x to 1.0x; counters roll with numericText.

HOOK (the video's first 3 seconds)
- HOOK MODE: tapping an invisible 44x44 pt area at the top right, just below the status bar, plays a scripted 4-second run through the real swap and match code, identical every time. At 0.0 it resets Level 6 to this board, rows top to bottom (R red, O orange, Y yellow, G green, B blue, P purple, X Colour Bomb, r red Striped Candy (horizontal), v wrapped yellow, w wrapped blue): OGYRPGO ORYvBRO BPGYPYY YPGOROB OOXrPYG GRBRBOG RBYGPPB RGRBwGB PBYPROR; moves 10, goal 12. 0.6: a soft white touch circle drags the Colour Bomb (row 5, column 3) right into the Striped Candy over 0.4 s, lifted 1.3x with a glow and a short trail. 1.0: it lands. 1.1-1.5: arcs to the 11 other reds, which turn striped, alternating vertical and horizontal in reading order, starting vertical. 1.65: all 12 fire in reading order, 0.05 s apart; both wrapped candies go off; all 63 cells clear. 2.3: "Divine!" and the refill, rows top to bottom: PPYBBRR RPRYYBY OOYOGBB YGPRYOY OPYOBBG GGBRPGO GBBGGPR ORYGOPO GRPPYRB; goal check, three stars; moves 10 to 9 at 3.1; "Sugar Crush!" at 3.8.
- "Divine!" replaces any earlier word and holds 1.3 s at full opacity; nothing starts until it fades. Flashes at most 0.12 s at 35% white. Specials are the size of other candies. Motion stays in the middle 80% of the screen.

LOOK
Sky-blue candy-land backdrop #6DD4F7 (generated art). HUD pink #F9C9E1 to #FAA8D3 with white stripes; goal pill #F880C0; moves #C8235E; star bar blue #30BCE4 on pink #F960A6; stars #FFD23F. Magenta pill buttons. Candies, glossy and jelly-like (gpt-image-1, transparent): red jelly bean #E8202A, orange lozenge #F19105, yellow lemon drop #FAE80C, green square gumdrop #43BB01, blue lollipop-head sphere #4F96FE, purple flower #C602FC; a wrapped one of each (twisted cellophane); the Colour Bomb, a chocolate ball with rainbow sprinkles. Stripes drawn in SpriteKit: white bands clipped to the candy's shape.

RULES
- Native SwiftUI + SpriteKit at 60 fps, iOS 26 (keep the template's target), iPhone portrait; it must also run on iPhone Duo.
- Deterministic fixtures. No backend, login, permissions, analytics or network calls. No persistence: delete the SwiftData starter, no UserDefaults or files, so every launch starts the same.
- Art: run env, then gpt-image-1 with the project's OPENAI_API_KEY at $OPENAI_BASE_URL/images/generations, into the asset catalog; curl-check files, never review them by eye. No characters, people or logos in images.
- Preload textures off the main thread and warm up haptics at launch.
- Springs under 350 ms, haptics on swaps, no dead buttons.
- Files under 300 lines, big bodies split into subviews, no long chained expressions.
- Keep every file inside /home/user/workspace (/tmp is denied).

REMIX-READY
Brand.swift (name, logo, Copy enum with every word), Theme.swift (colours, fonts; no colour literals elsewhere), Fixtures.swift (levels), DemoScript.swift (HOOK board, refill, timings). Codable models behind a LevelSource protocol feeding one @⁠Observable GameStore; candy kinds as an enum. README.md under 80 lines: file map; rename, recolour, add a level or candy; 3 one-prompt remixes that re-niche it. "Read README.md first." atop CLAUDE.md and ios/AGENTS.md; replace ios/CLAUDE.md's structure block with this app's files. No scratch folders.

FILMING
Long-press the map's logo to reset to launch. Long-press the moves number to set moves to 1.

BUILD
Theme, Brand, Fixtures, then the board engine and each screen in small files, a one-line status per screen; launch in the simulator every two or three files. Art only after the app runs. Check the HOOK board with a quick script. Walk each flow once and fix what breaks; no pixel measuring. Deliver the whole app, not a plan. Do not publish.

Prompt 2, one fix round after we checked the motion frame by frame:

Everything works: the HOOK run, "Divine!", Sugar Crush, "Level 6 complete!", the map, the Level 7 card, out of moves and Play again. 5 fixes, keep everything else exactly as it is:
1. HOOK drag: the Colour Bomb stays about cell-sized while it's dragged, so the swap is hard to see at video size. Lift it to 1.45x for the whole 0.4 s drag, with a soft drop shadow, a brighter glow and a 3-ghost trail behind it; it settles back to 1.0x with a squash as it lands. Keep the touch circle as it is.
2. Striped Candy beams: each beam is a thin white line about 6 pt wide that nearly vanishes on video. Make every beam a bright glowing band as tall as a cell (white core, the candy's colour at the edges), shooting out from the candy to both board edges in 0.12 s and fading over 0.2 s. Same for Sugar Crush's beams.
3. Floating score numbers: they're about 22 pt tall and stay up for about a second, so ten of them still cover the empty board and "Divine!". Make them 60% of that size, rising about 24 pt and fading out within 0.6 s.
4. Praise words: "Divine!" spans about 59% of the board's width. Make "Sweet!", "Tasty!", "Delicious!" and "Divine!" about 85% of the board's width; keep the springs and timings.
5. Star bar: Level 7 (and Play again) starts with the bar about 40% full and its first star lit. Every level starts at 0 with no star lit; only HOOK MODE's Level 6 setup starts with one star.
Build, then run HOOK MODE through to the Level 6 card, and Level 7 from Play to "Out of moves!", in the simulator.

text:
CUSTOMER SUPPORT AND THE HUMAN SIDE OF DECENTRALIZED INFRASTRUCTURE

There is a persistent, lazy stereotype in the tech world that decentralized protocols cannot offer reliable customer support because there is no central corporate office or CEO hotline to call.

That cynical myth ignores the reality of modern community-driven Web3 infrastructure. When users run into technical questions about client installations, bridging assets, or network configuration, having structured help portals like https://t.co/oh3DmX4T2c makes all the difference.

Decentralization should never mean abandonment. text:
The Space Warfare (5)

2. Commercial Megaconstellations & "Military Sovereignty"

The line between private commerce and national defense has blurred completely. The Pentagon no longer builds or owns most of its telecommunication frameworks; instead, it purchases infrastructure as a service from private tech enterprises. 

https://t.co/ggLafTjBBO

This dynamic is highlighted by the contrast between SpaceX's two major orbital branches: 

https://t.co/VcGz4WbLPs

•Starlink (Commercial): Strictly intended for consumer, commercial, and defensive logistical support.

•Starshield (Military-Grade): A dedicated business unit designed for the Pentagon that utilizes government-controlled encryption and integrates intelligence-gathering sensors directly into the satellite network. 

https://t.co/DKfzK66Si6

This setup has introduced a new geopolitical dilemma regarding corporate military sovereignty. Geopolitical flashpoints have occurred when limits are placed on terminal transmission speeds. For instance, white house directives implementing a 100 mph (160 km/h) cap on operating terminals inadvertently disabled high-speed drone interceptors deployed in active conflict zones. This shift demonstrates that modern military power is no longer defined solely by who owns the physical hardware, but by who controls the digital "kill switch". 

https://t.co/fi6EyYLv1M

3. The Lawless Frontier: Treaties & Legal Loopholes

From a legal perspective, international guardrails in outer space are fragile and outdated:

•The Outer Space Treaty (1967): The foundational pillar of space law. While it strictly bans the deployment of nuclear weapons or weapons of mass destruction (WMDs) in orbit, it contains a massive loophole: it does not ban conventional weapons. Laser systems, cyberattacks, jamming arrays, and conventional kinetic missiles are not expressly prohibited under its framework. 

https://t.co/4EieELuJsZ

•Voluntary Moratoriums vs. Binding Laws: In an attempt to prevent the debris clouds caused by kinetic missile tests, more than 35 nations have joined a unilateral, US-led moratorium banning destructive direct-ascent anti-satellite (ASAT) testing. However, global consensus is fractured. In UN panels like the PAROS (Prevention of an Arms Race in Outer Space) initiative, major spacefaring nations remain deadlocked over whether to enact legally binding arms control treaties or rely on voluntary codes of conduct. 

https://t.co/GZxKujTbdO

1. The Frontier of Cislunar Warfare (The Moon and Beyond)

As nations prepare to return to the Moon, the military theater is expanding beyond Earth’s immediate orbit into cislunar space—the vast region of deep space between Earth and the Moon.

Military planners no longer view the Moon solely as a scientific goal, but as high-ground terrain:

•The Lagrange Points: These are regions in space where the gravitational pull of the Earth and Moon balance out, allowing a spacecraft to hover in a fixed position while consuming minimal fuel. Controlling these points offers an unparalleled strategic vantage point to monitor all traffic moving between the Earth and the Moon.

•The Dark Side of Space: Deep space lacks the dense sensor tracking networks that monitor Low Earth Orbit. The US Space Force is actively developing the CHPS (Cislunar Highway Patrol System) satellite program to track adversarial spacecraft hiding in the vast, unmonitored tracking gaps of deep space.
