Little Office of the Blessed Virgin Mary

FRIDAY

Morning Prayer
God, come to my assistance.
- Lord, make haste to help me

Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit
as it was in the beginning, is now, and will be forever.  Amen.

Virgin of virgins,
I choose you today
as my sovereign, my queen, my empress,
and I declare myself, as I am in fact,
your servant and your slave.
I invoke your royal name of Mary,
that is, sovereign Lady,
and beg of you with all my heart
to admit me into the privileged circle¡
of your family
as one of your servants,
to do your will
as a humble slave and a loving child.
As a sign of your acceptance
engrave on my heart
with the fire of your love,
not the brand of an unwilling slave,
but those two gracious words of the angel:
Ave Maria.
As long as I draw breath
may your burning love ensure
that I bear these words
in my heart and in my memory,
and that until my dying breath
my will may be always on fire
with my great desire to serve you,
my sovereign and my queen,
glorious in your majesty.
Though I am in every way unworthy
of so honorable a title,
I resolve sincerely to be your slave,
to serve you wholeheartedly,
to protect your name,
and that of your Son,
against every insult,
as far as it may rest with me,
and never to allow anyone in my charge
to offend your Son in any way.
By your tender love for your Son,
by the glories you have received
from the Most Holy Trinity,
do not reject me from your service
but as my sovereign and my queen
preside over all my actions,
command whatever you will,
direct all my work,
remedy all its defects.
During my whole life
rule over me
as your servant and slave.
At the hour of my death,
as I hope for
at the end of my loving servitude
among the privileged members of your family,
receive my soul and escort it
into the presence of God.

St Bartolome de Los Rios(1580-1652)

PSALMODY

Ant.1 My soul clings to you, Lord Jesus Christ.

Psalm 51
O God, have mercy on me
Your inmost being must be renewed, and you must put on the new man. (Eph 4:23-24)
Have mercy on me, God, in your kindness.
In your compassion blot out my offense.
O wash me more and more from my guilt
and cleanse me from my sin.
My offenses truly I know them;
my sin is always before me
Against you, you alone, have I sinned;
what is evil in your sight I have done.
That you may be justified when you give sentence
and be without reproach when you judge,
O see, in guilt I was born,
a sinner was I conceived.
Indeed you love truth in the heart;
then in the secret of my heart teach me wisdom.
O purify me, then I shall be clean;
O wash me, I shall be whiter than snow.
Make me hear rejoicing and gladness,
that the bones you have crushed may thrill.
From my sins turn away your face
and blot out all my guilt.
A pure heart create for me, O God,
put a steadfast spirit within me.
Do not cast me away from your presence,
nor deprive me of your holy spirit.
Give me again the joy of your help;
with a spirit of fervor sustain me,
that I may teach transgressors your ways
and sinners may return to you.
O rescue me, God, my helper,
and my tongue shall ring out your goodness.
O Lord, open my lips
and my mouth shall declare your praise.
For in sacrifice you take no delight,
burnt offering from me you would refuse,
my sacrifice, a contrite spirit,
a humbled, contrite heart you will not spurn.
In your goodness, show favor to Zion:
rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you will be pleased with lawful sacrifice,
(burnt offerings wholly consumed),
then you will be offered young bulls on your altar.

text:
Let’s deal with Hellebuyck first. This trade has to sting to some degree for the Carolina Hurricanes, seeing him traded within the Metro after the reigning Stanley Cup champions felt they had a fair offer to the Winnipeg Jets on the table for a number of months. The Canes remained interested right up to the end.
So as far as fallout goes, does Canes general manager Eric Tulsky now pivot and look elsewhere for a goalie upgrade? I think he viewed Hellebuyck as a unique opportunity — a top-five goalie in the world who rarely is available. There won’t be a goalie of that caliber on the market again this season, one wouldn’t think. And I mean, they won a Cup in June with the guy they have in net now. But man, Hellebuyck in Carolina would have been deadly.
The Buffalo Sabres had tried as well, especially around the draft in June. The Utah Mammoth dabbled but never that seriously, I don’t think. And why would the Jets want Hellebuyck in their own division? Winnipeg made a very good deal with New Jersey given the circumstances.
In the end, the Devils swoop in and get the Team USA goalie who stole the gold medal in February.

@PierreVLeBrun @TheAthleticNHL @NHLJets @NJDevils

text:
I haven't seen Chaotic post anything in favor of Russia so I don't that is fair. Regarding E.M.'s statement my own thoughts are that I think the same thing could be said for Russia and the corruption of its elites. Part of the reason their full-scale invasion failed in 2022 was massive corruption and the siphoning off of wealth—and even fuel needed for the invasion. Also, Putin rewards people supporting the war and their government, for example, gave seized Google money to an Oligarch to support the war with his TV channel.

Related to the incentive differences argument, I recall monitoring Russian and Ukrainian channels in 2022. In the first days of the war, the Russians arrogantly extended beyond their supply lines, rushing for major Ukrainian cities while thinking they had it in the bag because the necessary people had been bought off and that there would be little to no resistance. The problem for them was that many ordinary Ukrainians said “fuck that” and fought back. If the people hadn’t stood up (civilians, national guard, etc.) and fought, it would have likely been over. I watched ordinary Ukrainian citizens pick up AKs and Molotovs and fight Russian armored vehicles as the Russians pressed close to Kyiv. That was a vote by the people and a reflection of what their will and incentives were.

Zelensky staying in Ukraine when Biden offered him an easy way out during the early days of the invasion—when the Russians were pushing toward Kyiv—was a huge testament to his character. He could have easily left the country, moved to South Florida, and lived a nice, easy life in a much better climate with his family in exile. Instead, he chose to fight to keep Ukraine independent. I don't think he thought in the early days that "gee, I should stay because we'll make billions off this war."

text:
AI keeps pulling back. What is the market pricing in?

U.S. tech stocks came under renewed pressure last night. The Nasdaq fell 2.6%, $NVDA dropped 4.4%, and $MU, SK Hynix and $SNDK fell 6.26%, 8.07% and 8.51%, respectively. Optical communications stocks sold off as well. Meanwhile, $META, which had jumped nearly 7% after hours the previous day, ended the session down almost 7%.

Right now, the market is selling AI, money is moving into bonds, and oil is rising. These three things are happening at the same time, but they are being driven by different forces.

My view is simple: this AI pullback is pricing in tighter funding conditions, not clear evidence of weakening demand.

This is a personal record of my thoughts and learning, not investment advice.
1. Several unusual signals in this pullback
If demand were truly deteriorating, we would expect to see order cancellations and lower guidance. What we have seen over the past two days points in the opposite direction.

TSMC's third-quarter results and fourth-quarter guidance both beat expectations. Western Digital reported 55% revenue growth last night, issued a midpoint forecast well above market expectations, and raised its quarterly dividend by 17%. Yet its shares still fell 6.54% after hours.

Earnings are being revised upward while stock prices are falling. What is changing is the valuation multiple. That is the first clue about the nature of this correction.

The second clue is the difference in drawdowns. Equipment, optical communications and memory have been hit hardest, while traditional software stocks have held up relatively better. The former depend directly on capital spending. The latter are more closely tied to end demand for services.

The pattern of declines effectively gives us a map of capital expenditure sensitivity. That is not what a typical demand downturn would necessarily look like.

The sector has fallen 16% since October 5 and is down more than 20% from its June high. Memory stocks are down more than 40% from their peaks, yet earnings estimates have not followed prices lower.

The third clue is interest rates. The 10-year Treasury yield fell below 5%, with some maturities dropping around 20 basis points in a single session. The market's fully priced-in timing for a rate hike shifted from December to January next year. Valuation compression usually comes with rising long-term yields. This time, long-term yields are moving lower, so the most direct variable on the discount-rate side has not deteriorated.

The fourth clue is market breadth. Equal-weighted S&P 500 performance relative to the cap-weighted index had its strongest day since July 2024. Consumer staples, healthcare and utilities led the market. The weakness was concentrated in a relatively small group of long-duration assets.

Meta is being sold for spending more. Other companies with stronger cash flow are being sold even when they spend less. The market is not simply targeting spending direction. It is repricing valuations that depend on distant future expectations.
2. Why credit markets moved first
Meta has committed to roughly $825 billion in future spending, up from around $700 billion disclosed in July.

That includes $355.7 billion in operating and finance lease obligations not recorded on the balance sheet, with maturities extending to 2036, as well as $454.5 billion in non-cancellable contracts, mainly for third-party cloud computing, data center power and Reality Labs hardware.

Annual capital expenditure guidance tells us how much a company expects to spend this year. The $825 billion figure tells us how much it has already committed to spending in the future. One is a flow. The other is a stock of obligations.

At this year's projected spending pace of $135 billion to $145 billion, $825 billion is equivalent to roughly six years of spending. The accounting categories are not perfectly comparable, but the scale shows how much future expenditure has already been locked in.

The clearest contrast came from Meta's stock price. It initially jumped nearly 7% after Wednesday's close, then finished Thursday down around 7%. There was no equivalent wave of new fundamental information in between. What changed was the price of credit.

Credit markets saw this risk first. Meta's five-year CDS spread rose 8.9 basis points intraday to 119.3 basis points, a record high for the contract, while its corporate bond spreads widened.

On the same day, the yield on CoreWeave's bonds due in 2030 moved back above 15%, while its CDS remained above 1,000 basis points. On a risk-neutral basis, that implied a cumulative five-year default probability of roughly 60%.

A CDS spread is the cost of buying insurance against a company's debt defaulting. Buyers of that protection are less concerned with next quarter's revenue growth than with whether principal and interest will be paid on time. Their focus is almost the opposite of the stock market's.

Meta's 119 basis points and CoreWeave's 1,000-plus basis points are not comparable in absolute terms. What matters is the direction and speed of the move. Spending commitments have risen by $125 billion in three months, while CDS spreads have hit a record. From the bond market's perspective, the company is committing capital faster than it is generating cash.

Equity and credit investors are looking at two different sets of numbers. Equity investors focus on the income statement: how much a company earns this quarter and what it expects next quarter. Credit investors focus on future obligations: how much must be paid over the coming years and where the money will come from.

When those two views begin to diverge, credit markets can start to influence valuation more than earnings do.

Meta's reaction has been more severe than that of some peers for structural reasons. Microsoft, Amazon and Google sell computing capacity to customers. Their cloud revenue can help absorb data center investment, and some of the risk is borne by customers renting that capacity.

Meta does not sell computing capacity externally on the same scale. The cost of overbuilding therefore remains more directly on its own books. The same increase in capital expenditure can have a greater impact on its credit profile.

The choice of financing also says something about the current cost of capital. Meta's announcement of non-voting Class C shares uses equity rather than debt. The cost is dilution, but it avoids interest payments.

Choosing equity instead of debt while free cash flow is under pressure is itself a signal that borrowing costs matter.
3. Demand, delivery and funding are moving at different speeds
Recent developments can be divided into three separate tracks.

First, demand remains strong.

At GTC, Jensen Huang said demand for new cloud capacity was far beyond expectations. But he also noted that a lack of capital supply was constraining industry growth.

Those hearing the demand side focus on strong business conditions. Those looking at financing hear a warning about bottlenecks.

Cloud providers have generally been accelerating growth. Market expectations for Microsoft Azure are around 46% to 47%, while AWS growth expectations have moved from roughly 37% toward 41% to 42%. These are signals from orders and contracted demand.

The key question is how concentrated that demand remains.

Amazon began disclosing annualized revenue run rate from AI-related products two quarters ago. The figures cited in the market have risen from $15 billion to $25 billion, with expectations of $40 billion this quarter.

The slope matters more than the absolute number. If the largest customers slow down in the third quarter but Amazon's AI revenue run rate continues accelerating, it could suggest demand is spreading from a handful of model developers to a broader base of enterprises.

If Amazon's growth slope also slows, it would suggest that computing demand still relies heavily on a small number of major AI customers.

That distinction determines how broadly we can apply the statement that demand remains strong.

Second, delivery is slowing.

Lam Research issued guidance below expectations and indicated that results could have been higher without supply constraints.

When equipment cannot be delivered, orders cannot turn into recognized revenue.

Nscale offers another example. Data center construction delays, equipment problems and power constraints have raised questions about its $30 billion valuation target.

Traditional infrastructure projects can take three years to build, while the market often expects data centers to become operational within six months.

Delays do not necessarily destroy demand. They change when revenue can be recognized. Valuations are sensitive to timing. The same five-year contract is worth less in present-value terms if revenue arrives a year later.

This may be one of the least discussed but most damaging factors for long-duration valuations.

Third, funding is getting tighter.

AI-related debt financing reached $466 billion in the first half of the year, 4.6 times the level of the same period last year. Monthly issuance peaked at $113 billion in June before falling to $23 billion in September, an approximately 80% decline.

The financing window is narrowing just as delivery schedules are being pushed back. That combination increases refinancing pressure for newer cloud infrastructure companies.

CoreWeave's earliest publicly issued bonds mature in 2030, so the pressure from 2026 through 2029 is more concentrated in project loans and equipment financing than in publicly traded bond maturities.
4. The bigger picture
Demand is accelerating, delivery is slowing, and funding is becoming more expensive. Together, these forces are putting pressure on valuation multiples.

There is another important difference: speed.

Demand is updated quarterly, one earnings report at a time. Delivery unfolds over years, as data centers are built and brought online. Funding costs can change daily, with credit spreads moving by double-digit basis points in a single session.

When these variables move at different speeds, prices tend to reflect the fastest-moving one first.

That is why funding-related news is currently overpowering demand-related news. The narrative can shift back toward earnings growth once delivery and revenue catch up.

A sharp selloff by itself does not tell us where the industry is headed. It tells us which variable the market is repricing most urgently.

The longer-term question is return on capital.

Industry success and shareholder returns are not the same thing. Excess returns depend on how much capital must be invested to generate profits. When too much money enters a sector, capital costs and competition can absorb much of the value created.

For AI, the question is whether an industry that succeeds technologically can still deliver attractive returns after accounting for the enormous cost of building it.

Goldman Sachs has modeled a scenario in which AI infrastructure capital expenditure exceeds $3.5 trillion by 2030. To cover capital expenditure, financing costs and a 12% return on investment, data center owners would need to generate a cumulative $8.5 trillion in revenue. Estimated revenue capacity from enterprise and consumer demand is around $3.6 trillion, leaving a gap of nearly $5 trillion.

The assumptions behind that model can certainly be debated. But the underlying question deserves attention: How much revenue and profit can the market ultimately generate from all this investment?

History also offers perspective.

In March 2020, the S&P 500 fell roughly 34% from peak to trough before recovering within months. In 2022, the Nasdaq fell more than 30%. Many investors thought the technology era was over, yet the index eventually went on to reach new highs.

History does not guarantee the same outcome this time. It does show that stock prices and underlying industry demand can move in very different directions.

Demand for memory, networking and power does not disappear simply because stocks fall sharply on a given day. The answer on the demand side is not found in price action alone. It must be confirmed through delivery schedules and financial results.

Here are the three things I will be watching next.

First, the relationship between the 10-year Treasury yield and investment-grade and high-yield credit spreads. If Treasury yields fall while credit spreads widen, it signals that investors are seeking safety while becoming more concerned about credit risk. That combination is particularly unfavorable for companies with heavy capital expenditure requirements.

Second, cloud growth and 2027 capital expenditure guidance from Google, Microsoft and Amazon next week, along with the trajectory of Amazon's AI revenue run rate. These will provide some of the clearest evidence of whether AI demand is broadening or slowing.

Third, delivery schedules and refinancing costs for newer cloud infrastructure projects. Whether CoreWeave's bond yields can fall below 12% may tell us more about its financing conditions than its stock price alone.

The chain to watch is straightforward:

Higher spending commitments → wider credit spreads → higher financing costs for new projects → delayed delivery → later revenue recognition → valuation compression.

Over the past year, AI expansion was driven primarily by demand. Over the next phase, the cost of capital may have a much bigger say.

One final thought I keep coming back to:

Building wealth in the market is difficult. If it were easy, everyone would succeed. Everyone wants returns, but far fewer are willing to endure the volatility, uncertainty and patience required to earn them.

Conviction alone is not enough. We still need to manage risk, understand what we own and recognize when the fundamentals genuinely change.

But we should not let a few difficult weeks in the market distract us from the investment opportunities that may emerge over the next decade.

Think in decades, not days.

This is a personal record of my thoughts and learning, not investment advice.

text:
Some thoughts on Colossal Biosciences CEO Ben Lamm's new spinout WARHOUND:

1) The basic pipeline is that they're going to SCNT a few of the best elite military, police, and first-responder dogs. Think Dolly the Sheep. Here's it's mainly Belgian Malinois, German Shepherd, or a mix.

2) This is downstream of Colossal's acquisition of ViaGen Pets, a startup that offered to clone your pet for $50k. I don't think that market was every going to be big enough. But ViaGen probably gives them an in house SCNT tech for dogs that's better than current state-of-the-art. For example, published SCNT success rates are low, maybe 2-10%. If they can routinely get 10% live birth per transfer, then this can work reasonably well, since you can transfer 10-20 embryos per surrogate.

3) The genetic enhancements are unnecessary. If you have a great working dog, it's not going to have recessive hip dysplasia or cancer risk. What would you change about Secretariat? If you've got canine MJ, are you really trying to make the Monstars? 

The same applies to healthy adult humans -- there is virtually no genetic edit that I could make that would majorly enhance your child. Most of the traits you care about are highly polygeneic.

4) This is going to be the ultimate nature vs nuture test for behavior and cognition. If you make 100s of genetic twins (a better term than clones), do they have the same trainability, temperament, and instincts? How much variation from developmental noise is there really? 

5) These dogs are going to be like Monsanto seeds - only available for purchase from the source. You won't be able to breed them because they're not inbred, and so any F2 is going to risk picking up undesirable recessives.

6) Picture below is a myostatin mutant, perhaps the most striking single mutation one could engineer. It is common in racing dogs, but not likely to be relevant for working dogs.

text:
3/4 — THE MOAT IS IN THE PROCESS, THE EQUIPMENT AND THE TRACK RECORD

#SFC Environmental Technologies’ strongest differentiator is not simply that it builds sewage-treatment plants. It has its own C-Tech process technology, plus manufacturing capabilities for key equipment used in treatment systems.

Three tangible advantages:

1. C-Tech: a proven installed base

Its sequencing batch reactor (SBR) technology treats sewage through a timed cycle of biological treatment and settling in the same reactor. As of July 2026, SFC reported 728 commissioned installations, treating around 17,511 million litres of wastewater per day, and claimed over 80% of India’s SBR technology market.

For a new competitor, replicating the process is only part of the challenge: it must also establish a credible track record of installations and reliable plant performance.

2. Critical equipment made in-house

SFC manufactures components such as decanters, diffusers and turbo blowers used in wastewater-treatment systems. This can improve integration between process design and equipment, reduce dependence on external suppliers and support execution.

3. Beyond wastewater: OREX and recycling technologies

Its proprietary OREX technology separates biodegradable organic matter from inorganic material and lignocellulosic fibres in mixed municipal waste. In wastewater recycling, SFC also offers ultrafiltration, closed-circuit reverse osmosis and membrane bioreactor solutions, supported by a supply arrangement with DuPont for selected components.

The investor test: These capabilities create a plausible technology-and-execution moat—but the real proof is repeat orders, successful project commissioning, dependable operating performance and cash generation. Market-share claims alone do not establish pricing power or patent protection.

Founded in 2005, SFC Environmental Technologies claims over 80% of India’s SBR wastewater-treatment technology market. It has commissioned 728 wastewater-treatment installations and is expanding across recycling, solid waste and compressed biogas.

The business has a specialised technology portfolio and a sizeable order book. But the IPO has a crucial distinction: ₹150 Cr is fresh capital, while ₹517.53 Cr is an OFS.

text:
🎮 Cyberpunk 2077 might be one of the greatest redemption stories in gaming history. And a glimpse into the FUTURE of gaming.

I believe Cyberpunk 2077 has become one of the greatest gaming experiences of this generation, possibly of ALL TIME.

And what makes that incredible is where it started.

When Cyberpunk launched, it was a disaster. Broken promises, technical problems, disappointed fans, and a reputation that seemed impossible to recover from.

For many games, that would’ve been the end.

🔥 But Cyberpunk became something far greater than its launch.

Through years of improvements and Phantom Liberty, CD Projekt Red demonstrated something I wish more of the industry understood:

❤️ Genuine love, passion, and commitment can turn failure into something extraordinary.

But Cyberpunk accomplished something even more significant.

It didn’t just redeem a video game. It created a WORLD that feels genuinely ALIVE.

Night City isn’t simply a map filled with missions. It’s a place with its own culture, history, politics, music, fashion, and moral complexities.

Every district has an identity. Every character feels like they’re surviving in a world that existed before you arrived and will continue long after you’re gone.

And then came Cyberpunk: Edgerunners. 🥹

That anime did something remarkable.

Rather than adapting the game’s story, it expanded the emotional reality of Night City.

Through David, Lucy, Rebecca, and the crew, we experienced the SAME world through completely different lives.

Suddenly, familiar locations carried emotional weight. Songs took on new meanings. The city’s beauty and tragedy became more personal.

You weren’t just watching an anime connected to a game. You were experiencing another LIFE within the same universe.

And THAT is where Cyberpunk offers a glimpse into the future of entertainment. 🚀

Think about Ready Player One.

The idea of entering a digital world so immersive and emotionally meaningful that it begins to feel like another life.

We’re not there technologically, but Cyberpunk has taken a step toward that vision.

Not through VR or photorealistic graphics alone.

✨ Through WORLD-BUILDING and emotional investment.

You can spend hundreds of hours in Night City and still feel like thousands of other stories are unfolding around you.

Edgerunners reinforces that feeling because it PROVES those stories exist.

V isn’t the center of the Cyberpunk universe.

Neither is David Martinez.

🌃 NIGHT CITY ITSELF IS THE MAIN CHARACTER.

That’s what separates a great game from an extraordinary fictional universe.

When a world becomes bigger than any single protagonist, the storytelling possibilities become limitless.

Imagine a future where games, animation, music, and interactive experiences become interconnected. Where you’re not simply consuming stories, but experiencing different lives within the SAME living universe.

Cyberpunk demonstrated how powerful that foundation can be.

And perhaps the most beautiful part is the redemption itself.

💫 Your beginning does NOT have to define your legacy.

A disastrous launch didn’t erase the incredible vision behind the project.

The developers kept building. The artists kept creating. The storytellers kept expanding the universe.

What was once considered one of gaming’s biggest disappointments became one of its greatest achievements.

❤️ That’s the difference between making a PRODUCT and creating something you genuinely LOVE.

Cyberpunk 2077 didn’t just show us that a broken game can be fixed.

It showed us what passion, perseverance, and artistic vision can accomplish when creators refuse to abandon something they believe in.

And for me, its greatest achievement isn’t simply becoming an incredible game.

It’s making me feel like Night City is somewhere I’ve actually LIVED.

That’s the future of gaming I want to see.

Not just playing another game.

🌆 LIVING ANOTHER LIFE.

Wake up, Samurai. We’ve got a world to build.
#Cyberpunk2077 #Edgerunners2

text:
KEN ATCHITY DIES AT 82

STORY MERCHANT LEGACY LIVES ON

Dr. Kenneth J. Atchity (January 16, 1944 – October 19, 2026)

Who was Dr. Ken Atchity?

Story Merchant Ken Atchity, a writer, editor, professor, producer, and literary manager, spent his life in the world of stories. He wrote over 20 books, produced more than 30 films, and made hundreds of Hollywood and traditional deals for his clients.

Atchity (Yale Ph.D.) was formerly a Fulbright-honored professor of comparative literature, turned literary manager and producer. His films included: the mega-blockbuster The Meg and Meg 2: The Trench (with long-term business and producing partner, Chi-Li Wong):, Gambino, Emmy-nominated The Kennedy Detail, The Lost Valentine, The Amityville Horror: The Evil Escapes, Hysteria (which premiered at the 6th International Rome Film Festival),  Angels in the Snow, Joe Somebody, and Life Or Something Like It. His own books included A Writer’s Time, Writing Treatments That Sell (with Chi-Li Wong), How to Escape Lifetime Security and Pursue Your Impossible Dream, The Messiah Matrix, Cajun Household Wisdom, 50 Irrelevants Who Rocked the World! (with Chi-Li Wong) and Japanese-in-Law (with father-in-law Keisaku Mitsumatsu). He developed and sold hundreds of his clients’ books to traditional publishers, film, and television and published another several hundred through his own imprint, Story Merchant Books.

Born in Eunice, Louisiana (Cajun country), and raised in Kansas City, Missouri, he graduated from Rockhurst High School’s Honor Program with an Ignatian Scholarship to study at Georgetown University. While in high school, he published his first book reviews for The Kansas City Star.

At Georgetown, Atchity majored in Classics and English, rose to Editor-in-Chief of The Hoya. He spent his junior summer at Cambridge University in England, studying literature and social institutions, then won the prestigious Vergilian Academy Silver Medal. His correspondence, literary artifacts, and entertainment memorabilia are archived at  Georgetown’s Atchity Aguillard Collection  . https://t.co/8Z6yTpOWRQ

At the birth of his son Vincent, he accepted a position at AT&T Longlines as a Communication Engineer in charge of the Headquarters Account for NASA. There, he designed and implemented the Green Network connecting NASA’s 26 research centers.

Atchity entered Yale’s Department of Theatre History, achieving his M.Phil. before transferring to Comparative Literature. He studied under A. Bartlett Giamatti and Erich Segal, before winning the University’s highest academic award, The John Addison Porter Prize, for his doctoral dissertation, Homer’s Iliad: The Song and Shield of Memory (published later by Southern Illinois University Press, with a foreward by John Gardner who said of it, “I know of no other book as good”).

With 14 job offers leaving Yale, Atchity accepted a position as Assistant Professor of English and Comparative Literature at Occidental College (teaching graduate courses at California State University/Los Angeles and creative writing at UCLA’s Writing Program). At Occidental, he received tenure and became a tenured full professor and Fulbright Professor of American Literature at the University of Bologna. During his 17 years at Occidental, Atchity founded and edited DreamWorks (advisory board including John Fowles, Ursula LeGuin, John Rechy, William S. Burroughs, Paul Bowles, among others) as well as CQ: Poetry and Art. He was awarded Occidental’s Faculty Achievement Award, UCLA Writers Program’s Distinguished Instructor Award, along with grants from the California Arts Council, the National Endowment for the Humanities, the National Endowment for the Arts, and the Graves Foundation. He pursued Dante studies in Florence, Italy, and Homeric studies in Greece. In all, he studied seven languages and published numerous articles in academic journals and book-length edited collections of essays on Greek, Roman, Medieval, and Renaissance literature.

While he was still a tenured professor at Occidental, the State Department in Washington asked him to receive a Middle Eastern ambassador who wanted to meet an academic interested in poetry and business. At the time, Atchity was the editor of two magazines, CQ: Poetry and Art and DreamWorks as well as a consultant in publishing, translation (biggest client, The Getty Museum), and commercial writing. At their meeting, the Ambassador pointed out to Dr. Atchity that, as a Lebanese American, he was following the tradition of his ancient ancestors, the Phoenicians. “They were not only merchants,” he explained, “but they brought the alphabet from one port to another to facilitate the spread of stories. You, too, are a story merchant.”

Atchity resigned his tenured professorship to produce a movie project he’d found financing for (between Astral-Bellevue-Pathé in Montreal and Warner Brothers). The sixteen Shades of Love romantic comedies were broadcast on HBO-Cinemax and released by WB internationally. As detailed in his book How to Escape Lifetime Security and Pursue Your Impossible Dream, he transitioned to literary manager and producer, thereby pursuing his dream.

More significantly, Ken’s clients often credited him with their accomplishments saying, “He changed my life.” He so believed in others that they learned to believe in themselves, to follow their dreams.

Ken also advised everyone to write their own obituary, “Who knows your story better?” he often said. His was published in two volumes, Daddy Holding Me and My Southern Belle, complete with the stories you’d expect from a professional story merchant and the treasured and delicious family recipes shared by someone of Lebanese and Cajun descent who grew up in Louisiana and Missouri.

Ken was preceded in death by his brother Fred Atchity and sister Andrea McKeown. Survivors are Ken’s wife, Kayoko Mitsumatsu, whom he always referred to as “an angel;” his son, Vincent Atchity, Ph.D.; his daughter, Rosemary Atchity, NP-C; his five grandchildren, Margaret D. McKenna, Esq., Edward J. McKenna, Oliver D. Atchity, Eliot J. Atchity, and Louis M. Atchity; and his sisters, Mary Calhoun and Laurie Dressman...

The family has requested that, in lieu of flowers, donations be made to Yoga Gives Back (https://t.co/gIXngECWTI). Ken served on the board of this organization empowering women and children in India since its founding.

1989 CENTENNIAL ACCORD WITH SOVEREIGN INDIAN TRIBES 

WA State Office of Equity 

Part 2

Oct. 23, 2026

☆ Inside the Multicultural Child and Family Hope Center

While the early learning center is the physical foundation, MCFHC operates 52 wraparound community programs. Moving the childcare operations into the new Cora Whitley Family Center frees up their older, neighboring buildings to expand vital social safety nets. Look at some of the services MCFHC offers:

Childcare – expanding to serve 320 children, including 19 classrooms and 4 dedicated infant care spaces

▪︎ A Recovery Café
▪︎ A Father Engagement Class
▪︎ A Neighborhood Gym
▪︎ A Food Bank
▪︎ A Diaper Bank
▪︎ Eviction Prevention and Rental Assistance
And much more!

TraeAnna Holiday, EQUITY Communications Director, and a friend at the Cora Whitely Family Center ribbon cutting (photo)

▪︎ Read more about CWFC on our Blog

https://t.co/YE6383so0B

Who is Cora Whitely?

To understand the profound weight of the new center, you have to understand the woman whose name is now proudly displayed on the building: Cora Whitley. Cora, who passed away in 2014, was a legendary figure in Tacoma.

"Cora Whitley was our Nana, the community's Nana, and so we're just living on her legacy," shared Turner Cagle, a long-time teacher and Director of Youth Programming at MCFHC. She was a woman who made sure every neighborhood kid had unforgettable holidays, great presents, and a safe environment. When she passed, nearly 800 people packed her funeral inside of three days—a testament to her quiet power.

"My mom was a force to be reckoned with," Cora's daughter, Gail Neal, told the crowd during the ribbon cutting, holding back tears. "Thank you so much for helping me with this dream and being able to carry on my mom's legacy."

▪︎ From the Director's Desk: Byrd Barr Place

What an unforgettable, spirit-filled evening at Byrd Barr Place’s Legacy in Motion Gala!

https://t.co/wYNRDJx6K7

As a Black woman, it is always a profound blessing to be immersed in my community, surrounded by so much joy, beauty, and Black excellence. In times of so much external noise, stress, and pressure, it's deeply restorative to step into a space where you are seen, heard, and valued—where you are among people who understand your walk, your culture, and your heart.

The theme Legacy in Motion immediately made me think of ** Sankofa—the wisdom of looking back to understand what was, so we can move forward intentionally. Our past informs our future. We don’t just inherit legacy; we build it every single day we are on this earth, and we must celebrate the giants doing the work while they are still here with us.

▪︎ Read about Byrd Barr Place

https://t.co/wYNRDJx6K7

Hearing from Dr. Michael Eric Dyson was an absolute masterclass. That brother is powerful. It's immensely comforting to know we have leaders who have our backs, can dismantle harmful narratives in real time, and stand unapologetically in truth. We must keep passing that knowledge down to our children so our history is never erased.

Beyond the incredible food, music, and energy, what touched me most was being in a room surrounded by powerful Black women leaders. Doing equity work is not easy, and Black women navigate challenges from every angle. But looking around at trailblazers like Dr. Angela Griffin, Michelle Merriweather, Seattle City Council President Joy Hollingsworth, Representative Dr. Kristine Reeves, FMS Global Strategies CEO Paula Sardinas, and so many others, I felt protected, grounded, and deeply inspired. You are reminded that you are never walking this journey alone.

Thank you to Byrd Barr Place for holding space for our collective brilliance, our resilience, and our future. 🤎✨

Megan Matthews
Office of Equity Director

text:
Crimson Desert is another game that I played when it first came out. They’ve released a lot since then, so I plan on playing it again in a couple of months, starting over from the beginning and going through everything again.

At this point, going back would mean more than just picking up the same game with a few bugs fixed. There are new ways to fight, more things to do with the camp, more animals and mounts, changes to the other playable characters, and an entire expansion coming up.

This covers the released updates through October 23, 2026. I'm grouping the smaller fixes together rather than copying hundreds of patch-note bullets, but I want to get into what actually changed and when. Some early patches may have overlapped with my original playthrough. I don't have an exact patch number for the day I finished.

March: the launch version and the first changes

Crimson Desert released March 19. The launch-period 1.00.02 update already adjusted boss encounters, added an Abyss Gear tutorial, changed the skill-learning presentation, and added follow-up attacks for the playable characters. It also stopped making you repeat the puzzle section of the Tenebrum encounter after dying during the fight. Bears lost their instant-kill damage, and several quest and character problems were addressed.

The first major post-launch changes came with 1.00.03 in the March 23–25 rollout. Private storage was added at the temporary Hernand lodgings and Howling Hill. More fast-travel points were added, learning through observation was simplified, and Force Palm became available earlier.

Logging took fewer hits, several minigames became less demanding, food restored more health, and blocking used less stamina. The patch also changed some early enemy and main-boss balancing. There were clearer puzzle clues and improvements to the keyboard, mouse, and gamepad controls.

Those are the sorts of changes you notice constantly throughout a game this size. Storage, movement, healing, gathering, and being able to understand what a puzzle wants all affect the hours between the big fights.

March 28: update 1.01.00

This added five summonable mounts: White Bear, Silver Fang, Snowwhite Deer, Rock Tusk Warthog, and Icicle Edge Alpine Ibex. Previously meeting the requirements for the legendary animals could qualify you for the corresponding rewards retroactively.

They added Refinement Tokens for upgrading equipment to stage four without spending the usual materials, a faster cooking and crafting option, bulk movement of selected items into storage, and wholesale grocers at farms.

Movement and flight were adjusted again. Flight used less stamina, turning was more responsive, and fast travel and revival loading were shortened. There were also map and notification improvements, clearer skill information, and more Photo Mode controls.

On the technical side, this was another round of rendering and stability work, including changes to upscaling and a fixed 4K output option on PS5. That setting shouldn't be confused with a promise that the game internally renders everything at native 4K.

April 4: update 1.02.00

Storage grew considerably. Private storage could now expand with the Greymane camp, starting at 240 slots and eventually reaching 1,000 across the camp upgrades.

They added headgear visibility options and a choice between Basic and Classic movement controls. So if you preferred holding the sprint input or preferred the older repeated-input approach, you had a setting for that rather than being stuck with one version.

There were more fast-travel improvements, better jump responsiveness, fixes for certain boss and weapon interactions, and repairs for quest progression problems. Cats also got an additional armor set and helmet.

I like including the little things in a rundown like this, because otherwise a game can receive months of additions and the conversation gets reduced to whether the frame rate changed.

April 11: update 1.03.00

Fast travel became usable while mounted, falling, swimming, or climbing. That's a substantial convenience change when you're moving around a world with this much verticality.

Kliff received Focused Aerial Roll. Damiane and Oongka received more of the abilities needed for exploration, including Axiom Force and Nature's Snare, while their existing skills gained functionality corresponding to Kliff's Force Palm.

The Pailune camp became easier to use, its farm and ranch areas expanded, and additional puzzle guidance was added. Standard dialogue could be fast-forwarded, with a speed setting. Minimum font size and weapon-display options arrived as well.

The changes to Damiane and Oongka are worth following through the later updates, because they kept getting more access to things that had previously been tied to Kliff.

April 23: update 1.04.00

This was a big one for difficulty and storage.

Easy, Normal, and Hard settings were added. Normal preserved the existing difficulty. Easy reduced several combat pressures and widened defensive timing windows. Hard increased the challenge, tightened those windows, changed food use so the animation had to finish, and added patterns for some bosses.

The new storage options included a 1,000-slot gatherables chest, food storage through the Kuku Cooler and its larger upgraded version, a 1,000-slot collectibles chest, and wardrobe storage that could grow to 1,000 slots. Materials and ingredients in the appropriate storage could be used for crafting or cooking without carrying them around.

There were also different house layouts to unlock, inventory categories, input presets, new skills and pets, and distant scenery improvements.

For a fresh playthrough, being able to choose the challenge level and organize the things you collect would change a lot of the routine from the outset.

May 2: update 1.05.00

Boss rematches and re-blockades arrived here.

The rematch system initially covered 69 bosses. You could revisit an encounter through its memory fragment and fight with Kliff, Damiane, or Oongka. Reminisce retained the original boss stats, while Resonate could scale a boss upward to your progress. Used consumables were restored afterward, and the rematches didn't provide separate loot.

Re-blockades let enemy forces return to eligible liberated strongholds. You could turn that off, have it happen intermittently, or have it happen frequently. The initial version involved 13 factions and 23 forts and quarries, with later patches expanding and adjusting the system.

The update also added legendary pets, including the Iron Eagle and Hyacinth Macaw, and the Mountain God Boar creature. Legendary mount summoning and comrade trust problems were fixed.

Having the option to revisit combat after clearing an area matters when you've already beaten the story. Otherwise, eventually you're walking around with all these abilities and fewer places left to use them.

May 11: update 1.06.00

A much wider selection of animals became registerable special mounts. That included animals such as bears, wolves, deer, boars, lions, tigers, camels, raptors, and Kuku Birds, with taming requirements depending on the animal.

Equipment extraction was added at smithies. You could lower an item's refinement and recover some of the resources invested in it without destroying the equipment. Special materials were fully returned, while ordinary materials had a partial return.

Oongka received new unarmed skills. Sword sheaths and a sheath-display setting were added. Pet dogs could participate in combat with the Sigil of Valor, and a claw machine offered additional rewards. Night Tone Mode was another new option.

There is a lot here that gives you a reason to experiment with equipment or explore the animal systems rather than just keep following the next story marker.

May 15: update 1.07.00

More bosses became available for rematches, including Muskan, Corrupted Caliburn, Goyen, Draven, and Clockwork White Horn.

Damiane received unarmed combat skills, and both Damiane and Oongka received Aerial Stab. Kliff gained an unarmed Blinding Flash Finisher. There were additional wolf and bear mount types and more mountable animals in the world.

They also worked on attack chaining, unarmed combat, quest blockers, equipment problems, and mount behavior. An AMD-driver-related GPU crash was addressed.

May 22: update 1.08.00

The camp pond arrived, letting you keep fish and, for suitable species, increase their numbers over time. Legendary fish received special handling so they could remain in the pond rather than being treated like ordinary disposable inventory items.

Baby Wyverns and another 20 small animal species became available as pets. Wild wyverns could be subdued and ridden temporarily. Raising your own into a permanent mount came in the following updates.

Kliff gained access to muskets and shotguns. Tools got their own equipment slot instead of competing with a secondary weapon. Damiane and Oongka received an equivalent to Focused Aerial Roll.

There were additional crafting and refinement conveniences, more keyboard customization, improved fish traps, and expanded re-blockade coverage at bandit camps and ruins. Blackstar also received control and camera improvements.

May 29: update 1.09.00

Controller remapping was added, along with approximately 30 more small-animal pet species. Damiane and Oongka gained further skills, and seed planting became easier through quickslots.

There were fixes to pond management, gathering tools, dispatch information, and combat behavior. The dispatch screen also became more helpful about which comrades had the skills a mission needed.

That continued the pattern of adding features and then making the surrounding menus and interactions less awkward to use.

June 5: update 1.10.00

Baby Wyverns and Kuku Bird Chicks could now be raised into special mounts. There was new equipment for them, including a wyvern saddle.

Re-blockades gained battle and reconstruction stages. Major strongholds could receive protection through regional contribution assessors, and liberation rewards included contribution, provisions, trade goods, and other items.

Pinball and Orb Roll were added as minigames with reward exchanges. Blackstar gained a ground attack. Some choices made during a boss attempt, including selected elements and ammunition, would now persist when retrying.

This is where the post-launch additions really start piling up if you stopped playing in March. You're looking at flying mounts you can raise, more repeatable fighting, and additional little activities around the world.

June 12: update 1.11.00

Pet registration could expand to 100 through challenges, although the camp summon limit remained 50. Damiane and Oongka could equip the mining drill and chainsaw.

Lost rare equipment could be recovered by buying it from shops after it entered their stock, at an increased price. Pinball was adjusted, pets retained their names as they grew, and more controller shortcuts became assignable.

There were also fixes for mount summoning, feeding, and certain combat and equipment interactions.

June 19: update 1.12.00

Housing expanded outside the house. You could decorate the outdoor area, use new workstations and looms, and make use of 58 new home items covering facilities, lighting, decorations, and pet furniture.

Damiane and Oongka could equip Visiones, read memories, and ride Blackstar. Sliding chain attacks were added across weapon types. There were new equipment pieces, a Greymane accessory, additional knowledge entries, and more ways to acquire certain previously missable knowledge.

Boss retries retained more of your setup, including weapons, selected elements, and quickslot choices. Loading was also optimized, and there was a large batch of fixes involving quests, pets, housing, mounts, and camp systems.

July 3: update 1.13.00

Damiane and Oongka could finally enter the Abyss. Between this and the earlier exploration changes, the other characters had become much more usable across the wider game.

Kliff and Oongka received 39 equipment additions, while Damiane received eight. Equipment compatibility expanded too: Oongka could wear most Kliff outfits, and Damiane gained access to specified boss equipment.

More weapons and outfits became dyeable. Bird pets received the Hunter's Sigil for retrieving appropriate prey and gatherables. There were additional crafting recipes, attacks for certain enemies, and options for hiding more of the HUD.

July 16: update 1.14.00

Cross-save was introduced for PlayStation, Xbox, Steam, and Epic Games Store, so supported platforms could continue from a shared save. Mac support was added later, in September.

The patch also fixed particular quests and interactions, adjusted Damiane's Skystep controls, and addressed several mounted movement and audio problems.

July 24: update 1.15.00

This was more of a repair pass. It addressed crops that stopped growing or couldn't be harvested, problems with equipped gear locks on Damiane and Oongka, cross-save loading crashes, and wyvern summoning in midair.

There were additional fixes for camera behavior, HDR interface rendering, mounts, wagons, and movement skills.

August 1: update 1.16.00

Trading received a major expansion: 133 new trading posts, 24 high-value trade goods, four regular trade goods, and seven wagon workshops.

The system became more practical to use. You could transfer goods between horses and wagons, sell individual goods, check more market information from the map, and follow wagon routes on the minimap. Prices could respond when you sold too much at one location, and more difficult routes could offer better returns.

There were changes to profits, stacking, royal trading posts, and banking, including bonds and a bond shop. Quest and challenge fixes accompanied all of that.

For somebody returning after launch, this is a whole part of the game worth checking again instead of assuming it works the way it did the first time.

August 7: update 1.17.00

This addressed challenge tracking, food quickslots, special headgear effects, movement animation and sound, and inaccurate map information for chests and trade routes.

August 15: update 1.18.00

The knowledge system gained a quest category with eight subcategories, including main quests, faction quests, investigations, research, daily life, guides, archive records, and constellations. Some completed-quest knowledge was awarded retroactively.

Research costs switched from silver to camp funds. Some animal knowledge could be obtained by picking animals up rather than killing them. Horse gear could be equipped at stables, and lock-on camera rotation gained manual, semi-auto, and automatic settings.

The map also distinguished areas revealed by bells from places you had explored directly. Further fixes addressed trade goods, workers, quests, lighting, and frame-generation problems.

August 25: update 2.00.00, Crimson Desert Enhanced

This is probably the update I would pay the most attention to before another full playthrough.

Enhanced was a free update for existing owners. It included the previous updates and added new cutscenes and story moments throughout the main questline, with additional dialogue and background material around bosses.

German, French, Spanish, Japanese, and Brazilian Portuguese voice-over support was added, along with Arabic interface text and subtitles.

The skill system gained Abyss Links. Spending Abyss Artifacts to learn skills on one character awarded a corresponding resource to the other playable characters. Skill resets became individual to each character, and existing invested resources were refunded when the new system first applied.

Kliff received eight new skills. After finishing the main quests, a new game could carry over Abyss Links and other in-game currency from an existing save. That wording matters: I wouldn't assume it carries absolutely every item and every bit of progress like some other games' New Game Plus modes.

Flying mounts gained a choice of camera-led or manual controls. The update also adjusted certain encounters and traversal rewards, alongside another batch of fixes.

September: updates 2.01.00 through 2.03.02

September 4's 2.01.00 added a gold-bar investment dispatch mission, increased the camp funds gained from silver donations, improved horse health recovery when retrying relevant quests, and added camera tilt in Photo Mode. It fixed issues involving housing, skills, mounts, quest completion, and the interface.

September 11's 2.02.00 brought cross-save to Mac. It also addressed missing trade-storage items, blocked progression in certain quests, housing availability, and a crash when starting a new game with DLSS Frame Generation enabled.

September 18's 2.03.00 added finer Photo Mode camera movement, improved how larger silver amounts carry into a new game, expanded Water Stride movement, and updated DLSS Ray Reconstruction support. Horse racing, dispatch persistence, quest guidance, and several movement problems were also addressed.

September 21's 2.03.01 fixed remapped lantern aiming, missing Duo opponents in Tommaso, and an NPC-interaction crash.

September 23's 2.03.02 fixed Grimnir failing to appear during The Mysterious Pot, missing map icons, and a power-core detection issue blocking Ether Rest.

That last hotfix is the latest released patch listed as I'm putting this together. And to fill in the smaller updates between those bigger releases:

- 1.00.04, March 23–24: separate PlayStation and Mac Steam fixes for character-switch interactions and crashes.
- 1.01.01, March 30: mount controls, mount death behavior, equipment refinement, horse-following, and Constellation Helm interaction fixes.
- 1.01.02, March 30: Steam-side DLSS and Ray Reconstruction image improvements, including blur and flicker.
- 1.01.03, March 31: bosses getting stuck during fights.
- 1.03.01, April 12: Nature's Snare projectiles and Xbox controls, plus liberation loot failing to reach storage.
- 1.04.01, April 23: missing mount quickslots, housing placement, customization crashes, combat and input problems, and pets eating gathered wood or ore.
- 1.04.02, April 24: incorrect difficulty when starting another save, font-size application, horse-gear dyeing, several interface problems, and PS5 Pro brightness stability.
- 1.05.01, May 3: canceled dispatches and missing resource refunds, plus pet summoning.
- 1.06.01, May 12: blocked progress at Vault of Vengeance.
- 1.10.01, June 6: crashes during fast travel, combat, and wyvern-egg hatching, alongside animal spawning, movement obstruction, and dispatch filter fixes.
- 1.12.01, June 20: disappearing outdoor furniture, climbing onto moving objects, glass lighting, floating terrain, and Skunky disappearing at camp.
- 1.12.02, June 24: AMD RX 5000-series crashes at 1080p, a Photo Mode/HDR crash, and incorrectly restricted ocean fishing areas.
- 1.13.01, July 8: bear-riding crashes, rendering and performance problems, missing challenge rewards, Hoenmark Ruins liberation, and ranch-feed behavior.
- 1.16.01, August 2: camp storage incorrectly displaying as wagon cargo after trading.
- 1.16.02, August 3: stuck loading or black screens, AMD and Mac graphics problems, and unavailable indoor housing features.
- 1.16.03, August 4: shields disappearing after switching to dual weapons and reloading.
- 1.16.04, August 5: equipment quantities becoming incorrect after saving and reloading.
- 1.18.01, August 16: delayed NPC interaction, missing older housing objects, startup crashes, and incorrect map display.
- 1.18.02, August 16: camp comrade counts, silver resetting after A Secret Deal, movement animation, and controls becoming unresponsive after shops.
- 2.00.01 and 2.00.02, August 28: Arabic text, cutscene lip-sync, frame-rate drops, some Mac launch failures, the Karin Quarry crane, and unwanted dismounting when colliding with a traveling merchant.

A lot of those sound small until you encounter one of them yourself. A missing shield, a stalled quest, or a save that won't load can matter much more than a new cosmetic item. That's why I wanted the repair work included alongside the additions.

What I'm waiting for next: Charting the Unknown

The expansion is currently scheduled for October 29, at 6 p.m. Eastern. It was originally due October 15, but Pearl Abyss moved it back two weeks for additional development and polish.

The announced content includes separate new storylines for Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane after the main story, plus an ocean-focused storyline available earlier after Howling Hill.

There's underwater exploration, shipbuilding and sailing, romance that can progress to marriage, a more flexible housing system, three castles you can claim, business management, and Garden of Trials, a sequence of boss battles with rewards.

The ocean portion extends exploration to islands and underwater ruins. The story preview mentions political conflict, a threat in the desert, a journey beyond time, and a secret beneath the sea. Those are announced premises, not things I've played yet.

Some activities have progression requirements. The character stories and Garden of Trials require completing the main questline. Ships, housing, businesses, and castles have their own camp, quest, or liberation requirements. Diving itself doesn't require a special unlock, although breath and equipment affect how long you can stay underwater.

The official listings have it coming to PlayStation, Xbox, Steam, and Epic. The Mac App Store isn't included at launch, and there are regional availability restrictions, so anyone buying it should check their own store rather than assume every version has the same availability.

I haven't seen a confirmed date when Pearl Abyss will be finished adding everything it intends to add. So I'm not treating this expansion as proof that the game will be complete forever after October 29.

But this is exactly why I want another playthrough eventually. I played and beat the launch-era game, and there is already a lot here that I haven't experienced in its current form. I want to give them time to put out the things they're going to put out, let the additions settle in, and then come back for another big run through the whole thing.

I can't wait to play it again. I'm just trying to wait long enough that I can really dig into everything when I do.

Guwahati is set to strengthen its growing hospitality and food-service sector with the inauguration of The Terminal, the city’s first round-the-clock food court. Formally inaugurated by Shri Chetan Kumar Srivastava, General Manager, Northeast Frontier Railway, the facility is located at Panbazar, Station Road, near Guwahati Railway Station. It will open to the public on 1 November 2026, operating 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

Bringing together around 40 food and retail outlets under one roof, The Terminal will offer Assamese and North-Eastern delicacies alongside North Indian, Chinese and Continental cuisines, cafés and desserts. Popular brands such as KFC, Domino’s, Subway, Costa Coffee, Baskin Robbins, Wow! Momo and Belgian Waffles will provide diverse dining choices. With seating for approximately 250 guests, the facility aims to serve residents, tourists, families and railway passengers.

Celebrating North-Eastern Cuisine and Culture

Assamese and North-Eastern cuisine is recognised for its distinctive flavours, indigenous ingredients and traditional cooking methods. Dishes featuring seasonal vegetables, herbs, fermented foods and boiled preparations reflect the region’s rich culinary heritage. By bringing regional specialities into a modern dining environment, The Terminal can provide local food entrepreneurs with opportunities to showcase traditional cuisine and reach wider customer groups.

Promoting Youth Entrepreneurship and Employment

The expansion of food courts, restaurants and cafés offers promising opportunities for educated young people to establish businesses and develop sustainable livelihoods. Food preparation, hospitality, outlet management, logistics, marketing and customer service can generate direct and indirect employment. The Terminal may also encourage local entrepreneurs and investors to explore new ventures in Guwahati’s expanding food and retail sectors.

Guwahati: The Gateway to North-East India

As a major gateway to the North-Eastern region, Guwahati plays an important role in tourism, transport and commerce. Improved connectivity and growing interest in the region’s natural beauty and cultural diversity are creating opportunities across hospitality and allied industries. A modern, accessible dining destination near the railway station can enhance visitor convenience while introducing travellers to Assam’s culinary identity.

A Positive Step Towards Economic Growth

Commercial ventures can stimulate local economic activity by creating jobs, generating income, encouraging investment and contributing to government revenue. Their long-term success, however, depends on hygiene, quality, customer satisfaction and sustainable business management.

It was great sharing the stage with Kate Burke, Joseph Harvey, and Ryan Eisenman to close out the Financial Times Future of Asset Management 2026 this week in Boston. Thanks to the FT Live team for organizing a must-attend event.  

The panel tackled the asset management version of the timeless question, “does size matter?” The universal answer was that distribution scale really does. But what matters most is the ability to solve problems for advisors - to become a trusted, reliable, and accessible partner. But what about investment edge? It’s Schrodinger’s alpha – both table stakes and a secondary concern.

That's how we've built F/m. TBIL, the F/m US Treasury 3 Month Bill ETF, exists because investors wanted on-the-run, precise, simple access to the most liquid part of the yield curve. RBIL, the Ultrashort Treasury Inflation-Protected Security (TIPS) ETF, exists because investors were frustrated with inflation solutions that always seemed to disappoint at the exact moment they were most needed. Neither came from a scale advantage. Both came from being close enough to the advisors to hear about the problems that needed solving, and the ability to see the simplest solution.  
  
Every firm has to work out where they can scale their edge. Our suggestion: start with a problem you can solve better than anyone else, not the solution.
