text:
MY DAD'S GIRLFRIEND OFFERED HERSELF AND LIED

I was home for the weekend when it happened. Dad had gone to pick up something from the store, leaving me alone in the living room with her. She came out of the bedroom in one of his old shirts and nothing else, the hem barely covering her thighs. She sat next to me on the couch, closer than she needed to, and rested her hand on my knee.

You have grown up, she said, her fingers sliding higher. Your father doesn’t have to know.

I moved her hand away and stood up. Don’t. I am not interested.

She laughed like I had said something funny. You are serious? Fine. Suit yourself.

I went to my room and stayed there until Dad got back. She was normal at dinner, smiling, serving food, acting like nothing had happened. I thought that was the end of it.

text:
My father kept a thick runner rug over one spot in our upstairs hallway for thirty years.

If my brother or I kicked it aside, he'd stop whatever he was doing and straighten it.

"Cold drafts rot the floorboards," he'd say, without looking up.

Dad died in August. We're getting the house ready to sell, so last month a contractor named Hector and I pulled up the old hallway flooring.

Under the spot where that rug had been, the pine subfloor wasn't rotted. A brass marine hatch, about twelve inches across, had been set flush between two joists. It was held shut with a combination padlock, and the lock was dark with oil that was still tacky. Dad had moved into the downstairs den in April after his fall and hadn't been up those stairs since.

"Could be a crawlspace access," Hector said. "But those are usually in a closet."

Dad worked at a marina on Lake Erie for most of his life, so salvaged brass hardware was normal in our house. A hatch in the floor was not.

I tried the obvious numbers: my birthday, my brother's, my parents' anniversary, Dad's birthday. Nothing. Hector offered to cut the lock off, and I told him to give me a minute.

I called my brother first. He'd never heard of it. "Dad probably put it in to run wiring," he said.

Under a lock, with a rug on top of it?

My mom has lived in Arizona since the divorce in 2004. I only called her because I'd run out of people to ask. I told her what we'd found, and she was quiet long enough that I checked the call hadn't dropped.

Then she asked, "Did you open it?"

I said not yet.

"Don't cut it," she said. "Try 0314."

It opened on the first try.

The hatch lifted on a short chain. Below it was a boxed-in space between the joists, lined with an old flannel shirt of my dad's. I recognized the plaid.

Inside was a small cedar box with a funeral home tag tied to the handle. On top of it sat a hospital bracelet that read "Baby Girl" and our last name, with a date in March of 1991.

I had never known I had a sister.

Under the bracelet was a knit cap small enough to fit in my palm, and under that a manila envelope of index cards in Dad's handwriting. Each card held one line.

*3/14/92. Told her you were getting big.*

*3/14/97. Brought the boys' report cards.*

*3/14/09. Sold the boat. Thought of you.*

There were thirty-five cards, one for every year, and the last one was dated this past March.

My mom was still on the phone, and she told me what I couldn't have known. After the baby died, she couldn't stand to be near the ashes. Dad promised to bury them at the cemetery in Maumee, and he told her he had...

I don't want to be a sad clown. and I know today is off. but I still wanted to make a prompt of the day so I could feel somewhat normal. it's a simple one. add two refrences or just one, to create a image of a forgiving hug.
Keep your friends close, they mean everything.
Special Thanks To: @Fatherlupis01, @Kaelyneneko, @NovaNekura, and @ReilaCircus 

Forgiven by Jolly Joebean

Prompt Start
---

Designate the attached primary character reference as @Image1.

@Image1 = the primary character identity and visual-design reference.

If a second OC reference is attached, designate it as @Image2.

@Image2 = the second character sharing the embrace. This character receives the same strict identity preservation as @Image1, not a simplified or loosely interpreted supporting role.

If only @Image1 is provided, the second participant is Jesus.

Using the attached character reference image(s), create a single, deeply emotional illustration of two individuals sharing a close, forgiving hug. Both are smiling gently, their eyes closed, with tears running down their cheeks, as though a difficult confession has just been made and answered with complete forgiveness.

This is an image-to-image transformation task — each referenced character must remain unmistakably themselves, translated into a clean, expressive early-2000s 2D television-anime style.

The image should communicate the relief of being fully known, forgiven, and still loved. The confession is already over. The forgiveness has already been offered. What remains is the embrace.

REFERENCE RULES — HIGHEST PRIORITY

Thoroughly analyze each attached OC reference and preserve the character's:

Face and facial structure
Hairstyle and hair color
Eye shape and established eye design
Skin tone or original body material
Body type and proportions
Species traits
Signature accessories
Outfit design and color placement
Recognizable markings, symbols, and motifs
Dominant color palette
Personality and emotional energy
Recognizable silhouette

Each character must remain unmistakably the same individual beneath the change in rendering style, pose, and expression. Do not use characters, costumes, names, or visual information from previous prompts, generations, or conversations.

Preserve each OC's original outfit. Allow natural folds, compression, and small shifts caused by the hug, but do not replace their clothing with generic garments or discard identity-defining accessories.

If a reference is a character sheet, use its views and readable character information to understand one individual. Do not reproduce its extra poses, expression thumbnails, labels, swatches, notes, borders, or background.

The eyes must remain closed. Preserve their established shape through the eyelids and surrounding facial structure rather than opening them to display eye color.

CHARACTER PAIRING LOGIC:

If two OC references are provided, depict those exact two OCs embracing one another. Both must be recognizable, emotionally present, and actively participating. Do not add Jesus as a third figure.

If only one OC reference is provided, depict that exact OC embracing Jesus. Do not invent another OC, duplicate @Image1, or leave the second participant unseen.

A multi-view sheet represents one OC, not several people. Images supplied only as hug examples are pose and emotional references, not additional cast members. Their photographed people, clothes, text, watermarks, and rendering style do not carry into the illustration.

The finished scene contains exactly two participants.

STEP 1 — ESTABLISH THE MOMENT OF FORGIVENESS:

Show the quiet emotional release immediately after a confession has been received with compassion.

The hug should feel like the moment someone realizes that telling the truth has not made them unloved. Their guarded posture has softened. The fear of rejection has given way to relief, and the person holding them has drawn them closer rather than stepping away.

Both participants should convey tenderness, acceptance, and emotional vulnerability. Neither should appear indifferent, reluctant, resentful, or distant.

With two OCs, make the reconciliation feel personal to their expressions and personalities without inventing a specific offense or assigning guilt from their appearance. The viewer does not need to know what happened to understand that forgiveness has been given.

With Jesus, the OC expresses the relief of being forgiven and welcomed. Jesus expresses compassion and loving assurance. His tears are tears of empathy, not an implication that he is confessing wrongdoing or seeking forgiveness himself.

Keep the moment sincere and intimate. Do not introduce a flashback, accusation, punishment, or written explanation.

STEP 2 — CREATE THE DEEP, REASSURING EMBRACE:

Pose the participants in a close, sustained hug with their upper bodies drawn naturally together. Both should return the embrace rather than having one person stand passively with their arms at their sides.

For humanoid characters, wrap the arms securely around the other person's shoulders and back. One hand may rest gently against an upper back or shoulder blade while the other settles around the middle back or softly supports the back of the head.

The hands should feel reassuring: open, gently curved, resting against fabric or hair rather than clutching painfully. Show small folds and compression where the embrace brings their clothing together.

Their heads incline toward one another. A cheek or temple may rest near the other person's hair, temple, or shoulder. Their shoulders relax, and their bodies lean into the contact with the natural weight of people allowing themselves to be held.

Use a slightly offset three-quarter arrangement that keeps both expressions readable. One face may nestle partly against a shoulder, but enough of each face must remain visible to show the closed eyes, smile, and tears.

The embrace must feel close without hiding the emotional evidence that makes the image meaningful. Do not turn either participant fully away from the viewer or bury one person's entire face behind the other's head.

Preserve established height and body-size differences. A taller participant may bend, kneel, or sit to meet the other naturally. Do not stretch necks, shrink bodies, or make either person float to align their faces.

This is a forgiving embrace, not a distant shoulder pat, handshake, wrestling hold, romantic kiss, or posed photograph.

STEP 3 — BOTH SMILING, EYES CLOSED, AND CRYING:

Both participants must display all three expressions at the same time:

A gentle, genuine smile
Fully closed eyes
Clearly visible tears

These requirements apply equally to both OCs, or to the OC and Jesus when only one OC is provided.

Give each participant a smile appropriate to their own face and personality. A reserved character may offer a small, trembling smile; an expressive character may smile more openly through the tears. Both should look relieved, loved, and emotionally moved.

Use softly lifted cheeks, relaxed closed eyelids, tender mouth corners, and brows releasing their tension. Their expressions should communicate warmth beneath the tears rather than despair.

Render tears as clear, delicate tracks emerging from the closed eyes and running naturally down the cheeks. Include small highlights along the wet trails and, where appropriate, a bead of moisture near the jaw.

Keep the tears visible on both faces. Adjust the highlights to remain readable against each character's skin, fur, scales, markings, or other material without recoloring their features.

Do not replace the tears with sparkling particles, hide them entirely in shadow, or assume that closed eyes alone communicate crying.

Avoid exaggerated fountains of tears, comic sobbing symbols, screaming mouths, or gag expressions. The emotion should be profound because it is sincere, not because it is theatrically oversized.

STEP 4 — DEPICT JESUS IF ONLY ONE OC IS PROVIDED:

When there is no @Image2, depict Jesus as the person embracing @Image1.

Give him a compassionate adult appearance, shoulder-length dark brown hair, a short full beard, warm olive-brown skin, a simple cream-colored robe, and a softly draped earth-toned mantle.

Render him in the same illustrated style, linework, cel shading, and level of finish as the OC. He must feel physically present in the same scene, not pasted in from another image or rendered as a glowing silhouette.

His posture should be calm, welcoming, and deeply reassuring. His head inclines toward the OC, his arms return the hug, and his face shows a tender smile with closed eyes and visible tears.

His compassion should be communicated through his expression and touch. A soft warm edge light may support the atmosphere, but do not obscure his features with radiance or replace the intimacy with a dramatic religious spectacle.

Do not depict a crucifixion, crown of thorns, judgment scene, or distant Jesus watching the OC from outside the embrace.

If two OCs are provided, omit this depiction entirely and preserve the two-OC pairing.

STEP 5 — ADAPT THE HUG TO THE CHARACTERS' ANATOMY:

Preserve each OC's established body plan. The embrace should accommodate the characters rather than changing their species to make the pose easier.

A quadruped may lean its head and shoulders into the other participant's chest while being held around its upper body. Existing wings, paws, tentacles, or mechanical manipulators may return the embrace when anatomically appropriate. A small OC may be supported securely against the other person's chest. A large OC may lower its head or upper body to meet the embrace.

Do not add human arms, hands, legs, or facial features to a character who does not have them. Use existing anatomy and established expressive features to communicate the same closeness and relief.

For characters whose canonical design genuinely lacks eyes or a mouth, use their established expressive equivalents without inventing organs. This exception does not remove the closed-eye, smiling, tearful requirements from characters capable of displaying them.

Keep horns, muzzles, hats, ears, wings, tails, and accessories from passing through either participant. Adjust the pose and camera angle naturally around those features.

STEP 6 — VISUAL RENDERING STYLE:

Render the entire scene in a clean early-2000s Japanese television-anime style with expressive character acting and crisp digital cel coloring.

Use:

Confident black or very dark outlines, slightly heavier around the outer silhouette and finer within the face and clothing
Clear, economical shapes with smooth curves and selective sharp angles in hair, brows, and fabric folds
Expressive faces with simplified noses, clearly shaped mouths, readable brows, and clean curved eyelid lines
Bright, saturated local colors that preserve each character's own palette
Crisp cel shading with a base color, one distinct shadow tone, and restrained highlight shapes
Purposeful, hard-edged shadows rather than soft airbrushed facial modeling
Hair organized into clear graphic locks, pointed tufts, or broad shapes instead of individually painted strands
Simple, readable clothing folds with strong color blocking
Small, clean white highlights on the tears
Softly painted environmental backgrounds behind sharply defined foreground characters
The polished digital finish of a hand-drawn television animation frame during a heartfelt dramatic close-up

Translate the characters into this rendering style without replacing their original design or proportions. Human characters remain human; nonhuman characters retain their own anatomy. Do not turn either participant into a generic animal mascot, add unrelated spikes or gloves, or give everyone the same cartoon body.

Apply the same visual treatment to both participants and the setting. Neither character should look more photorealistic, more painterly, or more three-dimensional than the other.

Avoid glossy CGI surfaces, photorealism, heavy painterly character shading, dense hatching, excessive texture, chibi proportions, and hyper-detailed modern anime rendering.

STEP 7 — BACKGROUND AND ENVIRONMENT:

Build a quiet, understated environment that supports the emotional moment without competing with it.

Choose a peaceful location consistent with the OC references where possible. If no setting is established, use a softly painted garden in late-afternoon light, with gentle greenery and warm illumination behind the embrace.

Keep the environment simple and believable. A suggestion of trees, a path, a wall, or softly lit foliage is enough to give the moment a place.

Do not add witnesses, crowds, dramatic events, or elaborate symbolic objects. The emotional storytelling belongs to the two participants and the way they hold each other.

COMPOSITION:

Use a cinematic horizontal 16:9 HD composition, ideally 1920 x 1080 or a higher equivalent.

Frame the embrace as a close medium shot, normally from the waist or mid-torso upward, adapting naturally to unusual anatomy or height differences.

Keep the two participants large, central, and visually connected. Both heads and the principal embracing hands should fit comfortably in the frame.

Choose a three-quarter camera angle near face level so both expressions remain readable while their bodies maintain close contact.

The visual hierarchy should be:

The two faces smiling through tears
The secure, tender embrace
The characters' recognizable designs
The quiet surrounding light and setting

Create one continuous scene and one held moment. Do not use panels, a collage, a montage, a split screen, or a reference-sheet layout.

Do not include any readable text. The title of this prompt is not a title to display in the image.

LIGHTING AND MOOD:

Use warm, gentle directional light with soft reflected fill and a restrained edge highlight along the hair or shoulders.

Keep both faces clearly illuminated. Let the tears catch small, crisp highlights without exaggerating them into glowing streams.

Preserve each character's signature colors beneath the lighting. Do not wash the entire image orange or gold, bury the faces in shadow, or overexpose their features with bloom.

The mood should feel sweet, deep, peaceful, and emotionally honest — the quiet relief of forgiveness after the fear of rejection.

ANATOMY AND CONTACT:

Keep every visible arm connected naturally to its own shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand. Overlapping arms must remain distinguishable.

Human hands have five digits unless the reference establishes another count. Preserve species-specific digits and limb structures.

Hands rest on the surface of clothing, hair, or bodies rather than passing through them. The two torsos remain distinct beneath the embrace, with believable contact and fabric compression.

Keep necks, shoulders, spines, and wrists natural. Do not twist heads impossibly toward the camera to expose the faces. Solve visibility through the pose and camera placement.

QUALITY TARGET:

High-quality 2D television-anime illustration with unmistakable character identity, clean expressive linework, crisp cel shading, accurate anatomy, believable embracing hands, both participants smiling with closed eyes and visible tears, gentle emotional lighting, and a clear feeling of confession answered with compassion.

DO NOT:

Do not change either OC's identity, species, age presentation, markings, proportions, signature accessories, or outfit design.
Do not blend the two characters' faces, colors, clothes, or features.
Do not omit a referenced OC or replace them with an invented character.
Do not add Jesus when two OCs are provided.
Do not omit Jesus when only one OC is provided.
Do not duplicate the OC to fill the second role.
Do not treat people in hug examples as additional cast members.
Do not hide either participant's entire face.
Do not leave capable participants with open eyes, dry cheeks, or an expression lacking a smile.
Do not make the hug distant, reluctant, restraining, or one-sided.
Do not replace forgiveness with a joke, punishment, accusation, or romantic kiss.
Do not invent a specific offense or imply that Jesus is confessing wrongdoing.
Do not add extra people, clones, crowds, flashbacks, or unrelated events.
Do not force nonhuman characters into a human body plan.
Do not add titles, names, dialogue, captions, Bible verses, logos, signatures, watermarks, borders, or interface elements.
Do not create malformed hands, extra limbs, broken joints, stretched necks, fused bodies, intersecting accessories, or impossible contact.
Do not obscure faces with lighting, effects, or foreground objects.
Do not use characters or visual information from previous prompts or conversations.

The finished image should feel like the quiet breath after “I forgive you” — two people holding each other a little closer, smiling through their tears because the truth has been spoken and love has remained.

---

そんな中、天使のような存在が現（あらわ）れますが、その描写（びょうしゃ）が「ヨハネの黙示録（もくしろく）」でのイエス・キリストの描写にそっくりなので、これは、イエスという人として生まれるまえの「子なる神」がダニエルのまえに現れたのではないか、とも考えられています。

その姿（すがた）がダニエルにしか見えなかったのは、霊的（れいてき）存在は見える人と見えない人がいるためですが、見えなかった人たちも逃げ出したほどだというのですから、ただならぬ気配のものがそこに存在することは、だれもが感じ取れたのでしょう。

[Ryusui’s Commentary]

During the era of the Persian Empire, some of the Jews who had been held captive in Babylon returned to Jerusalem and began the reconstruction of the Temple.

However, they faced ongoing difficulties due to interference from surrounding foreign peoples.
Daniel, by then in his late eighties, lived a disciplined life and continued to offer prayers to God.

Amidst this, an angelic figure appeared.
The description of this being bears a striking resemblance to the depiction of Jesus Christ in the Book of Revelation, leading some to suggest that it may have been the "Son of God"—appearing before His incarnation as the man Jesus—who manifested Himself to Daniel.

Although this figure was visible only to Daniel—as the ability to perceive spiritual entities varies from person to person—the presence was so overwhelming that even those who could not see the figure fled in terror; it is clear that everyone present sensed the existence of something truly extraordinary.

🔥 Theyyam, derived from “Daivam” (divine) & “Deva” (God) to the living embodiment of deities. 🇮🇳🙏

Deep in Kerala, an ancient sacred ritual brings gods and spirits to life through towering headdresses, thunderous drums, fierce dances and blazing fire. 🔥

Deep in North Kerala’s Malabar region, an extraordinary ritual transforms performers into embodiments of gods, ancestral spirits and legendary heroes. As drums thunder, flames blaze and towering ceremonial headdresses rise into the night, Theyyam becomes a breathtaking fusion of faith, folklore, music and fire.

But the name itself carries a fascinating linguistic connection: Daivam means “God” or “deity” in Malayalam and is related to the Sanskrit word Deva, meaning a god or divine being. The term Theyyam is associated with this divine concept, reflecting the sacred identity of the tradition.

Here are the fascinating details behind this centuries old heritage. 👇

🔱 WHAT IS THEYYAM?

Also known as Kaliyattam, Theyyam is an ancient ritual art form and living religious tradition practised primarily in North Malabar, especially in Kannur and Kasaragod, with related traditions in parts of Karnataka.

🙏 THE MEANING BEHIND THE NAME

The name Theyyam is associated with Daivam, the Malayalam word for God or deity, which is related to Sanskrit Deva. This connection reflects the central belief behind the ritual: for devotees, the performer does not merely portray a divine figure; the deity is believed to manifest through the performer during the ceremony.

🎭 MORE THAN 400 DISTINCT FORMS

Theyyam encompasses more than 400 recognised forms representing regional deities, legendary heroes, ancestral figures and spirits. Each form has its own mythology, ceremonial costume, facial designs, music and ritual practices.

🔥 THE TRANSFORMATION OF A THEYYAM PERFORMER

Before the performance, artists undergo hours of elaborate face painting, traditionally using prepared pigments. They wear intricate costumes adorned with ornaments and natural materials, along with enormous, towering headdresses known as mudi.

Accompanied by powerful traditional percussion, ritual invocations and intense movements, the performer enters a trance-like state. Certain Theyyam traditions also feature spectacular fire rituals.

🗓️ THEYYAM SEASON — WHEN TO WITNESS IT

The main ritual season generally runs from late October through May, with many prominent performances taking place between December and April. Exact dates vary according to the shrine and local tradition.

📍 WHERE TO EXPERIENCE THEY YAM

• Kannur and Kasaragod: The heartland of Theyyam in North Kerala.

• Village shrines (kavus): Sacred spaces where local communities preserve their ancestral rituals.

• Ancestral family compounds: Traditional settings where certain ceremonies take place.

• Parassinikadavu Muthappan Temple: Known for regular ritual performances throughout the year.

📅 Planning a visit? Explore the official Kerala Tourism website for Theyyam calendars and regional performance details:

https://t.co/aOrvqaeV9q

✨ WHY THEY YAM IS EXTRAORDINARY

Theyyam is far more than a dance. It is a living cultural heritage passed down through generations, where mythology, devotion, artistic mastery and community identity converge. For devotees, it is a sacred encounter with the divine; for visitors, it offers a remarkable glimpse into Kerala’s ancient spiritual traditions.

How’s this for corruption 😡@UN @POTUS 

These involve specific, documented cases from roughly 2022–2026, investigated primarily by Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU), Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (SAPO), and covered by Ukrainian investigative outlets and the New York Times (based on internal audits). They concern procurement markups, non-delivery or defective goods, and diversion of humanitarian items—not wholesale theft of Western weapons stocks. Amounts are typically in the tens to hundreds of millions of hryvnias or low hundreds of millions of dollars for the larger procurement issues; outcomes range from ongoing investigations and bail to convictions in some cases.
Defense procurement irregularities
•  Timeline and scale: Internal audits by Ukraine’s State Audit Service and Defense Ministry auditors covering 2024 (and into 2025) identified roughly $1.2 billion in losses from fraud, waste, and mismanagement in defense procurement that year. About $126 million was linked to rejecting lower bids and overpaying; other issues included contracts with companies that had defaulted on prior deals or whose executives faced open investigations. Seven of the top 10 military contractors received new business despite such red flags. One example involved a company that delivered none of 600 specialized drones, then won a contract for 1,950 more (delivering only a fraction on time). Another involved overpaying by roughly $130 million on Turkish-made artillery rockets by selecting a higher-priced intermediary offer for identical products.
•  Specific munitions case: The state-owned Pavlohrad Chemical Plant supplied ~233,000 unusable mortar rounds (many with defective fuses or propellant) in 2024. Its director, Leonid Shyman, faced prior investigations for embezzlement/fraud and was out on bail when the Defense Procurement Agency awarded further contracts, including one for $280 million. He was later sentenced to five years in prison in a related case involving inflated prices for explosives.
•  Other NABU/SAPO cases: In 2023, officials at the State Special Communications Service and linked companies allegedly inflated drone prices (DJI Mavic and Autel models) by 60–90% in contracts totaling losses of ~254 million hryvnias (~$6–7 million). NABU/SAPO completed the investigation in October 2026; five suspects (officials and company representatives) were notified; over $4 million was frozen abroad and 17 million hryvnias in Ukraine. Other cases have involved embezzlement of funds for tank reactive armor or spare parts for armored vehicles (tens of millions of hryvnias).
•  Outcomes: Mixed. Some executives faced arrest, bail, or conviction (e.g., Shyman’s five-year sentence). Many investigations remain ongoing or result in new contracts being awarded despite issues. The Defense Procurement Agency director resigned in August 2026 amid the audit coverage. NABU/SAPO reported hundreds of investigations, dozens of convictions, and billions of hryvnias in recovered or saved funds across anti-corruption work (including defense-related) in recent periods, but systemic problems persist according to the audits.
Diversion or resale of humanitarian/military aid
•  Tyshchenko, Radkovskyi, Pohadayev and related “volunteer” schemes (primarily 2023–2026): MP Mykola Tyshchenko and associates (including Odesa regional figures) were linked to schemes involving vehicles for the Armed Forces (kickbacks cited around $40,000 for four cars), resale of free generators received as humanitarian aid (e.g., 10 generators resold for ~1.3 million hryvnias to a community), and the sale of over 50 tons of humanitarian aid (clothing, footwear, etc., valued at over 40 million hryvnias) that was diverted to markets such as Odesa’s “7th Kilometer” instead of free distribution. text:
They would be dead if it were me. Maybe even mysteriously. Insurance will cover my Garage, remember though it is a confined space and gases can build up easily. 

No, two or more are considered lethal force, you can match that. Rights are more respected in higher courts in the US. 

This judge is protecting a Criminal Gang or Mob, that covers federal legal definitions of those words. 

This time, they won't come back to the same house. That's for sure, but this judge is ignoring that next time, it will be a more vulnerable neighbor. 

If it were my house. They would be a nice meal to the overpopulated feral hogs and no one would be talking about them... Because no one will come forward and say...

"Oh, they came up missing when they were out burglarizing people's homes." 

That doesn't happen in reality. It's actually called suppression of evidence if they do not automatically investigate the Obvious. 

That obvious thing is probably that group didn't just attempt to rob his garage, they were more than likely going from house to house, night to night. 

Maybe not every house in the neighborhood. But I can assure every person that watches this video those guys are a team that does this over and over again. 

The reason you would eliminate them, is not for you, it's to Stop them from doing it to someone else. Doesn't matter what "race" or of what skin color they are. This is a team of organized criminals. 

White people also do organized crime. That is a fact. I would not want them treated differently, at all. It may not be a larger number and I am not going to argue about it. 

I suppose the people in the video are Black. They are wearing masks and attempting to hide their identity. That could also be White People. But I would make sure neither made it out of the Garage ALIVE. 

When they erected a Self Storage next to our house, people would break into the BACK cutting holes through the Metal exterior. Our neighbor who owned it and the property next to us. Put that building less than 3 feet from our property. Meaning they had to STAND on our property to cut into it, to accomplish it. 

Simple, K every person on our property in the Criminal Conspiracy. We didn't like the self storage, we don't like the neighbor. It was not specifically for that neighbor. 

I was 15 when I first used a shotgun to eliminate one of the conspirators. I don't regret it. Turns out they were WHITE. They didn't get a chance to flee, I snuck up and blew his head off and stood in the position while my uncle and grandfather dealt with the others. In complete darkness. The guy realized I was taking aim and started begging for his life and I cut that short. I had no crisis of my conscious. I wasn't going to let him live. 

And I shouldn't. For my neighbors sake. Not specifically for that neighbor, for the entire neighborhood. FAFO. 

Their gang attempted to attack us in revenge. Putting us under siege more than once. But every single person in that gang died in maybe 3 of such occurrences. 

People still tried robbing the self storage, but what happened changed it, they did not step on our property to do so, ever again. Legally you cannot shoot over a property line. 

If you cannot see where the bullets will travel to, you shouldn't shoot. With a Shotgun you crouch and shoot from that angle. Because we don't want it traveling through our other neighbors house at speed. I do care about that. 

In Texas, though if they are committing a felony on your property while trespassing, you are not liable. You do not have to warn, you do not have to capture, you do not have to fire warning shots and you do not have to SEE a gun. You should assume they do. They did. But he was begging me, while he was digging in his pocket. I only found out, because the crime scene photos showed his hand on a (STOLEN) pistol in his pocket. 

Literally to get the pistol out of his pocket they had to pull his hand off of it. 

I had not seen it. I though, was told to shoot without hesitation. Afterwards that fact was reinforced. 

All 3 of them were carrying stolen pistols and those were stolen from our neighbors just a short distance from our house. We did not have to guess that they had burglarized them. Proving the theory that they were in deed burglarizing most of the neighborhood. 

I will state one more time they were white. 

Our Ethnically Diverse neighborhood. Most of the burglaries happened in the trailer park on the next street over. A predominantly Black and Spanish neighborhood. But not even all of them. 

Which is perfectly fine with me. I played with all of them as a child. They just couldn't come over for a swim, because of their hair and body products. You can't filter that stuff out. It will require maintenance. So unless they are paying for that, the answer is NO. 

The porch in our town is for guests mostly. My grandparents had metal lawn chairs there for that purpose. So did they. Such is normal. The entire yard except fenced in gardens and the private pool. 

We weren't that good of friends. But protecting people in that neighborhood was a consideration. Several times. We had constructed some of their homes. Taking less than we would from people that had the money to charge market rate to them. Sold them our trailers at times. We never hated them for their racial identity. We just did not openly cohort with them. I bet that is because of enforced segregation and RUMOR stoppage. That would have happened before I was born. Rumor persists when people are confused about what happens inside of a house. Not just out of sight from the road. 

Everyone should always shower before and after a swim. After because of the chlorine. Before is to promote hygienic water in your pool. Refilling a swimming pool and cleaning it, even yourself as we did, does not cost less than hundreds in the 80's and 90's. As the primary user of our pool, I was EXPECTED to do most of the cleaning. 

Only family and some invited guests could come into our house. They often did contact us and ask us to help them. I can remember sitting on their porches with our guns, at their request. We sold them fresh produce and my uncles and Grandfather were carpenters. My father was a Green Beret and my Grandfather had been a career merchant marine. 

We always offered our help, free or with the food from our farm below market rate. My grandfather had a general contractors license. We often hired people others would not and not pay them differently. My grandfather was known for that. Would not take jobs where Black people would not be allowed to work. We built dozens of homes for them with HUD funds and a few of them we did not even ask to be paid for our labor, from them or the government. 

They even allowed us to come by if we heard gun shots. We would call them or they would call us first. Simple neighborhood solidarity. Strange how it was mostly us doing so. But we were as comfortable with them as they were with us. A mutual defense pact is an HONORABLE one. Same as the US has with Israel, Europe, Mexico and Canada. In various forms.

Some of the crime in their part of the neighborhood, you could set a watch by. So we could predict when it was going to happen and be ready there to defend THEM.

I would walk alone in that neighborhood on the street. Presenting myself as a target. I only carried an extendable baton in that case. If you know how to use it, you can send them to the surgeons table with a quickness. 

It was not for myself. It was for them. We had no sight line into the neighborhood. Walking it on the public street was the only way. The Sheriffs department did not patrol there at first. But after some violence, we made the Sheriffs department promise to do that instead of us. 

Often when the Sheriffs did come by when we were doing that, the residents would go into their homes and leave us to do the talking. That is not STUPID at all. We are related to most of the Sheriffs and the constable up until recently was my cousin. 

We did it almost every day. School Bus wouldn't stop on our street anyway. Me, my sister, my cousins all had to take the bus from that more dense neighborhood. Adults were messing with the other children. But I was told to push, drag or taunt, them away from the other children. I was not told why. 

I did and a bullet whizzed by my ear. And a hole you could fit a boxing glove through appeared in his shoulder. The other kids scattered and ran. I simply laid down in the ditch as I had been taught. I knew I was safe, mostly. More shots were fired coming from several places after we cleared the area. Most of them came from the houses close to the bus stop. 

The car they had come in, didn't have anyone left alive to drive it off. It never happened again. It was a CLEAR message. It was not even our family that loosed bullets in that direction. I think that round was from the BLACK MARINE that lived across the street. But I did not know that at the time. Met him at the range though. A private one. On land a different black man owned. That we merely leased as part of our farm. 

Most of the land surrounding our farm on two sides were owned by black people. We even bought the farm from black people. There was more of an uncomfortable tentative relationship with them, but we were all committed to the same goals. Even if we didn't talk much. 

I learned later about the history. About the Fredonian rebellion. That happened before the Texian Revolution. We have always had a tentative and uncomfortable defensive relationship in the territory of East Texas. In our unorganized militia, it does not matter if you are European, Spanish or Native or even Black. As far as I know, it never has. The Cherokee are known for sheltering runaway slaves. The Independence of Texas from Mexico was wanted by all those people. Despite the Political Theater and what Wikipedia wants you to think. 

If you go to downtown Nacogdoches. You might miss it because of the way the roads are and the geological features. But the land in a certain spot has one way in by road. It's difficult to walk from Main street to it. But I know where it is, because I helped work on their houses. 

It is owned by Black people. It is in the middle of what is a black neighborhood now. As far as records show, it has been passed down generations in East Texas. It is probably still OWNED by their families, from the original title being passed to them. Hidden, discrete and more than likely passed to them from runaway slaves. 

I do not go there much, but they know exactly who I am and who my grandfather was. It's a great little outlaw hideout. I could go there and sit on their covered porches for hours while people searched for me. No one would go there except my grandfather. Not the police, not the sheriffs department and especially the families of the other teenagers I had fought to make me need to hide. 

He knew where I was and he would not have to be called... At least by me. I wouldn't put it past them, they had phones too. But more than one night, I have laid down on their porch. With their permission. It's one unbroken piece of property, with only a private driveway leading into it. 

You will absolutely miss the dozen or less houses there driving past on the maintained road. 

Because my grandfather got a HUD grant to turn their shacks into up to code housing. Bought the materials. EMPLOYED THEM TO DO THE WORK. Took not a penny in payment. You can look, his name is the General Contractor. He did not pay himself. He did not hire others to do the work. He Hired THEM. It was not a mistake or an oversight. Man had served with a couple of them in the Merchant Marines. 

Otherwise the land legally can be taken as public nuisance having been held as condemned and unfit for human habitation. 

The Caddo tribe historically inhabited the northeastern area of East Texas, particularly in the Piney Woods region, where they cultivated land and built cone-shaped huts. They were organized into three main confederacies: the Hasinai, Kadohadacho, and Natchitoches.

The Caddo maintained complex relationships with enslaved people and maroons along the Red River borderland, where their position as intermediaries between Spanish, French and later American authorities created spaces for negotiation and limited shelter for those fleeing slavery.

I am Caddo as well. Though we were never moved from our homes and land. That's the key element here. My DNA says I am mostly French, German, Caddo and African. In that exact order. People can't see that though. And I DNGAF. It's only important to me to know, not anyone else.

If I don't talk to you, don't take that as I hate you. I don't know you and I don't want my every relation known to everyone. I will allow other people's prejudice to lead them astray. To a different conclusion. Our covenant is older than all of us. It is a habit to not betray that. We are Americans and that is our covenant. Let's maintain the peace, that's all I want to talk about with you, no offense. It's not even a long conversation. That way we don't screw up that tentative peace. All I want to know is that you will work with me to defend our peace. I think I already know the answer to that question. That makes us brothers. We don't need a dance, a barbecue together or to sit on a porch and chat after that. 

It's our town, our country and our peace. We could do with a little of that "old fashioned" cooperation, that I learned as a child. I love it when people recognize me, wave and say hello. But I don't need it. I don't need to virtue signal. I would prefer if people didn't associate us together. That makes it a surprise. I like surprises. A nod here and there wouldn't hurt. That's not that visible through a scope or binoculars unless you are watching both people at the same time.

Special Forces like my father, gave the first Green Beret to a Black man ever. When asked why, he said "You already have a Black Man wearing a Beret." He meant himself. I intentionally gave the first Militia Uniform I ever gave to a Black Man. It was a private exchange. But I knew that he would pass that on through his community. Making our militia stronger. Making it a big surprise when they show up to the fight. Already trained by him and to stand next to the rest of us. There is value in that. A common defense. 

An Unorganized Militia's only true purpose is to defend against an invasion, by securing the neighborhoods and therefore the people in them. Because the Regular Military enlisted will be fighting away from populated areas, in all hope. To relieve pressure from the police and medical services in that time of great need. I don't agree with any other use of a militia. It is not political, it's purpose is to protect and take on certain roles like medic and entrenched guerilla fighter. We do not take orders, we evaluate, prepare, train and teach. Only a defensive role. 

I didn't wear my uniform or go to DC on Jan 6th. I thought it was stupid. I can understand why they did it. I do not have to agree with it. I do agree with their view on the situation, I do not agree with their actions or the actions of congress either. It's difficult to pick a side when everyone is wrong.

I wear my uniform openly, so that when people ask me I can tell them about it. I think a great number of people misunderstand it and have vague conceptions of it. I can clear that right up, I don't even need an ointment.

If it makes some people feel uncomfortable, there's probably a reason they do. That's okay. They need to hear the Truth. When I have on my protective gear, they do not have to like it. I don't need to do anything. The Kevlar makes most people, even criminals, not a threat. I have better than that, but largely unnecessary. I wear a camera and it makes good content, even if some of it I have to host in other countries because of the content.

Eliminating the gangs made everyone in the neighborhood safer. So all our neighbors could walk day or night in our neighborhood. 

Anything less than that is a comfortable LIE.

text:
In 1996 an envelope arrived at the home of an old man in New York. Inside was a Pepsi-Cola advertisement, forty-odd years out of date, showing a woman holding a six-pack while a small boy reached up toward one of the bottles.

The woman in the picture was a Harlem model named Sylvia Fitt, hired for the shoot. The boy was Ronald H. Brown, who grew up to become Secretary of Commerce of the United States and who had been killed that April in a plane crash on a trade mission to Croatia.

Brown had kept that advertisement on display in his office. After he died, his mother mailed it back to the man who had made it.

His name was Edward Francis Boyd, he was eighty-two years old, and almost nobody in America knew what he had done. The story starts half a century earlier, with a company that was losing.

In 1947 Pepsi-Cola was the cheap cola. Coca-Cola owned the country, and Pepsi was the twelve-ounce bottle for a nickel, the drink you bought when you were counting.

Walter Mack ran the company and had done arithmetic his competitors would not do. There were roughly fourteen million Black Americans and they bought soda like everybody else.

Almost no major corporation in the country was addressing them as customers. The ones that pictured Black people at all pictured them as Aunt Jemima.

He had tried this once already. In 1940 he hired an advertising man named Herman T. Smith, ran an essay contest to recruit Black college graduates, and brought Allen L. McKellar and Jeanette Maund to New York as interns before the war shut the whole effort down.

In 1947 he tried again. He called in a thirty-two-year-old housing specialist from the National Urban League and offered him a job he had not come asking for.

Boyd had been a singer and an actor in Hollywood in the late thirties, and he knew what rooms in this country were closed. On the night Hattie McDaniel became the first Black performer to win an Academy Award, Boyd was her escort.

He took the title of assistant sales manager and built a team of twelve. On paper they were absurdly overqualified to be selling soda.

Charles E. Wilson came out of Hampton Institute wanting to be a doctor. Jean F. Emmons held one of the very few business master's degrees in Black America, William Simms had been told by W. E. B. Du Bois himself to go get educated, and Alexander L. Jackson had a Harvard degree.

Boyd's idea for the advertising was so plain it should not have been revolutionary. Show Black Americans as ordinary middle-class people, in their own homes, buying things, living well.

One series was called Leaders in Their Fields and put men like Ralph Bunche in front of the country before Bunche had his Nobel Prize. A run of six magazine ads in 1949 profiled outstanding students at Black colleges, and those pages ended up pinned to classroom walls in Black high schools and colleges around the country.

Another series was drawn by Jay Jackson, a Black cartoonist known for putting satire about race into the Chicago Defender. The Ron Brown ad came out of the same work, a mother and a son and a six-pack, nothing remarkable in it, which was the entire point.

Then there was the selling, and the selling is the part that gets left out.

These twelve men worked the country on the ground, and much of that ground was the segregated South. They called on bottlers, churches, civic clubs, business associations and professional meetings, and they often did it seven days a week.

They rode in the back of buses. They ate behind curtains on trains, and when the curtain was more than a man could take, they carried their meals into the Pullman car.

They drank from the fountains marked for them. Hotels turned them away, so they slept in the spare rooms of Black families in whatever town they were working that week.

Alexander Jackson was ordered to the back of a bus during a campaign in the South. He had a degree from Harvard University and a Pepsi-Cola sales case in his hand, and he got up and moved.

The Ku Klux Klan sent threats. The insults that landed hardest came from inside the company, from white Pepsi employees who did not care for the sight of them.

In 1949 Mack stood up at the Waldorf-Astoria in front of five hundred Pepsi bottlers who were nervous that the campaign was turning Pepsi into a Black drink and would cost them their white customers. To settle the room, the president of the company used the ugliest word in the American language to describe what he did not want Pepsi to become.

Boyd was in that room.

He got up and walked out of the auditorium. Mack apologized to him afterward, and Boyd went back to work building the thing his own president had just disowned in front of five hundred men.

He talked about it decades later, in his eighties, to a reporter from The Wall Street Journal. He said he had not forgotten it and had not held it against the man either, which is a sentence worth sitting with for a while.

What those twelve men built out of all that worked. Pepsi sales climbed through Black communities across the country, and in Chicago the company passed Coca-Cola for the first time, in a market where that had been considered impossible.

Coca-Cola's chairman, in those same years, publicly backed Herman Talmadge in Georgia, a governor who ran on segregation. Word of that traveled through Black America the way word travels, and Pepsi picked up a reputation as the cola that treated you like a person.

The salesmen themselves became known. Jet and Ebony wrote them up, and families cut the pictures out, because a photograph of a Black man with a briefcase and a corporate title was not a thing you saw.

There is a detail in all of this that will stay with you. Harvey Russell, who joined the team in 1950, said that in a striving Black household you served Pepsi in the kitchen and brought out Coke when guests came into the living room.

They were selling a drink some of their own people were quietly ashamed to be seen holding. They kept selling it, and they turned the shame around into something like loyalty.

Around 1950 Walter Mack lost a corporate fight and left the company. The special markets team did not survive him by long.

The new leadership dismantled the division. Some of the men were folded into regional sales, and Edward Boyd, who had built the entire thing from nothing, was let go.

He was thirty-seven years old and he had just proved something no other corporation in America had proved.

One of the twelve, a man who had spent years succeeding at Pepsi and who held a master's degree in business from the University of Chicago, later took a job mopping floors to feed his family. That is what sat on the other side of the door for a Black executive in 1951.

There was no next corporation and no second offer. A man who had helped build a national market for one of the largest brands in the country picked up a mop, and the record of his working life after Pepsi is a job cleaning somebody else's building.

Harvey Russell was the one who stayed.

He had tried the other road first. Before Pepsi he worked briefly for the Brown Belle Bottling Company, a Black-owned soft drink outfit run by A. G. Gaston that put out Joe Louis Punch with Joe Louis himself invested in it, and the company failed.

He joined Pepsi as a field representative in 1950 and stayed thirty-three years. In July 1962 the company made him a vice president, and he became the first Black officer of a major American multinational corporation.

More than a hundred newspapers carried it and cabinet members wrote letters of commendation. Ebony called him "the top Negro in American big business."

The Klan called for a boycott of Pepsi over the promotion of one man. It failed.

Forty-three years after Boyd took the job, in July 1990, Pepsi-Cola sold controlling interest in its Washington bottling operation to Earl G. Graves Sr. and Earvin Johnson for sixty million dollars. Graves took better than sixty-five percent of it and the title of chief executive.

The trucks running out of that six-acre yard in Forestville, Maryland delivered to the White House, the United States Capitol and Air Force One. It was announced at the National Press Club and covered as the largest minority-controlled Pepsi franchise in the country, which it was.

Edward Boyd was seventy-six that summer and living in New York. Go through the coverage of that announcement, the wire copy and the trade press and the business pages, and the twelve men who made Black America a Pepsi market are not in any of it.

The market Graves bought into was not lying there waiting for somebody with sixty million dollars. The building of it started on foot, in the Jim Crow South, seven days a week, with men sleeping in strangers' spare rooms because the hotels were shut to them.

Boyd lived to ninety-two and died in 2007. He went a few months after a Wall Street Journal reporter named Stephanie Capparell finally put the whole story between covers, which is the closest thing to a reckoning he got.

Go back to 1949 and leave him there.

That year Boyd went to see a play in New York, Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman, about a man who gave a company everything he had and was thrown out at the end of it. He was thirty-five, at the height of the thing he was building, two years from being let go himself.

He sat in the dark and he wept.

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter.
If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/Vm6JEQzdIW
Every coffee helps me keep creating.

text:
211,000 people liked a post asking for an app where you upload your bills and bored billionaires swipe right to pay them. John Oliver ran the real version in 2016, and it cost him under $60,000 to erase $14.9 million of medical debt.

The post went up on Thursday and passed 7,300 bookmarks. By Friday morning @denis_kasala had a working prototype called Swipe a Bill.

The business model behind the idea already exists, and it works best when the bills are bought in bulk.

In June 2016 the team at @LastWeekTonight spent about $50 to register a debt-buying company in Mississippi. They named it Central Asset Recovery Professionals, CARP for short, after the bottom-feeding fish.

CARP was soon offered a portfolio of Texas medical debt with a face value of $14,922,261.76. The asking price was less than half a cent on the dollar. The file came with the names and Social Security numbers of nearly 9,000 people.

@iamjohnoliver handed the whole portfolio to a charity called RIP Medical Debt, which wiped it out and structured the relief so it stayed tax-free for everyone on the list. He called it the largest one-time giveaway in television history.

RIP Medical Debt had been started in 2014 by Craig Antico and Jerry Ashton, two former debt collection executives who knew exactly what these portfolios trade for. Their pitch fit in one line: $1 donated relieves about $100 of medical debt.

The group crossed $1 billion abolished in December 2019. MacKenzie Scott has given it $130 million since 2020, per AP. It renamed itself Undue Medical Debt in April 2024, and its site now lists $53.3 billion relieved for more than 32.8 million people.

The retail version of the swipe app is @gofundme. It launched in 2010, dropped its 5% platform fee on US personal campaigns in November 2017 and moved to optional tips from donors. By February 2024 campaigns on the platform had raised $30 billion. Medical bills took more than a third of the money raised in 2017, by the company's own count.

The billionaire version already happened on a stage. In May 2019 Robert F. Smith, founder of @Vista_Equity, told the 396 graduates of @Morehouse he would pay off their student loans. The final gift came to $34 million that September and covered their parents' loans too.

Put those side by side and the math is clear. A billionaire swiping right on one bill pays full price. The same billionaire buying the portfolio from a collector pays half a cent.

Swipe right is the expensive way to do it.

The dog needed multiple stitches and was in critical condition. Animal-welfare groups called it sexual abuse/torture and offered a €1,500 reward for information on the perpetrator. A man later appeared at the police station claiming to be the owner (“Rex”) and said the dog had escaped that morning; the microchip could not be scanned. The attacker has not been publicly identified in the reports. This is the case that generated a lot of Greek headlines last fall. 
There are older isolated cases as well (a 2016 report in Zografou, Athens, etc.).
These are criminal acts under Greek animal-protection law (Law 4830/2021). Bestiality and sexual abuse of animals carry prison time and fines. I won’t go into graphic details.

Arachova, late 2023 – “Oliver” the husky An 8-year-old husky was found badly injured and later died. The first vet described anal trauma consistent with sexual abuse with an object; public veterinarians later said the injuries could also fit an attack by other dogs. The case went to the Supreme Court prosecutor’s office and is still the most famous animal-torture story in Greece. No one was convicted. 
Karditsa, January 2026 A roughly 3-month-old female puppy was found tied to a tree. University of Thessaly forensic vets concluded severe sexual abuse with a large object. Media compared it directly to the Oliver case. A hunter living nearby was mentioned as a person of interest; DNA results were still pending in later reports. 

Rhodes, 2021 A 57-year-old man was convicted of trying to force his wife to have sex with his Rottweiler after she admitted an affair. He beat her when she refused. Court gave him 4 years 6 months for attempted rape, threats, and bodily harm. 

Zografou, Athens, 2016 A man was accused of repeatedly abusing his own dog. A sex worker he had hired reported it to police.

Florida influencer Logan Guminski (arrested early 2025) – posted videos of sex with her Chihuahua; Greek sites (ANT1, Parapolitika) picked it up.

text:
What happens when a company sells radioactive water and guarantees it is harmless? You get one of the most dangerous health fads of the 1920s.

Welcome along, fellow time travelers. Radithor was a bottled radium solution sold by William J.A. Bailey of East Orange, New Jersey. It was promoted as an energy tonic for a long list of ailments. One museum says Bailey even offered $1,000 to anyone who could prove it held less radium than stated.

His best-known customer was Eben Byers, a Pittsburgh steel executive and former amateur golf champion. After hurting his arm in 1927, Byers began drinking Radithor on a doctor's recommendation, and he praised it to friends. He reportedly drank well over a thousand bottles.

Byers died on March 31, 1932, of radium poisoning. The Federal Trade Commission had already ordered Bailey to stop selling Radithor in December 1931.

His death made national news and helped push the government toward tighter rules on radioactive products.

It is a reminder that "new science" and "safe" are two different things.

text:
There are car shows, there are collector car auctions, and then there is RM Sotheby's at Hershey!

As part of my 2026 adventure at the AACA Eastern Fall Meet in Hershey, Pennsylvania, I had the incredible opportunity to spend time inside the RM Sotheby's auction at the Hershey Lodge. If you love automotive history, rare automobiles, beautiful craftsmanship, and the excitement of watching extraordinary vehicles cross the auction block, this is an experience unlike any other.

My goal at Hershey this year has been simple: The Cars of Hershey. I want to bring you up close to the machines, the history, and the people who make this gathering one of the greatest celebrations of the automobile.

And the RM Sotheby's auction certainly delivered!

A Collector Car Auction Unlike Any Other

Celebrating its 20th year at Hershey, RM Sotheby's returned October 7 and 8, 2026, as the official auction of the AACA National Fall Meet.

Held inside the Hershey Lodge, this prestigious auction brings together some of the finest examples of early automotive engineering and design. Unlike auctions dominated by modern supercars and muscle cars, Hershey has a particular emphasis on Brass Era automobiles, pre-war classics, historic luxury cars, and vehicles with remarkable stories.

Walking among these automobiles was like stepping into a museum where nearly everything had the potential to find a new owner.

From massive luxury touring cars and handcrafted coachbuilt masterpieces to early electric vehicles and rare sports cars, there was something fascinating around every corner.

The Cars: Extraordinary Machines Crossing the Auction Block

1934 Duesenberg Model J Convertible Berline by Murphy

Estimated Value: $900,000 to $1,200,000

One of the undeniable stars of the auction was the magnificent 1934 Duesenberg Model J Convertible Berline, featuring coachwork by the Walter M. Murphy Company of Pasadena, California.

Duesenberg represented the absolute pinnacle of American automotive luxury and engineering during the Classic Era. These were automobiles built for an exclusive clientele who demanded performance, prestige, and craftsmanship.

This particular example, chassis number 2434, is especially significant because approximately five examples of this close-coupled Murphy Convertible Berline design are believed to survive.

Its elegant proportions, dramatically angled windshield, distinctive beltline, and beautifully sculpted bodywork make it a rolling work of art.

With an estimated value approaching $1.2 million, this was certainly one of the automobiles I was most excited to see.

1935 Auburn 851 Supercharged Speedster

Estimated Value: $850,000 to $950,000

If there is one automobile that perfectly captures the drama and elegance of 1930s American automotive design, it might be the Auburn Speedster.

The 1935 Auburn 851 Supercharged Speedster is famous for its sweeping bodywork, distinctive boattail rear end, and supercharged eight-cylinder engine.

But the example offered at Hershey was even more special. RM Sotheby's identified it as the very first 1935 Auburn 851 Supercharged Speedster produced.

Imagine being able to see such an important piece of American automotive history in person!

These cars are instantly recognizable, and their combination of Art Deco styling and advanced engineering continues to attract collectors nearly a century later.

1915 Mercedes 28/60 HP Town Car and Tourer Display Chassis

Estimated Value: $450,000 to $650,000

Another fascinating automobile was the 1915 Mercedes 28/60 HP Town Car and Tourer Display Chassis.

This extraordinary early Mercedes represents an era when automobiles were transitioning from experimental machines into sophisticated transportation for the wealthy.

Its history is particularly interesting because it is believed to have been owned by Carl Laemmle, one of the founders of Universal Pictures.

For me, automobiles like this demonstrate just how closely automotive history is connected to the broader history of American culture, entertainment, and industry.

1913 Fiat Type 55 Speedster

Estimated Value: $250,000 to $300,000

One of the more surprising vehicles in the auction was the 1913 Fiat Type 55 Speedster.

While many people associate Fiat with small Italian automobiles, the company once built enormous, powerful luxury vehicles in the United States.

This particular Fiat represents that fascinating chapter in automotive history. Featuring a massive four-cylinder engine displacing nearly 9.4 liters, the Type 55 was an impressive performance machine for its time.

It is a reminder that the automotive industry looked very different more than a century ago!

1909 Detroit Electric Model D, Type K Brougham

Estimated Value: $120,000 to $160,000

Electric cars are nothing new!

Long before Tesla and today's modern electric vehicles, manufacturers were experimenting with battery-powered transportation.

The 1909 Detroit Electric Model D, Type K Brougham offered at Hershey is believed to be the earliest surviving example of its model family and one of only two surviving Detroit Electrics equipped with an early dual-chain-drive configuration.

Seeing an automobile like this really puts the evolution of electric vehicles into perspective.

More than 115 years ago, engineers were already exploring alternatives to gasoline-powered transportation.

1965 Sunbeam Tiger Mk I

Estimated Value: $80,000 to $100,000

For enthusiasts who appreciate a little more horsepower, the 1965 Sunbeam Tiger Mk I was another exciting offering.

Developed with involvement from legendary American performance engineer Carroll Shelby, the Sunbeam Tiger combined British sports car styling with the power of a Ford V8.

The result was a compact, lightweight roadster with a tremendous personality.

It's exactly the type of automobile that demonstrates how creative engineering and unexpected partnerships can produce something special.

A Special Moment: Meeting Wayne Carini at Hershey!

As if being surrounded by these incredible automobiles wasn't enough, another highlight of my evening was getting to spend a little time with Wayne Carini, the legendary collector car expert and star of the popular television series Chasing Classic Cars!

Jason and Wayne Carini at RM Sothebys in Hershey

For those unfamiliar with Wayne, he's one of the most recognizable personalities in the collector car world. As the owner of F40 Motorsports in Connecticut, Wayne has spent decades discovering, restoring, buying, and selling some of the world's most extraordinary automobiles. His passion for cars began at a young age, working alongside his father, and eventually led to a career that has made him a household name among classic car enthusiasts.

Through Chasing Classic Cars, Wayne has taken millions of viewers behind the scenes of rare automotive discoveries, prestigious auctions, and remarkable restorations.

And there he was, right in the middle of the RM Sotheby's Hershey auction, doing exactly what he's famous for!

I had the opportunity to watch Wayne actively participating in the auction, holding up his bidder paddle, bidding on cars, and following the action as these extraordinary machines crossed the block. It was fantastic seeing him in his element, doing what he loves!

I also had the chance to say hello, spend a little time with him, and grab a photograph together. What a great experience!

For someone who has spent years enjoying classic cars and sharing automotive adventures through jamzDOTnet, moments like these make events such as Hershey even more memorable.

You never know who you're going to meet or what incredible automotive history you're going to experience!

More Than Just Expensive Cars

What makes the RM Sotheby's Hershey auction so interesting is the diversity of the vehicles.

There were cars representing the earliest days of motoring, magnificent coachbuilt luxury automobiles, distinctive American classics, and even unusual historic machines that rarely appear at public events.

Each automobile has a story. Some were engineering breakthroughs. Others belonged to notable individuals. Many survived decades of changing ownership, restoration, and preservation.

And unlike simply looking at photographs in a catalog, seeing these machines in person gives you an appreciation for their scale, design, materials, and craftsmanship.

That is what makes Hershey so special.

From seeing million-dollar Duesenbergs and beautiful Auburn Speedsters to watching Wayne Carini in action, my evening at RM Sotheby's was an unforgettable part of the 2026 AACA Eastern Fall Meet.

And the best part? There's plenty more to come!

I'm bringing you even more photographs, videos, and up-close looks at the incredible automobiles of Hershey. My mission this year is all about The Cars of Hershey, and I can't wait to share them with you.

Be sure to follow jamzDOTnet: Cars, DIY, and Adventures on YouTube

Stay tuned. You won't want to miss what's coming next! https://t.co/ftbosIL1Vo
